articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival.

Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.

articles.title: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance.

The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

articles.title: Fatal disagreement: on the COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.

The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy.

The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

articles.title: Action sought against author during Hubballi protest over remarks on Basavanna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Members of people’s organisations stage protest condemning derogatory remarks about the 12th century social reformer and the Constitution

Members of various people’s organisations staged a protest in Hubballi on Thursday, condemning the derogatory remarks about 12th century social reformer Basavanna and statement concerning the Constitution.

The protest, organised by the Hubballi Janapara Sanghatanegala Okkoota, began with the garlanding of B.R. Ambedkar’s statue on the occasion of Constitution Day, followed by a display and reading of the Preamble to the Constitution.

The protesters later took out a procession from Ambedkar Circle to the Tahsildar’s office where they burnt author Ravi Hanj (Hanjmath), journalist and Vishwavani editor Vishweshwar Bhat and seer of Kanheri Mutt Adrushya Kadasiddeshwar Swami in effigy.

The protesters demanded legal action against Mr. Hanj for his remarks about Basavanna, Mr. Bhat for encouraging the publication of controversial material and Kanheri seer for reportedly saying that the Constitution contains ideas from the Manusmriti.

articles.title: No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu government is taking appropriate legal action, says VCK leader

Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) founder Thol. Thirumavalavan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said there was no need for a CBI probe into the allegations that the Kallakurichi TVK MLA had sent inappropriate messages to a District Collector. He said the Tamil Nadu government was taking appropriate legal action.
He said the VCK had consistently maintained that strict action should be taken against the MLA if he had sent messages to the Collector in a manner that caused mental distress.

“We have now received confirmation that a District Collector has formally lodged a complaint. Following this, the government has acted swiftly, registered a case against the particular MLA and initiated an investigation . We do not see any need for the CBI to intervene at this stage,” he said.

Responding to questions about the alleged delay in taking action, with 116 days having elapsed since the incident, Mr. Thirumavalavan said it was important to distinguish between the date of the alleged incident and the date on which the formal complaint was lodged.

“The incident came to light through the media and social media. The information available to us is that the Collector lodged a formal complaint only recently . We also learnt through social media reports that, when the incident occurred, she had not submitted a written complaint but had sought that the MLA be called and warned,” he contended.

He was responding to allegations that the Collector had earlier brought the matter to the attention of the Chief Secretary, who had allegedly attempted to persuade her to seek a transfer to another district. Opposition parties have cited the alleged delay and the handling of the complaint as reasons for seeking a CBI probe.

“Now that she has come forward and lodged a complaint, I believe the government is acting swiftly. A case has been registered under the appropriate sections, and I am confident that legal action will follow,” Mr. Thirumavalavan said.
Tamil Nadu / Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam

articles.title: Railways put in place extensive arrangements for Sabarimala pilgrimage; 204 train services notified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Southern Railway has put in place extensive arrangements to ensure safe, comfortable and hassle-free travel for pilgrims during the Mandala–Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026–27. Since the season commenced on November 16, 2026, a series of measures has been implemented across railway stations, especially the major stations that serve as transit points for devotees travelling to Sabarimala.

Southern Railway has put in place extensive arrangements to meet the increased passenger demand during the Mandala–Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026–27 in coordination with other railway zones, by introducing a record number of special train services, to facilitate the travel of Sabarimala-bound pilgrims from different parts of the country.

As on November 23, a total of 204 trips of Sabarimala special trains have been notified, covering inter-zonal and intra-zonal services with the majority of services operating between Chennai – Kollam, Thiruvananthapuram–Mangaluru, Panvel–Kottayam, Visakhapatnam–Kollam, Hyderabad–Kollam and Vijayawada–Kottayam. Further services will be planned based on passenger demand and reservation trends, said the railways in a statement here on Wednesday.

Kottayam, Chengannur, Ernakulam Junction and Ernakulam Town are the key transit stations for Sabarimala pilgrims, where special arrangements have been made for accommodation, rest, catering, sanitation and onward transportation. A three-storeyed pilgrim facilitation centre near the main entrance of Kottayam station is fully operational and can accommodate up to 900 pilgrims at a time.

In Chengannur, three spacious pilgrim shelters can accommodate up to 600 passengers. Since Ernakulam Junction is an important transit point for pilgrims from different parts of the country, AC waiting halls, catering facilities and cloakroom services are available although station redevelopment works are underway. Temporary prefabricated pay-and-use toilets have also been provided at the station for the benefit of Sabarimala pilgrims.

Pilgrim assistance booths, manned by Railway Protection Force (RPF) personnel, function round the clock at Chengannur and Kottayam to guide and assist devotees. Additional unreserved ticket counters and reservation facilities have been opened at Chengannur and Kottayam, also functioning round the clock, to handle the heavy demand for tickets.

Southern Railway is working closely with the State Revenue department, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), Travancore Devaswom Board, Police and Medical departments for the smooth movement and welfare of pilgrims. Security has also been strengthened at important stations and on trains to ensure the safety of pilgrims throughout their journey.

Railway officials from various departments are closely monitoring special train operations, passenger amenities, station management and crowd movement throughout the season. A dedicated task force will be deployed on Makaravilakku Day at Chengannur, Ernakulam Junction and Kottayam stations to coordinate passenger movement, monitor special train operations and ensure the smooth functioning of the additional booking counters and other facilities.

articles.title: Indira Gandhi gave ST status to Lambada community members: Revanth Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy said former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi recognised the backwardness of Lambada community and included it in the Scheduled Tribes category in 1976, thus enabling the community to secure opportunities in education, government employment and public life, including positions as IAS and IPS officers.

Addressing a public meeting at Maddimadugu in Nagarkurnool district after laying the foundation stone for a ₹38-crore statue of Sant Sevalal Maharaj, he said Lambada community members would never forget Indira Gandhi for her decision.

The Telangana government, he said was equally committed to their development and that a separate Commission for Scheduled Tribes (STs) would be constituted soon. He also promised to secure the political representation due to the community by taking up the issue with the party high command.
Mr. Reddy said the government would develop a temple for Sant Sevalal Maharaj on 20 acres by acquiring an additional four acres, and make it one of the prominent spiritual centres in the country.

Earlier, he laid foundation stones for three projects involving a total investment of ₹71 crore - which include a Haritha hotel near Sri Pebbathi Anjaneya Swamy temple at a cost of ₹15 crore, temple development works worth ₹18 crore, and Sant Sevalal Maharaj statue project costing ₹38 crore.
Ministers Damodar Rajanarsimha, Adluri Laxman Kumar, Jupally Krishna Rao and Vakiti Srihari, MPs Mallu Ravi and Balaram Naik, and other public representatives and officials attended the meeting.

articles.title: Expired food, mouldy sugarcane seized during surprise inspections in Kozhikode
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inspections found several violations of food safety and sanitation norms, including the storage of perishable ingredients in unhygienic freezers and poorly maintained kitchens

The health squad of the Kozhikode Corporation seized expired food products and mould-infested sugarcane during surprise inspections at hotels and eateries across the city on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

The inspections, which began at 6 a.m., found several violations of food safety and sanitation norms, including storage of perishable ingredients in unhygienic freezers and poorly maintained kitchens. Some establishments were also found discharging untreated wastewater into public drains without proper waste management facilities.

Expired chicken, beef, spices, and other stale food items kept for sale were seized from two hotels near Mananchira and Kozhikode South beach. The squad also confiscated mouldy sugarcane stalks stored for preparing juice from an outlet at South beach.

Inspections found several violations of food safety and sanitation norms, including the storage of perishable ingredients in unhygienic freezers and poorly maintained kitchens

The health squad of the Kozhikode Corporation seized expired food products and mould-infested sugarcane during surprise inspections at hotels and eateries across the city on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

The inspections, which began at 6 a.m., found several violations of food safety and sanitation norms, including storage of perishable ingredients in unhygienic freezers and poorly maintained kitchens. Some establishments were also found discharging untreated wastewater into public drains without proper waste management facilities.

Expired chicken, beef, spices, and other stale food items kept for sale were seized from two hotels near Mananchira and Kozhikode South beach. The squad also confiscated mouldy sugarcane stalks stored for preparing juice from an outlet at South beach.

Officials who were part of the searches said show-cause notices were issued to two hotels that were found with unhygienic kitchens and discharging wastewater into the public drainage system. articles.title: Tiruvannamalai railway station nets over ₹60 lakh revenue during Karthigai Deepam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tiruchi Railway Division had made comprehensive arrangements for issue of tickets, crowd management, and had operated 24 special trains to the temple town to clear the extra rush

Amid a massive turnout of devotees for the Karthigai Deepam festival, the Tiruvannamalai railway station falling under the Tiruchi Railway Division’s jurisdiction netted over ₹60 lakh as originating revenue through sale of unreserved and reserved tickets from November 23 to 25 when special trains were operated to clear the extra rush.

Anticipating a large turnout of devotees for the annual festival, the Tiruchi Railway Division had put in place special measures at Tiruvannamalai station for ticketing facilities, crowd management, and ensuring safety of travellers. Tiruvannamalai is a block station on the Villupuram-Katpadi broad gauge section and classified under the NSG-4 category.

As for ticketing facilities, additional counters were opened in the booking office at Tiruvannamalai station besides two special counters for the festival at the Chief Booking Supervisor office. Besides these, three additional Automatic Ticket Vending Machines were installed to cater to the ticketing demand. In addition to the existing commercial staff, extra staff were deployed for the booking counters and at the enquiry booth/ help desk at the station.

Railway sources said the originating revenue of the Tiruvannamalai station on November 23, 24 and 25 was over ₹60 lakh through sale of tickets. The originating revenue peaked on November 24 when the Mahadeepam’ was lit atop the Arunachala hill at Tiruvannamalai on the Karthigai Deepam festival day. It was over ₹29.5 lakh on that day, said the sources. A day after the Mahadeepam on November 25, the originating revenue of the station exceeded ₹27 lakh. The originating revenue on November 23 was more than ₹5.29 lakh.

The sources said the total footfall at Tiruvannamalai station on November 23, 24 and 25 exceeded 85,000. The footfall at the station on the day when the Mahadeepam was lit on November 24 was more than 44,000. A team of railway officers, led by the Divisional Railway Manager, Tiruchi, camped in Tiruvannamalai from November 23 to 25 to monitor the arrangements and crowd management.

A round-the-clock help desk was set up by the Railway Protection Force at Tiruvannamalai station where a war room equipped with CCTV camera surveillance for constant monitoring of crowd movements was established. Over 90 Railway Protection Force personnel of Tiruchi Division were deployed at the station.

As Tiruvannamalai station falls on the Villupuram -Katpadi broad gauge section, train escorts were provided at both ends. Close coordination was maintained with the Government Railway Police and the local police for crowd regulation from the railway station to the temple and back.

Sources said 24 special trains were operated exclusively for the festival from November 23 to 25, including from Tiruchi to Vellore Cantonment, Villupuram to Vellore, and from Tiruvannamalai to Villupuram. Over 600 unreserved coaches were deployed to cater to the needs of the passengers.

articles.title: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The latest proposal by the USTR takes the tariff framework on India back to what it was at the start of trade deal negotiations

The new 25% tariffs proposed by the U.S. on India do not pose a substantial risk to Indian exports, and India should go ahead with a trade deal only if it is balanced and reciprocal, according to exporters and trade and tariff experts.

An analysis of India’s trade relationship with the U.S. over the last two years showed that the latest tariffs announced by the U.S. have returned the tariff relationship to where it was at the start of trade deal negotiations.
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed a net tariff of 25% on goods imported from India, which could be reduced to 17% if a trade deal is signed by the two countries.

The proposed 25% tariff is nearly the same as the 26% tariff U.S. President Donald Trump had originally proposed in his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariff measure in April 2025. A week later, Mr. Trump paused these tariffs in a bid to secure trade deals with other countries.

In July 2025, he announced a 25% tariff on India, the same as what the USTR is now proposing. But Mr. Trump soon announced an additional 25% tariff as a penalty for India’s Russian oil imports taking the total tariff on Indian goods to 50%.

During that time, Mr. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on the import of steel and aluminium from all countries. The latest tariffs by the USTR are not in addition to those tariffs, meaning Indian steel and aluminium will continue to attract a 50% duty.

In February 2026, India and the U.S. issued a joint statement announcing the framework for an interim deal on trade, under which the U.S. would reduce its tariffs on Indian goods to 18%. This is very close to the 17% the U.S. is proposing now, should a deal be signed, nearly 10 months after the joint statement was issued.
As such, the pre-deal, post-deal, and steel and aluminium tariffs by the U.S. on India largely remain where they were at the start of negotiations.
Exporters and trade experts have said that India should proceed with a trade deal only if it satisfies Indian interests.

“FIEO supports the government’s efforts to conclude the Bilateral Trade Agreement at an early date,” said S.C. Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations. “The agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level-playing field with suppliers from other countries in the U.S. market.”

The president of the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Anil Gupta, pointed out that the tariffs will have a limited impact on Indian exports due to the nature of the commodities that India predominantly exports to the U.S.

“India’s top exports to the U.S. include electronic goods, drugs and pharmaceuticals, gems and jewellery, and textiles and apparel,” Mr. Gupta said. “As these products account for more than 50% of Indian exports to the U.S. and are price-sticky, there will be limited impact in the short to medium term.”

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.
High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article.

Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18.
“The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out.
Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased.

On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.
“Strong bank and non-bank credit growth continues to support the domestic economy. Further, sustained double-digit export growth broadened the base of economic expansion,” they added.
Equity markets remained buoyant amid robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio investment inflows, while net inflows through external commercial borrowings and NRI deposits remained strong.

articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.
Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.
Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

📈 Economy & Finance 📅 25 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates

Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.

September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.

Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.

Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27

Air passenger services recorded 35.52% inflation in the July-September quarter, recording the highest rate of price rise among the seven major services for which the inflation data was released on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

Securities transaction services and banking services, however, recorded a deflation of 6.93% and 3.96% respectively, the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27 released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry showed.
The PPI has inflation data for seven major services — Banking, Securities Transaction, Insurance, Management of Pension Funds, Railways, Air (Passenger), and Telecom — with base year 2022-23.
Service PPI measures the change in the average prices received by producers on production of a service.
As per the data, inflation in Air (Passenger) Services rose 35.52% YoY in the second quarter, compared to 31.94% in the first quarter.
Annual inflation in the railway passenger service price index rose 2.17% during the September quarter, lower than 3.50% in the June quarter.
Inflation in 'Banking Service Contribution' was 3.86% in Q2 of FY27, higher than 2.62% in Q1. The 'Banking Service Price' witnessed 3.96% deflation in Q2, vis-a-vis 4.98% deflation in Q1.
Securities Transaction Service Prices saw a deflation of 6.93% in Q2, compared to 1.32% deflation in June quarter.

Pension fund management, insurance and telecom services recorded an inflation of 1.01%, 0.49% and 0.54%, respectively in September quarter, compared to 5.48%, 0.98% and 0.72%, respectively in the June quarter.
The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.

The government in June came out with the maiden PPI data for both goods and services to better reflect price movement at producer's level, paving the way for phasing out wholesale price index (WPI)-based inflation numbers in the next five years. Thereafter, in August the services PPI data was issued.

articles.title: Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fuel ‘clout’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the negotiating process more urgent than ever.

The failure of the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, to agree on its central political statement, with countries unable to bridge their differences over fossil fuels and other key questions of climate action, has exposed the fragility of international climate cooperation. It should also sharpen scrutiny of who gets access to climate negotiations, whose interests they represent and what safeguards keep decisions accountable to the public.

The Türkiye summit ended without agreement on an overarching statement. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he shared the “deep disappointment” of many that the conference was unable to reach consensus on a statement that typically sends a policy signal to all nations. Some separate negotiating decisions were reached though. Nevertheless, the absence of a political consensus was a serious setback.

The breakdown does not show that fossil fuel lobbying caused the impasse. But it does make more urgent a separate question about the credibility of the process. A forum that asks governments to make decisions in the global public interest must be transparent about who is seeking to shape those decisions, what interests they represent and how conflicts are managed.

The international climate negotiations that take place every year still lack a comprehensive, enforceable system to identify and manage conflicts of interest involving powerful commercial interests, including fossil fuel companies and state-owned energy businesses. The Antalya conference has underlined why that gap matters.

The fossil fuel industry’s record of muddying the waters is well documented. A 2017 study by Geoffrey Supran and Naomi Oreskes compared 187 ExxonMobil communications between 1977 and 2014, including internal documents, scientific publications and paid newspaper advertorials. It found that as the company’s communications became more public, they increasingly expressed doubt about climate science. The researchers concluded that ExxonMobil had contributed to climate science while promoting doubt about it in its advertorials.

An industry team discussed a 1998 draft of the Global Climate Science Communications Plan at the American Petroleum Institute’s headquarters. The plan’s stated goal was to persuade a majority of the American public that significant uncertainties remained in climate science and to raise questions among policymakers.

This history matters because companies with large investments in oil, gas and coal have a financial stake in how quickly those fuels are phased down, which technologies receive support and how the costs of the transition are distributed. That does not mean every company representative at a climate summit is there to obstruct progress, or that attendance proves influence over a decision. It, however, does mean commercial interests need to be visible and the process needs rules to prevent undue influence.

The scale of corporate participation in Antalya brings the issue into sharper focus. An analysis by a coalition of non-profits identified 103 major polluter groups with delegations at the summit, including fossil fuel businesses, financiers and companies from other high-emitting sectors. It also identified 30 banks whose fossil fuel financing between 2021 and 2025 amounted to more than $2.2 trillion.

These are the coalition’s classifications, not official UN figures. They do not establish that the companies or banks influenced the negotiations. But they show the scale of commercial interests present at a conference whose purpose is to limit global warming.

Lien Vandamme of the Center for International Environmental Law says the problem goes beyond the number of corporate participants. Although the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has introduced limited disclosure requirements, she argues that it still lacks a policy to curb corporate influence. “There is currently no policy to curb corporate influence within the UNFCCC process, and this is a fundamental problem,” she says. Once companies gain access, she argues, it becomes extremely difficult to monitor how they use it to influence negotiations.

The distinction between access and proven influence matters. The presence of a company representative does not show that a final decision was shaped by that company. But without public information about who participants represent, who funds their participation and what interests they promote and advance, it is difficult to assess where influence may be exercised.

The issue also extends beyond private companies. Some governments are major producers of oil and gas, while state-owned energy firms have direct commercial interests in the outcome of climate negotiations. Safeguards that examine only private corporations would leave a substantial part of the problem untouched.

articles.title: Serbia sets Presidential election for December 27 after students won Parliamentary vote
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25

Serbia 's Parliament speaker on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set an early Presidential election for December 27, after former President Aleksandar Vucic resigned in September to pursue what turned out to be a failed bid to become Prime Minister.
The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25.

Mr. Vucic and his party had ruled virtually unchallenged for 14 years. He had run for Prime Minister after serving two near-complete five-year terms as President, and was banned by law from seeking a third term.
“I hope we will have a tough choice between top candidates and their programmes," Speaker Aleksandar Cupic said. “Building democratic institutions is the task for all of us.”
It was not immediately clear who the Presidential candidates will be. Mr. Vucic has suggested that his SNS party could sit out the election.

The Presidency in Serbia is largely ceremonial. The President commands the Army and has a say in foreign policy but has no executive powers. While he was in office, however, Mr. Vucic concentrated power in the Presidency, facing accusations of authoritarian rule. Mr. Vucic regularly announced important state decisions and policies and even presided over government sessions.

Since losing power, Mr. Vucic has accused the election winners of imposing a “revolutionary terror,” although his government is still technically in control until a new one is formed. The change in power has led to a surge in detentions of officials and police officers suspected of abusing their positions during Mr. Vucic's rule.

The youth-led movement had led two years of street protests that started in response to a train station canopy collapse in northern Serbia that killed 16 people. Many blamed the tragedy on alleged rampant corruption and negligence during the building renovation in Novi Sad.

articles.title: U.K. net migration falls to lowest since 1997; Indians largest foreign group entering and leaving the country
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed

Net migration to the U.K. has fallen to 77,000, its lowest levels since 1997, excluding the pandemic, as per official U.K. government figures released on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group immigrating and emigrating longterm to and from the U.K.

The net migration figure, which represents the number of people arriving in the U.K. minus those emigrating, fell dramatically from 2,04,000 for the year ending June 2025 and from a record high of 9,00,000 in the year ending June 2023. The news is likely to a shot in the arm for the governing Labour Party, as migration has become a political lighting-rod in recent years.

The latest drop in numbers was predominantly due to a fall in non-EU migration to the U.K. This figure fell by more then 1,00,000 while emigration remained mostly stable. Non-EU+ nationals arriving in the U.K. fell by 17% to 7,38,000. Just under half came to study, a quarter for work, and 13% for asylum.

Of those migrating to the U.K., the largest group consisted of Indians , then Chinese, then Nigerians, Pakistanis and Americans. Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed.
More EU+ and British nationals left the U.K. than non-EU+ nationals. Some 2,45,00 Britons left the country longterm in the year ending June 2026, with net migration of Britons at -1,37,000.

These record high net migration numbers in 2023 — called the ‘Boriswave’, occurred during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative, following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, when visa rules were eased to fill certain occupations such as social care. Migration from non-EU countries consequently increased at this time. Mr. Johnson’s successors, Rishi Sunak, a fellow Conservative, and then Prime Minister Keir Starmer of the Labour Party, further tightened immigration policies resulting in falling numbers.

articles.title: German police arrest two Iraqis over alleged Cologne synagogue bomb plot
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Germany has suffered a series ⁠of attacks and plots in recent years, including a fatal attack in July in which a man who pledged ‌allegiance to Islamic State attacked a Pride celebration in Berlin

German prosecutors said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) they had arrested two Iraqi nationals suspected ​of belonging to a terrorist organisation that plotted attacks ‌on Jewish and other targets in Europe, including ​a Cologne synagogue.

Germany has suffered a series ⁠of attacks and plots in recent years, including a fatal attack in July in which a man who pledged ‌allegiance to Islamic State attacked a Pride celebration in Berlin. Jewish institutions are under heightened protection after warnings of threats linked ‌to ⁠West Asia tensions.

Prosecutors said officers had ⁠detained Mostafa Al-R. in Heidelberg and Ameer J. in Cologne, with their full names withheld in line with privacy rules, following ​17 raids in ‌the states of Baden-Wuerttemberg, Hesse and North Rhine-Westphalia.

They said Mostafa Al-R. had ties to Mohammad Al-Saadi, an alleged member of an Islamist group that ‌has said it was behind a series ​of attacks on U.S., Israeli and Jewish facilities in Europe since March.

Prosecutors said that ⁠Al-Saadi, Mostafa Al-R. and others had formed a separate organisation in late 2025 to prepare further attacks ‌in Germany and elsewhere in Europe. Ameer J. was a member of that group, they said.
It recruited external operatives and raised funds for explosives attacks, prosecutors said.

They said that on two consecutive nights in late March, unidentified individuals suspected of ‌acting on the group's behalf and carrying explosive devices ​had travelled to a synagogue in Cologne and another unspecified location in Europe, but no ⁠attacks were carried out for reasons that were ⁠unclear.
The two suspects were due on Thursday (November 26, 2026) to appear before a Judge who will ‌decide whether they remain in pre-trial detention.
Authorities said the investigation was launched because of intelligence supplied ​by Germany's domestic intelligence agency.

articles.title: Situation in India-China border areas remains ‘generally stable’, says China
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh

The situation in the India-China border areas remain “generally stable”, China’s Defence Ministry spokesperson and PLA Senior Colonel Chen Xi said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) adding that China “does not recognize the so-called Arunachal Pradesh illegally set up by India.”

“China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels, including general-level talks, to jointly implement the consensus reached by the two sides and safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas”, he said in response to a question at a press briefing on recent tensions in the Eastern sector of the border, Chinese state media reported.

On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.

Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between. The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector. Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

articles.title: ‘Unbelievable catch’: Pakistan motorbike passenger becomes cricket sensation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Batsman Abrar Lala struck a looping six, sending the ball towards the road adjoining the cricket ground in Pakistan’s picturesque Swat Valley, where Khan plucked it out of the air with one hand

Returning home from work on the back of a friend’s motorbike in northwest Pakistan, Mehran Khan acted on pure instinct when a cricket ball sailed towards him and he nonchalantly took a one-handed catch that has won him instant global fame.
“I told my friend who was riding the motorcycle to lower his head. I stood up slightly on the moving motorcycle and caught it,” the civil servant, an experienced amateur cricketer, told AFP .
“Words cannot describe how happy I was after taking that catch. It felt as though I had achieved something extraordinary,” the 27-year-old added.
Khan and his friend were motoring past a match in the Swat Premier League in the city of Mingora when the ball arched towards them over the boundary on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
Batsman Abrar Lala struck a looping six, sending the ball towards the road adjoining the cricket ground in Pakistan’s picturesque Swat Valley, where Khan plucked it out of the air with one hand.
“I have been playing cricket since childhood and have played several matches at this very ground,” Khan, a government employee with the Public Health Engineering Department, explained.
“When the batsman hit the six I instinctively wished I could catch the ball,” he added.
The moment has gone viral around the world and drawn the praise of cricketing greats.
“Fame that some people do not achieve in years came to me through a video lasting just a few seconds,” Khan said.
“My life has changed completely. Now, whenever I go out, people recognise me and ask to take selfies with me.
“When I returned home that night my family gave me a wonderful welcome,” he said.
“Nobody had ever asked to take selfies with me like that before,” he added.

articles.title: BITS Pilani-Hyderabad researchers develop affordable way to grow microalgae
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Researchers at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, have secured an Indian patent for a low-cost nutrient medium that could make large-scale cultivation of microalgae more affordable, opening possibilities for applications in renewable fuels, carbon capture and biotechnology.

The patented innovation, titled “Nutrient Medium Composition for Mass Cultivation of Microalgae” (Patent No. 603126), has been developed by Sandip S. Deshmukh of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, K. Pranav Narayan of the Department of Biological Sciences and research scholar Sama Sanghamitra, as per a press release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

Microalgae are microscopic organisms that use sunlight and carbon dioxide to produce biomass. They are considered a promising resource for wastewater treatment, carbon dioxide capture, biofertilisers, food and nutraceutical products, and the production of biodiesel and other bio-based fuels. However, the high cost of cultivation has limited their large-scale adoption.

The BITS team developed an alternative nutrient formulation using locally available agricultural-grade fertilisers instead of expensive laboratory-grade chemicals. The formulation supplies key nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur required for microalgal growth while reducing the complexity and cost of preparing the cultivation medium.

The macronutrients needed to prepare 100 litres of the new medium cost about ₹2.40, compared with around ₹43 for the conventional Bold’s Basal Medium (BBM). The cost is estimated to be around ₹4.50 per 100 litres, making it significantly cheaper than conventional alternatives.

The formulation is also easy to prepare and can be supplied as a dry powder, which can be dissolved in water before use. The technology was tested in laboratory, non-sterile and outdoor cultivation conditions. The microalgae was also successfully cultivated in a 10,000-litre open pond using natural sunlight and atmospheric carbon dioxide.

Researchers are now in discussions with a potential industry partner, which has proposed a two-month evaluation of the formulation for carbon capture and biomass production applications. They are also seeking collaborations with companies in biofuel, algal biotechnology and carbon management sectors to explore commercialisation of the technology.

articles.title: IREF say non-basmati rice export bans are unlikely, but urges exporters to remain cautious
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The government is unlikely to impose restrictions on non-basmati rice exports over the next month, the Indian Rice Exporters’ Federation (IREF) said on its portal on Wednesday (November 26, 2026).
It, however, urged rice exporters to continue business with appropriate contractual and inventory safeguards.

The Federation claimed that based on information received from sources familiar with policy discussions, its current assessment was that while policy options remain under consideration, there is no indication of an immediate move to curb exports.
However, the possibility of export duties or other policy measures cannot be ruled out, particularly if domestic rice prices continue to rise.

India’s substantial rice stocks provide an important cushion for domestic supply. The Public Distribution System (PDS), through which eligible households receive subsidised or free foodgrains under their entitlements, also helps protect beneficiaries from fluctuations in open-market prices.
However, strong international demand continues to influence domestic market dynamics. Any further significant icrease in domestic prices can prompt a review of the export policy.

articles.title: Mercury in cosmetics: What does the Kerala case reveal about the health risks of skin-lightening creams? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: What does the recent case in Kerala reveal about mercury poisoning from cosmetics? How does exposure affect the kidneys, and what safeguards are in place to regulate unsafe products?

The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Kerala.

Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm

After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online

Vivo X500 Pro Max ships with a 7,800 mAh battery supported by a 90W wired charger and a 40W wireless charging support. It is IP68 and IP69 rated for dust and water resistance.

Vivo X500 Pro Max runs on MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset with up to 12 GB RAM and 512 GB storage. It operates on OriginOS 7 based on Android 17 out of the box. The phone will get 7 years of OS and security patches.
The Vivo X500 Pro Max sports a 50 MP main camera, a 200 MP telephoto camera and a 50 MP ultrawide lens. It has a 50 MP front camera.
Vivo X500 Pro Max comes in Apex Orange and Eternal Black. It starts at ₹1,64,999 (12GB/256GB) and ₹1,79,999 (12GB/512GB). The sale begins December 3.

Vivo X500 Pro uses a 6,510 mAh battery with a 90W wired and 40W wireless charging support.
Vivo X500 Pro also features MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro with up to 12 GB RAM and 256 GB storage. It too operates on OriginOS 7.
Vivo X500 Pro sports a 50 MP main camera, a 64 MP telephoto lens and a 50 MP ultrawide camera. It also features a 50 MP selfie camera.
Vivo X500 Pro starts at ₹1,49,999 (12GB/256GB). It goes on sale starting December 3.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

Editorial Context: Core accountability: On core sector performance. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Climate action has to be timely, with adequate resources and monitoring

That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.
