articles.title: IIMBAA to bring 500 alumni, 115 CXOs and 21 management institutions together for sports fest in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A two-day inter-institutional alumni sports festival will see participation from several premier institutions, including alumni communities from IIM, ISB and XLRI

The IIM Bangalore Alumni Association (IIMBAA), to bring together some of India’s management institutions on a common sporting platform, is hosting a two-day inter-institutional alumni sports festival in Bengaluru, with participation from 21 premier institutions, including alumni communities from IIM, ISB and XLRI.

The event, scheduled to be held between November 28 (Saturday) and November 29 (Sunday), is expected to bring together approximately 500 alumni participants and 300 visitors, making it a significant gathering of India’s management alumni community, as per a statement.

"The event is distinctive for the participation of more than 115 senior corporate leaders, founders, CXOs, partners and Vice Presidents from leading organisations, who will step away from their boardrooms and business responsibilities to compete alongside fellow alumni on the sports field,’’ IIMBAA said.

The participating institutions include IIM Ahmedabad, IIM Amritsar, IIM Bodh Gaya, IIM Calcutta, IIM Indore, IIM Jammu, IIM Kozhikode, IIM Lucknow, IIM Mumbai, IIM Raipur, IIM Ranchi, IIM Rohtak, IIM Sambalpur, IIM Shillong, IIM Sirmaur, IIM Tiruchirappalli, IIM Udaipur, IIM Visakhapatnam, the Indian School of Business (ISB) and XLRI Jamshedpur.

According to the statement, the event would be part of IIMBAA’s initiatives towards building bridges across various management institutions in the country. "By leading the conceptualisation, organisation, and convening of alumni communities from 21 premier management institutions, IIMBAA is creating a distinctive platform for inter-institutional engagement through sport,’’ it said.

articles.title: Three held for killing 22-year-old in D.J. Halli over motorcycle dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The D.J. Halli police have arrested a group of three for beating their 22-year-old friend to death over a dispute related to a motorcycle in D.J. Halli.
The accused have been identified as Mohammed Tameem, 23, Mohammed Mudassir, 22, and Syed Yunus. The victim, Amber, was staying with the accused in D.J. Halli.
They were doing odd jobs and staying in a room on the terrace of the house belonging to the father of one of the accused.

According to the police, a quarrel broke out among them over an issue related to a motorcycle theft. During the argument, Junaid, Yunus and the others allegedly assaulted Amber, punching him repeatedly on his face, back and stomach.

The assault reportedly caused internal bleeding. However, instead of taking him to a hospital, the accused allegedly kept him at home. They reportedly gave him oral rehydration solution (ORS) and some food, but Amber, who was injured and in a deteriorating condition, died in his sleep after the accused left for work.

Initially, the police treated the incident as a case of suspicious death. However, a post-mortem examination revealed that Amber had died due to internal bleeding, prompting the D.J. Halli police to register a murder case and launch an investigation.
The investigation revealed that Amber had been assaulted by his own friends. The four accused were subsequently arrested.
The police said the failure to provide timely medical attention despite knowing about his condition led to the death. The accused have been booked for murder.

articles.title: IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up.

It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities.

Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence.

Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival.

Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.

• Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.

articles.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”.

In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”.

He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”.

The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties.

Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi

The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer.
Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house.

The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages.
The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation.
The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry.

In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. The protesters raised slogans alleging lack of safety for women.
The DMK’s women wing also staged a demonstration at the Four Roads junction in Kallakurichi demanding the arrest of the MLA. They burnt the effigy of the MLA and raised slogans against him.
Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

articles.title: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say they have received no such communication and warn that Section 163 of BNSS remains in force in the area

No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls , scheduled for November 26 , senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration.

The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands.

An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu , was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. It stated: “This is to inform you that we, the Delhi People Against SIR, are going to observe Constitution Day as per the details given.”

The email further stated that participants would assemble outside Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 and march towards Jantar Mantar via Kali Bari Marg. “This is for your information and any follow-up/arrangements,” it added.
“We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, told The Hindu .

Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration.

Public notice 🔶Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on 26.11.2026. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march. 🔶Section 163 BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi District. Unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas are prohibited. 🔶All are requested to comply with the order u/s 163 BNSS and cooperate with Police. Violations will invite legal action.

However, New Delhi police officers denied receiving the intimation and stressed that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remain in force in the area and warned that action would be taken against gatherings in violation of the restrictions.

The police said “preventive” security measures would be put in place to prevent any unauthorised gathering in the area. These would include multi-layer barricading, deployment of additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, to disperse crowds and prevent protesters from assembling in violation of the prohibitory orders.

People Against SIR was formed on October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.

The platform has claimed that more than 50% of the voters who were on Delhi’s electoral rolls in January 2025 and voted in the February 2025 Assembly election have either been deleted or categorised as doubtful following the revision exercise.

The organisers have described SIR as an attack on the Constitution and the right to vote, alleging that the exercise disproportionately affects marginalised communities, including minorities, Dalits, transgender persons, women, migrant workers and the homeless.

articles.title: G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.

Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges.

According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme.

articles.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court

The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6. The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided.

Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government. The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders.
“And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally.

The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions. The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30.
The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute.
The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144.

A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise.

Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents.
After the Single Judge Bench had refused his pleas for an interim stay of the elections, Mr. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.

articles.title: Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This was a promise made the BJP during their 2026 Assembly election campaign

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign.

During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security.

He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution.

“We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar.

At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it.

He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district.

articles.title: Fuel tanker crash ignites massive fire on highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 30 people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor’s office said in a statement
A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor's office said in a statement.
The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.

At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading amongst the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.
Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.

Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.

Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 injured in a massive multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

articles.title: Uttariya instead of robes: West Bengal Government suggests universities to adopt Indian attire in convocations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay said that the government was putting effort to follow own Indian culture and tradition and Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies

West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony.

“We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya.
“As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college.
In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes.
Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients.

Monday’s (November 23) notice to the VCs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said.

“In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay said that the government was putting effort to follow own Indian culture and tradition and Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies

West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony.

“We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya.

“As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college.

In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes.

Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients.

Monday’s (November 23) notice to the VCs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said.

“In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

articles.title: Congress wins majority of Zila Pramukh posts in Rajasthan polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts

After its decisive victory in the last week’s Panchayati Raj elections, the Opposition Congress in Rajasthan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) took control of 24 of the 37 zila parishads which elected their heads, while the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party secured 10 Zila Pramukh posts despite having a majority in just five rural district bodies.

The Bharat Adivasi Party won tribal-dominated Banswara and Dungarpur, while Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal’s Rashtriya Loktantrik Party retained Nagaur. No independent candidate was elected Zila Pramukh in any district.

The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts. Members elected in the panchayat polls voted on Wednesday to choose their respective heads, while the results in the remaining four districts – Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar – will be declared in December.

The BJP pulled off a surprise victory in Churu, where the Congress had a clear majority, and secured five of the eight zila parishads where no party had an absolute majority. The Congress largely managed to keep its flock together, losing only one of the 23 rural bodies where it enjoyed majority.

Congress candidate Mamta Gurjar defeated BJP’s Nirmala Rawat by just one vote in Beawar, despite the BJP having a majority. Renu Wala of Congress defeated BJP’s Pooja Jatav by 17 votes to 14 in Bharatpur, which is Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma’s home district.

Among the zila parishads where no party had a clear majority, the BJP won Balotra, Didwana-Kuchaman, Deeg, Khairthal-Tijara and Pratapgarh, and the Congress won Salumbar. In Churu, where the Congress held 21 of the 39 seats against the BJP’s 17, ruling party candidate Kanika Singh, daughter-in-law of former Minister Rajendra Rathore, defeated Congress candidate Prakash Devi, indicating cross-voting.

Congress candidate Nikita Dudi defeated party rebel Sarita Choudhary, who contested as an Independent, by 23 votes to 18 in Bikaner. Dissatisfaction over the party nomination had reportedly led to the rebellion, while the BJP had withdrawn its candidate in Bikaner.

The Congress narrowly avoided an embarrassment in Dholpur despite holding 21 of the 29 seats, as its candidate Anisha Singh defeated her nearest rival by just one vote. The BJP also secured Balotra zila parishad by one vote. The Congress registered comfortable victories in several of its traditional strongholds, including Jaipur, Jodhpur, Alwar, Sikar and Bhilwara.

Twenty-one-year-old Congress candidate Santosh Kumari was elected unopposed as Zila Pramukh in Jaisalmer. Ms. Kumari, who completed her class XII and is unmarried, belongs to a Scheduled Tribe community. Two other candidates elected unopposed were Beena Bairwa in Dausa and Asha Devi in Sawai Madhopur. Both of them were Congress candidates.

There were stray incidents of arguments and jostling at some places during the election process. Tensions were reported in Jaipur, Bharatpur and Bhilwara, where workers and leaders of rival parties were involved in heated exchanges.

Veteran Congress leader and former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot congratulated the new elected Zila Pramukhs, saying the rural public had reposed faith in them by voting against the BJP government’s “misrule”. “I trust that you will become the voice of the villagers, farmers and livestock keepers,” Mr. Gehlot said.

articles.title: Delhi High Court grants time to ED to respond to Engineer Rashid’s plea
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Sachin Datta listed the matter for further hearing on December 16 after the prosecutor said he needed one week to consult the special public prosecutor in the case

The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) granted time to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to respond to a plea by Baramulla MP Abdul Rashid Sheikh , challenging the framing of charges against him in a money laundering case linked to alleged funding from Pakistan through hawala channels for secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir.
Justice Sachin Datta listed the matter for further hearing on December 16 after the prosecutor said he needed one week to consult the special public prosecutor in the case.
Mr. Rashid Sheikh, also known as Engineer Rashid, has challenged a September 9 order by which the trial court had ordered the framing of charges against the people.

On October 24, the special court had formally framed charges against the accused and put them on trial under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) after finding sufficient material on record to raise a strong suspicion of their involvement in the offence.
The ED has alleged that proceeds of crime amounting to Rs 8.94 crore were generated and received, routed, transferred, concealed, possessed, acquired and used by the accused through various channels.

The seven accused include Malik, chief of the banned Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF), separatist leader Shabir Ahmad Shah, Masarat Alam, Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali, Naval Kishore Kapoor, and M/s Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd.

The ED case stems from a 2017 National Investigation Agency (NIA) case in which charges under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) were invoked.

The prosecution has alleged that the accused received funds from the “Pakistani establishment” through hawala channels and other means to propagate secessionist activities and carry out acts prejudicial to the law of the land.

articles.title: Thane Crime Branch arrests five in Mumbra dacoity case, cracks seven other cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Some of the accused became acquainted in prison; stolen valuables worth ₹2.39 lakh recovered, four others wanted in the Mumbra case

The Thane Crime Branch has arrested five members of a gang allegedly involved in targeting bungalows and farmhouses across Thane district, solving eight cases, including the November 17 dacoity in Mumbra, officials said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Police have recovered stolen valuables worth ₹2.39 lakh from the accused.

The arrested accused have been identified as Vijay Chavan (45), Laxman Bhosale (43), Satish Waghe (27), Narayan Thombre (27), and Jayesh Kathore (35). All five have been remanded in police custody till November 30, while a search is underway for four other accused directly linked to the Mumbra case.

According to the police, eight to nine persons allegedly broke into the bungalow of complainant Tukaram Munde in Mumbra on November 17, threatened him with sharp weapons, restrained him and fled with gold ornaments worth ₹1.55 lakh and ₹84,000 in cash. Police have since recovered the stolen property.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav said the accused had been conducting reconnaissance in the area for six months.
“Even after the November 17 dacoity in Mumbra, Bhosale and Vijay Chavan conducted reconnaissance in Panvel. Information regarding this has emerged during the investigation,” Mr. Jadhav said.
The accused allegedly targeted residential properties, forcibly entered houses, restrained occupants and security guards, and assaulted or threatened them before fleeing with valuables.

During the investigation, Crime Branch officials examined footage from around 150 to 200 CCTV cameras, conducted technical analysis and gathered intelligence through informants to identify and apprehend the accused.

Police said Chavan, the main accused and a resident of Badlapur, has 18 criminal cases registered against him, including dacoity, robbery and theft, across several police jurisdictions in Maharashtra. Another accused, Thombre, also has a previous criminal case registered against him.

According to Mr. Jadhav, some of the accused had previously committed offences alongside Chavan, while some had become acquainted in prison. Police said members of the gang had been released from prison around six months ago. The accused allegedly operated in different groups and assembled after identifying potential targets.
The investigation has also led to the detection of seven other cases registered at the Kulgaon, Kalyan Taluka, Vasind and Padgha police stations.

Mr. Jadhav said the involvement of several other individuals who allegedly assisted the accused in conducting reconnaissance had also emerged during the investigation, taking the estimated number of wanted persons to seven or eight.

The Mumbra police are conducting further investigations, with the Crime Branch carrying out a parallel probe to apprehend the remaining accused and ascertain whether the gang was involved in other offences.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The band’s imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as ‘Girls on Film’ and ‘Union of the Snake’ and the moody ballads ‘The Chauffeur’ and ‘Save a Prayer’

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran , whose huge pop hits include “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life, he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed,” the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Music Award recipients.

The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as “Girls on Film” and “Union of the Snake” and the moody ballads “The Chauffeur” and “Save a Prayer”. Other hits in the coming years included “The Wild Boys,” “New Moon on Monday” and “Come Undone.” Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song “A View to a Kill” and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesisers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan, and that meant a lot to the band.

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran , whose huge pop hits include “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life, he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed,” the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Music Award recipients.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu introduces 15 days of paternity leave for married government employees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The paternity leave can be availed by male employees either 15 days before the birth of the child or within six months from the date of birth.
In a significant move, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male employees of the State government.

According to an official release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026), the paternity leave can be availed by male employees either 15 days before the birth of the child or within six months from the date of birth. While female employees working in the Tamil Nadu government are currently provided 365 days of maternity leave, the government has introduced paternity leave for male employees following requests from government employees.
What did the Supreme Court say about paid maternity leave?

The provision of 365 days of maternity leave to female government employees reflects the importance attached to motherhood and the welfare of the child, the release said. Similarly, extending paternity leave to male government employees would help them share family responsibilities and ensure the father’s involvement in raising the child, it added.

articles.title: Situation in India-China border areas remain ‘generally stable’, says China
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh

The situation in the India-China border areas remain “generally stable”, China’s Defence Ministry spokesperson and PLA Senior Colonel Chen Xi said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) adding that China “does not recognize the so-called Arunachal Pradesh illegally set up by India.”

“China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels, including general-level talks, to jointly implement the consensus reached by the two sides and safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas”, he said in response to a question at a press briefing on recent tensions in the Eastern sector of the border, Chinese state media reported.

On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.

Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between. The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector. Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

articles.title: Amid wildlife deaths, Keralam Forest dept warns Sabarimala pilgrims against littering on Pamba route
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two bonnet macaques and a Nilgiri langur died after being hit by vehicles on the route between November 16 and 23, officials said

The Keralam Forest Department on Thursday urged Sabarimala pilgrims travelling along the Nilakkal-Pamba route not to throw food waste and plastic materials from vehicles, warning that littering is attracting wild animals to the road and increasing the risk of road accidents, officials said.
Two bonnet macaques and a Nilgiri langur died after being hit by vehicles on the route between November 16 and 23, officials said.
Assistant Conservator of Forests Manu Sathyan, in a statement, said the Nilgiri langur is a Schedule I species under the Wildlife Protection Act and primarily lives in trees.
The 19-km Nilakkal-Pamba road passes through forest areas, and the widening and asphalting of the road have increased the risk of vehicles travelling at high speeds, he said.
The department has recommended additional speed-control measures and the deployment of more sanitation workers in coordination with the Ranni Forest Division.

He has also appealed to pilgrims not to throw food waste or plastic materials from vehicles, as these attract monkeys and other wild animals to the roadside, exposing them to the danger of being run over.
The department has called for greater awareness among pilgrims and improved waste management along the route to prevent further wildlife deaths.

Meanwhile, the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) said that a 7,000-square-foot resting facility for pilgrims has been developed at Lower Appachimedu along the Sabarimala trekking route, providing space for up to 1,000 devotees to rest during their arduous climb to the Ayyappa temple.
Located near the existing offering centre, the facility has been developed with tiled flooring, steel benches, and built-in seating.
A drinking water kiosk and toilets have also been provided for the convenience of pilgrims.
The site had earlier remained abandoned and was renovated for ₹11 lakh, TDB said.
TDB president K Jayakumar, in a statement, said the inauguration of the renovated facility would be held before December.

articles.title: Polling under way in 23 urban local bodies and 3,240 gram panchayats in Andhra Pradesh | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 25 lakh voters to exercise their franchise in 964 wards; 2,968 candidates are in the fray; the count of votes scheduled for November 30
Tirupati MP Maddila Gurumoorthy alleged that the police had been detaining YSRCP leaders in Srikalahasti since 6 a.m. and stopping its polling agents from doing their work.

Mr. Gurumurthi also alleged that about 200 outsiders had gathered near Balaji School in Wards 20 and 26 to keep YSRCP workers away from polling stations, and that a party polling agent was beaten and driven out of a polling station in Ward 34. He urged the police to release the detained leaders and the State Election Commission to act on the party’s complaints.
The YSRCP alleged that two of its workers were injured in attacks by TDP leaders during polling on Thursday.

At Kattakindapalli in Anantapur Rural mandal, part of Raptadu constituency, Bonagiri Chandrashekar Reddy was injured in a clash and admitted to hospital, the party said. At Srirampuram in Reddigudem mandal of NTR district, YSRCP alleged that TDP leader Kesibabu and his followers attacked its polling agent, Veldi Rambabu, at the polling station. Mr. Rambabu was taken to hospital.
In the Kakinada Municipal Corporation, 26.64% of the 2,85,950 voters had cast their votes in the 66 wards by 11.30 a.m.

In the gram panchayat elections in Kakinada district, polling is under way in 99 panchayats in Kakinada Rural, Karapa, Thalluru, Peddapuram and Samarlakota mandals, where turnout was 62.29% at 11.30 a.m.”

On the orders of State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha, polling staff are marking the little finger of the left hand instead of the index finger, since ink from ​ the MPTC and ZPTC elections ​ earlier this month has not worn off for many voters.
ink.jpeg A woman shows the indelible ink on her little finger after voting at a polling station in Enikepadu, NTR district, on Thursday. Photo: K.V.S. Giri
The TDP alleged that YSRCP workers had indulged in rigging at Jammaladinne in Allagadda mandal of Nandyal district and attacked TDP leaders who tried to stop them, throwing acid at them.
The YSRCP, meanwhile, alleged in a post on its official X handle that TDP workers had rigged votes in front of the police at Vellaturu village in Palnadu district.

The YSRCP alleged in a post on its official X handle that the police had illegally taken former ZPTC member Gorla Upendra Reddy into custody at Shettipalli in Sambepalle mandal of Annamayya district. Villagers protested against the action, the party said, posting a video that it said showed the protest.
Polling in the gram panchayats ends at 1 p.m. Counting will begin at 2 p.m., and results are expected late in the afternoon. Turnout picked up towards noon, officials said.

articles.title: Why viral video of an earthmover near Kashmir’s Sheshnag Lake has sparked protests | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dismissing social media claims of fresh construction as “incorrect,” the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) clarified that the ongoing activity is strictly confined to widening and maintaining existing pilgrimage tracks

The story so far : A viral video showing an earthmover operating on the shores of Sheshnag, a high-altitude alpine glacial lake, in south Kashmir’s Anantnag district has sparked both online outrage and street protests across Jammu and Kashmir. Shot earlier this month by the operator of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO)-hired machine and posted to his Instagram account, the clip has drawn sharp criticism from environmentalists and political parties alike. They warn that deploying heavy machinery in an ecologically fragile zone, already threatened by receding glaciers, risks irreversible damage.

Located at an altitude of 11,780 feet, Sheshnag Lake spans roughly 1.1 km in length and 0.7 km in width. The alpine lake serves as a vital stopover for devotees undertaking the annual Amarnath pilgrimage in south Kashmir’s Anantnag district. Historically, pilgrims could only reach Sheshnag via a steep, 13-km trek —on foot, horseback, or palanquin— after the macadamised road ended at Chandanwari, before covering another 18–20 km of unpaved terrain to reach the Amarnath cave shrine at 12,756 feet.

Dr. Raja Muzaffar Bhat, chairman of the J&K Climate Action Group (JKCAG) and an environmental activist, cautions that ongoing excavation around Sheshnag Lake risks destabilising the lake’s morphology and threatening densely populated downstream areas. In a formal representation to the J&K administration, activists have called for an independent scientific investigation into slope cutting, excavation, and debris dumping at the site, citing serious risks to natural drainage, sedimentation, and environmental laws.

Pahalgam hosts major glaciers that feed the Jhelum River, including Kashmir’s largest glacier Kolahoi, which according to reports, has retreated substantially, losing up to 24% of its area and 50% of its ice volume since 1962. Meanwhile, data presented in the J&K Assembly this year revealed that authorities have mapped 616 glacial lakes across 12 districts, flagging 68 as “potentially dangerous” due to the rising threat of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) that can trigger devastating downstream flooding.

In response to the outcry, the Jammu and Kashmir government dispatched a 12-member inspection team, headed by a Forest Range Officer, to Sheshnag Lake on November 24. According to J&K Forest Minister Altaf Kaloo, the team found the viral video misleading, stating that the ongoing work is actually taking place 200 to 300 feet away from the lake. Mr. Kaloo ruled out tampering and maintained that “not a speck of earth has fallen into the lake.”

articles.title: ‘Unbelievable catch’: Pakistan motorbike passenger becomes cricket sensation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Batsman Abrar Lala struck a looping six, sending the ball towards the road adjoining the cricket ground in Pakistan’s picturesque Swat Valley, where Khan plucked it out of the air with one hand

Returning home from work on the back of a friend’s motorbike in northwest Pakistan, Mehran Khan acted on pure instinct when a cricket ball sailed towards him and he nonchalantly took a one-handed catch that has won him instant global fame.
“I told my friend who was riding the motorcycle to lower his head. I stood up slightly on the moving motorcycle and caught it,” the civil servant, an experienced amateur cricketer, told AFP .
“Words cannot describe how happy I was after taking that catch. It felt as though I had achieved something extraordinary,” the 27-year-old added.
Khan and his friend were motoring past a match in the Swat Premier League in the city of Mingora when the ball arched towards them over the boundary on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
Batsman Abrar Lala struck a looping six, sending the ball towards the road adjoining the cricket ground in Pakistan’s picturesque Swat Valley, where Khan plucked it out of the air with one hand.
“I have been playing cricket since childhood and have played several matches at this very ground,” Khan, a government employee with the Public Health Engineering Department, explained.
“When the batsman hit the six I instinctively wished I could catch the ball,” he added.
The moment has gone viral around the world and drawn the praise of cricketing greats.
“Fame that some people do not achieve in years came to me through a video lasting just a few seconds,” Khan said.
“My life has changed completely. Now, whenever I go out, people recognise me and ask to take selfies with me.
“When I returned home that night my family gave me a wonderful welcome,” he said.
“Nobody had ever asked to take selfies with me like that before,” he added.

“Giving shares, which are stakes in ‌the future economy, directly to the people is the way,” Mr. Musk ​added.

articles.title: FedEx airplane overruns runway at Miami airport, closing all but one runway
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: There were no reports of injuries after the plane ran off the runway at about 8.40 p.m., the airport reported

A FedEx airplane overran a runway at the Miami International Airport on Wednesday night (November 25, 2026), forcing all but one runway to temporarily close the day before Thanksgiving, according to officials.

There were no reports of injuries after the plane ran off the runway at about 8.40 p.m., the airport reported. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units have responded. The incident happened almost three months after an Amazon cargo jet overshot another runway in Miami, killing five people on the ground.
The McDonnell Douglas MD-11 was coming from Memphis, and flights will be resuming shortly, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. The administration will investigate.
FedEx said the plane had “an issue upon landing” and that it is coordinating with investigating officials.
“We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries,” the company said in a statement.

FedEx had just started flying MD-11s again in May to deliver packages after that type of plane crashed in Kentucky last year as it was taking off. The UPS plane's left engine flew off and three pilots along with 12 people on the ground were killed. The FAA had approved Boeing's proposed fix for the MD-11s “after extensive review.”
The airport recommended that passengers scheduled to fly Wednesday night should check with their airlines for the latest flight updates before travelling to the airport.
“We appreciate our passengers' patience as we work to safely resume normal operations,” the airport said in a statement.

The runway this FedEx plane landed on Wednesday is different than the one the Amazon cargo plane overran in September. But three of Miami's runways converge at the west end, so the FedEx plane ended up close to where the Amazon plane careened across a road and struck a van filled with a plane cleaning crew.

The incident also comes less than two weeks after a minor collision between two planes at a taxiway intersection at the Miami airport. The wing of the Copa flight and the nose of the UPS plane collided.
The National Transportation Safety Board said it had no information about the incident.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The National Transportation Safety Board said it had no information about the incident.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return gambit tests Bangladesh’s political fault lines
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The ousted leader’s December 16 return plan has energised the Awami League leaders and cadre, tested Tarique Rahman’s government and complicated Dhaka’s efforts to reset ties with New Delhi

Mahmud Tanzid, a 27-year-old private-sector employee in Dhaka, has postponed a trip he had planned for the first week of December. After weeks of unrest, particularly in Gopalganj, and with former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announcing her intention to return to Bangladesh on December 16, he fears the situation could deteriorate further. He is no longer certain what the coming weeks will bring as Ms. Hasina’s Awami League has already called a nationwide lockdown on November 29-30.

Whether Ms. Hasina actually lands in Dhaka on December 16 or not, she has already reshaped Bangladesh’s political calendar. Her announcement has turned the countdown to Victory Day, which marks the end of the nine-month Liberation War in 1971 and the official surrender of Pakistani forces to the joint command of Bangladeshi and Indian forces, into a test of political will.

The 79-year-old former Prime Minister intends to end more than two years of exile in India on Victory Day. It is the first time she has specified a date for her return. In doing so, the Awami League, which was banned by the post-Hasina interim administration, has transformed what began as a localised law-and-order crisis into a national contest over political legitimacy.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government’s response has been uncompromising. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir said Ms. Hasina could return only through extradition, effectively “in handcuffs”. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed reiterated the government’s position on Wednesday (November 25), saying “a convicted fugitive” could return only through the extradition process.

Dismissing the shifting deadlines — initially November, then December, and now December 16 — Mr. Ahmed said the government felt “no worry or pressure” and that law enforcement agencies remained on constant alert. He warned that the Awami League would face strict legal action if it resorted to militancy, arson or attacks on people and property.

articles.title: U.S. Army declares success in detonation of lead-based explosives stockpile in Iowa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Army and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said emission monitors detected zero levels of airborne lead in the surrounding region immediately after the explosion

The U.S. Army conducted a controlled detonation of an ageing stockpile of lead-based explosives in rural Iowa on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), declaring the ‌operation a success at safely destroying the unstable material while minimising toxic fallout.

Residents of the Iowa farm town of Middletown closest to ​the adjacent munitions depot were evacuated ahead of time as a precaution, while others hunkered down inside their homes to avoid exposure to ⁠lead dust emitted from the blast.

The Army and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said emission monitors detected zero levels of airborne lead in the surrounding region immediately after the explosion. Still, residents were told to remain indoors until officials gave the all-clear, and some expressed doubts about official reassurances.

The detonation followed days of public rancour and legal wrangling over the controversial disposal ‌plan, which authorities said was far safer than waiting for the deteriorating chemical drums to eventually blow up on their own.
Environmental Protection Agency Supervisor Susan Fisher collects soil samples in Augusta, Iowa, on November 25, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP

Shortly after 9 a.m. CST (1500 GMT), the Federal Emergency Management Agency posted a message on its X account confirming the detonation had been carried out and urging ‌nearby residents to remain indoors for the time being.

“Following this morning’s controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa, residents within 20 miles who have not evacuated should continue ‌to ⁠shelter in place and follow EPA safety guidance until given the all clear by officials. FEMA has provided safe lodging to those who ⁠evacuated,” the agency wrote.

A short time later, Army Secretary Aaron Telle declared that the “controlled, mitigated detonation”, designed to dispose of nearly 5 tonnes (4,500 kg) of highly volatile lead azide stored in 68 degrading plastic barrels, had “exceeded all expectations and was a huge success”.
“The threat of a spontaneous detonation has been eliminated,” he said on X.

In a videotaped public service message posted online afterward, Army Colonel Aaron ​Teller, a munitions specialist who oversaw the operation, said the demolition and ‌the array of safety measures to muffle the blast and emissions worked.
“All of the lead azide barrels were definitively removed,” Mr. Teller said, adding there were no secondary explosions.

“There was no kickout. There was no infrastructure damage in or around our installation,” Mr. Teller said. “We reduced as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa.”

articles.title: Cyril Ramaphosa wins court bid to overturn impeachment report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The 74-year-old leader was accused of hiding from police and tax authorities a 2020 break-in and theft of $580,000, which was stashed in furniture at his luxury Phala Phala farmhouse in the northern Limpopo province

A South African court ruled on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) in favour of President Cyril Ramaphosa , overturning a 2022 report that found he may have a case to answer over the theft of large sums of foreign currency from his private farm.

The 74-year-old leader was accused of hiding from police and tax authorities a 2020 break-in and theft of $580,000, which was stashed in furniture at his luxury Phala Phala farmhouse in the northern Limpopo province.

An independent parliamentary panel found that Mr. Ramaphosa may have committed serious misconduct, but he survived a National Assembly vote that could have triggered proceedings to remove him from office.
He challenged the panel’s report after the Constitutional Court ruled that parliament had violated the constitution by blocking efforts to impeach him.

On Wednesday (November 25, 2026), the high court said the report could not stand, ruling that the panel “went beyond its lawful remit, asked itself wrong questions, and made several material errors of law”.
“Any steps taken by the National Assembly pursuant to the report are reviewed, declared unlawful and set aside,” judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana ruled.

The complaint against Mr. Ramaphosa was laid by a former spy boss and one-time ally of Mr. Ramaphosa’s predecessor, Jacob Zuma, who claimed Mr. Ramaphosa hid a robbery of $4 million from police and tax authorities.

Mr. Ramaphosa, a former anti-apartheid activist who became a businessman before entering politics, denied any wrongdoing, saying he reported the break-in to the police and that the money came from the sale of 20 buffaloes.
The scandal nearly cost him the leadership of the African National Congress (ANC) in late 2022, but a motion against him was defeated in parliament, where the party held a majority.
In May, the Constitutional Court ordered that the panel’s report be referred to an impeachment committee, in response to a complaint lodged by several parties.

articles.title: Apple to open first store in Hyderabad on December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Apple Kukatpally opens Thursday, December 10 at 5 PM, the iPhone-maker announced
Apple is gearing up to open its first store, Apple Kukatpally, located at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall in Hyderabad, on December 10.
The new store is Apple’s seventh in the country, as the premium gadget-maker grows its retail presence in India by targeting its largest cities.
Customers will be able to experience and buy Apple products, apart from accessing services and support directly, the company highlighted.
Hyderabad houses Apple’s Research and Development and Retail Customer Care teams.
The design language for Apple Kukatpally takes inspiration from pearls, in a nod to Hyderabad’s identity and historical legacy as the ‘City of Pearls.’

The iPhone-maker’s other retail locations in India include Apple BKC and Apple Borivali in Mumbai, Apple Saket and Apple Noida in Delhi NCR, Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru, and Apple Koregaon Park in Pune.

“Ahead of opening day, customers are invited to download exclusive Apple Kukatpally wallpapers and stickers, explore a curated Apple Music playlist inspired by the sounds of Hyderabad, and learn more about the upcoming store at apple.com/in/retail/kukatpally,” announced Apple in a press release.

articles.title: Vivo launches X500 Pro Max, X500 and X500 along with Watch GT2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Chinese smartphone maker also launched its first smartwatch, Vivo Watch GT2, in India having a 2.07 inch display, with up to 25-day claimed battery life

Vivo on Thursday (November 26, 2026) launched new smartphones under its super-premium X series , featuring Vivo X500 Pro Max, X500 Pro and X500. The camera-centric phones succeed the X300 series, and bring ZEISS-tuned lenses and OriginOS 7 out of the box.
The Chinese smartphone maker also launched its first smartwatch, Vivo Watch GT2, in India having a 2.07 inch display, with up to 25-day claimed battery life. The Vivo Watch GT2 costs ₹14,999.
Vivo X500 Pro Max has a 6.85 inch flat LTPO AMOLED display, with up to 144Hz refresh rate and 5,000 nits peak brightness.
Vivo X500 Pro Max ships with a 7,800 mAh battery supported by a 90W wired charger and a 40W wireless charging support. It is IP68 and IP69 rated for dust and water resistance.

Vivo X500 Pro Max runs on MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset with up to 12 GB RAM and 512 GB storage. It operates on OriginOS 7 based on Android 17 out of the box. The phone will get 7 years of OS and security patches.
The Vivo X500 Pro Max sports a 50 MP main camera, a 200 MP telephoto camera and a 50 MP ultrawide lens. It has a 50 MP front camera.
Vivo X500 Pro Max comes in Apex Orange and Eternal Black. It starts at ₹1,64,999 (12GB/256GB) and ₹1,79,999 (12GB/512GB). The sale begins December 3.
Vivo X500 Pro get a 6.36 inch flat LTPO AMOLED display, with up to 144Hz refresh rate and 5,000 nits peak brightness.
Vivo X500 Pro uses a 6,510 mAh battery with a 90W wired and 40W wireless charging support.
Vivo X500 Pro also features MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro with up to 12 GB RAM and 256 GB storage. It too operates on OriginOS 7.
Vivo X500 Pro sports a 50 MP main camera, a 64 MP telephoto lens and a 50 MP ultrawide camera. It also features a 50 MP selfie camera.
Vivo X500 Pro starts at ₹1,49,999 (12GB/256GB). It goes on sale starting December 3.

articles.title: Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing.
The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar

The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands.

Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on.
The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar

The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself which begins from a landscape that includes Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, the Caspian Sea and Tibet, before reaching the wintering grounds, the lagoons, islands and mudflats of the Gulf of Mannar. As temperatures drop in the Arctic and the food becomes scarce, it triggers the bird to move towards warmer regions. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite.

Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.”
Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.
File photo of little stints and kentish plovers | Photo Credit: PRINCE FREDERICK

For more than four decades, researchers have been monitoring shorebird populations in the Gulf of Mannar region. “The numbers have fallen by 60 percent across the monitored shorebird population . The mudflats are not merely places to pause, they are feeding stations where the birds replenish the energy needed for their onward journeys. When these habitats disappear, there is no easy alternative,” says Sivakumar.
