articles.title: India’s defence start-up boom is outrunning its talent pipeline
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Without targeted skilling, 40-45% of roles in the sector could remain unfilled by 2030, a gap that risks bottlenecking aircraft development, unmanned systems, naval projects and secure communications networks

2026 has proven to be the best year on record for India’s defence manufacturing sector, with the annual defence production reaching an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. Defence exports reached a record ₹38,424 crore in FY 2025-26, which is 62.66% higher than ₹23,622 crore the previous year, with Indian-made equipment now being exported to more than 80 countries.

Indigenous defence production has quadrupled, rising from ₹46,429 crore in FY 2014-15 to ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025. The government has set its sights on ₹3 lakh crore in annual defence production and ₹50,000 crore in exports by 2029, alongside achieving roughly 88% self-sufficiency in ammunition production. Moreover, the share of the private industry is also expanding rapidly. Its contribution increased to 24% of total output (around ₹42,000 crore) in FY 2025-26, up from 22% the previous year.

Behind the headline numbers lies a more contested story: whether India has a sufficiently trained workforce to sustain this growth, and whether the engineering colleges, and State-run startup schemes can actually support this development. Interviews with founders, a former Navy officer-turned-entrepreneur, a materials science executive and an academic administrator suggest the sector’s talent problem is not a shortage of engineers, it is a shortage of engineers who understand what happens when a prototype has to survive a battlefield.

India’s defence technology market alone, was valued at $7.6 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $19 billion by 2030 according to a private industry report by staffing firm Quess Corp. By 2030, technology-led systems are expected to make up almost half of India’s overall defence market, marking what the report calls a shift “from platform-driven development to advanced engineering and digital capability building”.

The same report flags a structural problem: specialised roles in radar engineering, RF engineering, avionics, propulsion, optical engineering, quantum communications, systems integration, test and validation, and certification currently account for less than 5% of the existing defence workforce. Without targeted skilling, the report warns, 40-45% of these roles could remain unfilled by 2030, a gap that risks bottlenecking aircraft development, unmanned systems, naval projects and secure communications networks.

articles.title: How IITs and IISc are redefining medical education in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A technical institute’s medical degree will only be distinct if its curriculum, admissions, and thesis requirements are deliberately built around that engineering core

In March 2026, IIT Kharagpur—the oldest Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) that has been training thousands of minds to design bridges, cars, and computer chips for the last 75 years did something unprecedented. It formally applied to the National Medical Commission (NMC) to offer a postgraduate medical degree, the Doctor of Medicine (MD).
(Sign up for THEdge, The Hindu’s weekly education newsletter.)

It was not an isolated move. In August 2026, an alumnus of IIT-Kanpur pledged a massive ₹400 crore boost —building on a landmark ₹100 crore donation in 2022 — to expand its medical school and 450-bed super-specialty hospital to offer postgraduate programs in super-specialty medicine.
Within days, IIT-Madras stepped up to announce an even bolder vision: offering not just an MD, but an MBBS and a Ph.D. in medicine through its School of Medical Sciences, started in 2023.
A century-old assumption — that engineering colleges build engineers and medical colleges make doctors — is falling apart.

articles.title: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The latest proposal by the USTR takes the tariff framework on India back to what it was at the start of trade deal negotiations

The new 25% tariffs proposed by the U.S. on India do not pose a substantial risk to Indian exports, and India should go ahead with a trade deal only if it is balanced and reciprocal, according to exporters and trade and tariff experts.

An analysis of India’s trade relationship with the U.S. over the last two years showed that the latest tariffs announced by the U.S. have returned the tariff relationship to where it was at the start of trade deal negotiations.
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed a net tariff of 25% on goods imported from India, which could be reduced to 17% if a trade deal is signed by the two countries.

The proposed 25% tariff is nearly the same as the 26% tariff U.S. President Donald Trump had originally proposed in his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariff measure in April 2025. A week later, Mr. Trump paused these tariffs in a bid to secure trade deals with other countries.

In July 2025, he announced a 25% tariff on India, the same as what the USTR is now proposing. But Mr. Trump soon announced an additional 25% tariff as a penalty for India’s Russian oil imports taking the total tariff on Indian goods to 50%.

During that time, Mr. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on the import of steel and aluminium from all countries. The latest tariffs by the USTR are not in addition to those tariffs, meaning Indian steel and aluminium will continue to attract a 50% duty.

In February 2026, India and the U.S. issued a joint statement announcing the framework for an interim deal on trade, under which the U.S. would reduce its tariffs on Indian goods to 18%. This is very close to the 17% the U.S. is proposing now, should a deal be signed, nearly 10 months after the joint statement was issued.
As such, the pre-deal, post-deal, and steel and aluminium tariffs by the U.S. on India largely remain where they were at the start of negotiations.
Exporters and trade experts have said that India should proceed with a trade deal only if it satisfies Indian interests.

“FIEO supports the government’s efforts to conclude the Bilateral Trade Agreement at an early date,” said S.C. Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations. “The agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level-playing field with suppliers from other countries in the U.S. market.”

The president of the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Anil Gupta, pointed out that the tariffs will have a limited impact on Indian exports due to the nature of the commodities that India predominantly exports to the U.S.

“India’s top exports to the U.S. include electronic goods, drugs and pharmaceuticals, gems and jewellery, and textiles and apparel,” Mr. Gupta said. “As these products account for more than 50% of Indian exports to the U.S. and are price-sticky, there will be limited impact in the short to medium term.”

articles.title: Vellappally Natesan says he has ‘no differences’ with Keralam CM Satheesan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Natesan and Satheesan before UDF came to power following Assembly election earlier this year

Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan on Thursday said he had “no differences” with Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, signalling a softening of his stand towards the Congress leader after a series of public exchanges between them.
The SNDP Yogam represents the numerically strong Ezhava community in Keralam.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Natesan said there had been no differences between him and Mr. Satheesan. “There are no differences with me in the first place. So, why should we talk about reconciliation,” he asked.
The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Mr. Natesan and Mr. Satheesan before the UDF came to power following the Assembly election earlier this year.
Asked about his past criticism of Mr. Satheesan, Mr. Natesan said there was no difference in his assessment of the Congress leader “then and now.”
“I have only expressed my views on specific issues,” he said.
Mr. Natesan said he had criticised Mr. Satheesan for “an immature stand” and for not respecting the Opposition when the latter was the Leader of the Opposition during the previous government.
When asked whether Mr. Satheesan has matured since becoming the Chief Minister, he said: “It is only six months. Let’s wait and see.”

Mr. Natesan said it was Nair Service Society (NSS) general secretary G. Sukumaran Nair who had earlier announced that Mr. Satheesan would not be allowed into the organisation’s office, adding that he had never objected to the Chief Minister visiting the SNDP premises.
“I have never objected to anyone coming here. It was the NSS leadership that announced such a restriction,” he said.

Mr. Satheesan is scheduled to inaugurate the Mannam Jayanthi celebrations at the NSS headquarters in Perunna, Kottayam, on January 2, 2027, marking the 150th birth anniversary of the organisation’s founder, Mannathu Padmanabhan.
Asked about the differences between Mr. Nair and Mr. Satheesan and reports that they had since been resolved, Mr. Natesan said it was “their own matter.”

articles.title: Plea seeks guidelines to govern protests; Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, CJP leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Supreme Court to examine plea for uniform protest guidelines; Centre, CJP leaders issued notice as demands SOPs to regulate demonstrations

The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) agreed to examine a plea by a lawyers’ body seeking directions for formulation of uniform guidelines and a standard operating procedure governing public demonstrations and protests.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke , Saurav Das , Ashutosh Ranka and others.
Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani appeared for the lawyers’ body.

The Supreme Court was hearing a plea by Lawyers Voice seeking directions for framing comprehensive, uniform and effective guidelines defining the responsibilities of organisers and participants at public protests.
The petition argued that while dissent is part of democracy, protests must stay within legal bounds and avoid paralysing the capital or disrupting lawyers’ livelihoods.

“Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction directing the respondents to review, modify, formulate and implement a standard operating procedure [SOP] for dealing with public protests conducted in violation of applicable law, lawful restrictions or valid directions of the competent authorities, ensuring timely, coordinated action to ensure normal public life,” the plea said.
The petition referred to the protests organised by CJP during July and October, 2026.

Referring to media reports, the petition said the Delhi Police, by way of a “one-time exemption”, permitted the CJP to hold a Dharna at Jantar Mantar on June 6, 2026, strictly between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. on the strength of the undertaking furnished by its organisers.

Permission was sought and granted for a single day on June 20, 2026 again, confined to the hours between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m., but the demonstration was not discontinued at the expiry of the permitted hours, it said.

“No extension was ever granted, and that the organisers unilaterally announced an indefinite sit-in in the absence of any permission. The sit-in is reported to have continued until July 25, 2026, a period of about thirty-five days, during which a march towards Parliament was also undertaken on July 20, 2026 without the permission of the authorities,” the plea said.

The plea further said a letter was received on October 7 from Mr. Das seeking permission for a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, with the organisers indicating that thousands of persons were expected to participate.

“The Delhi Police is reported to have refused permission on October 9 on the ground that the intimation had been furnished merely three days before the proposed event, as against the 10 days prescribed.

articles.title: Constitution Day LIVE updates: U.P. taught BJP a lesson in 2024 LS polls, silenced Modi’s ‘400 paar’ slogan: Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: PM Modi said the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide in realising the resolve of a developed India

Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan called for respecting all languages and cautioned against looking down upon other people’s mother tongues, saying that respect for one’s own language must go hand in hand with respect for the languages of others.

“If I don’t respect the sentiments of others, then I don’t deserve that my sentiments will be respected by others,” Mr. Radhakrishnan said, stressing that linguistic diversity should be a source of mutual respect and national unity.

Addressing an event organised by the Union Law Ministry to mark the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution, he released its updated versions in all 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule.

Describing the initiative as a celebration of India’s linguistic diversity and democratic inclusiveness, the Vice-President said making the Constitution available in different languages would bring governance closer to the people and enable citizens to understand the country’s foundational document in their mother tongues.

“Our Constitution is our pride and our duty,” he said, adding that the availability of the document in multiple languages reflected the spirit of Jan Bhagidari and the collective responsibility of citizens in upholding constitutional values.
He also cautioned against equating knowledge with proficiency in English, saying it was just another language like any Indian mother tongue.
“Never think that speaking in English is knowledge. English is also one of the languages like our mother tongue. It’s nothing more,” he said.
“If our nation is not protected, none of our languages will be protected,” he said, urging citizens to work with the spirit of ‘Rashtra Pratham’ (Nation First). — PTI

articles.title: 10 years and doubled cost: The four-laning saga of Mangaluru-Bengaluru NH 75 in Dakshina Kannada and Hassan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The key highway connecting the state capital with coastal Karnataka becomes completely four-lane except the 26 km stretch of Shiradi Ghat between Maranahalli and Addahole

In the decadal saga of widening about 115 km stretch of Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75 between Hassan and B.C. Road in Dakshina Kannada district (excluding the 26-km Shiradi Ghat stretch), the total project cost has close to doubled, from about ₹1,220 crore estimated in the year 2017 to about ₹2,220 crore when the project was almost complete by 2026-end.

While the travel time (by a car) has reduced to about three-four hours between Hassan and Mangaluru from about five hours, road users endured tremendous ordeal during the past decade when the construction was underway, with the project witnessing an almost complete halt between 2018 and 2021 . Driving from Mangaluru to Hassan had become a nightmarish experience during this period.

While the Union Road Transport Ministry handed over the highway stretch to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in July 2016 to widen the stretch into a four-lane road, contracts were awarded to M/s Isolux Corson for the Hassan-Maranahalli stretch (about 50 km) at an estimated cost of ₹400 crore and M/s Larsen and Tubro for the Addahole-B C Road stretch (about 65 km) for ₹821 crore in 2017.

Within about 20 months, M/s Isolux declared insolvency and left the Hassan project while M/s Larsen submitted a letter of foreclosure as the NHAI wanted to change the scope of the project and refused to revise the project cost by about ₹140 crore for the changed scope. The Authority spent a good about two years in choosing new contractors for the Dakshina Kannada stretch and arranging the sub-contractor M/s Rajkamal Builders, to continue the Hassan district work.

The abnormally slow pace of construction, notwithstanding Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari’s claim of constructing about 40 km highway in a day, irritated road users as well as general public in the vicinity of the project highway.

With the contractors seldom following proper construction methods, including providing motorable alternative roads during the construction period, road users struggled to negotiate pothole and crater-ridden highway for years. While clouds of dust engulfed the highway during summer, the stretch was riddled with slush during the rainy season for years. Kalladka Town near B.C. Road where the NHAI built a 3 km elevated road (flyover) due to public demand, suffered massively for almost five years during the construction period.

While the project highway is almost complete except for about 1 km at two places in Dakshina Kannada district, the NHAI needs to take measures to ensure pedestrian safety at many places, including Mani, Uppinangady, Melkar, and other places as the vehicles move at high speed on the newly built wide carriageways.

Road users are also upset at the speed being limited to 80 kmph on the widened section with one user quipping, “Earlier, it was impossible to drive; now we cannot drive.” However, NHAI has justified the restrictions saying the carriageways are designed for those particular limits.

articles.title: AIADMK announces protests across Tamil Nadu against TVK government on December 2
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Referring to alleged irregularities in governance and corruption, party general secretary Edappadi Palaniswami said the administration was more concerned about retaining power than addressing people’s problems.

AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Thursday (November 26, 2026) announced State-wide protests by his party on December 2, accusing the TVK government of failing to fulfil its electoral promises and allowing law and order to deteriorate in Tamil Nadu and to highlight other issues.

Mr. Palaniswami criticised the TVK government over the safety of women, rising prices of various commodities, alleged deterioration of law and order situation, alleged “silence” over the Mekedatu issue.
Palaniswami continues tirade against TVK regime on investment, law and order, crime
Palaniswami attacks TVK government over law and order, Cauvery issue

In a statement, Mr. Palaniswami said the government had completed six months in office but had pushed the State backwards on several fronts. He alleged that incidents of murder, robbery, drug trafficking, sexual violence and custodial deaths had become frequent, while the government had failed to take effective action.

The former Chief Minister also accused the government of failing to ensure women’s safety, curb the drug menace and protect public property. Referring to alleged irregularities in governance and corruption, Mr. Palaniswami said the administration was more concerned about retaining power than addressing people’s problems.

In a separate development, AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran criticised the TVK government’s move to shift paddy procurement from the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to cooperative societies, alleging that the decision was anti-farmer.

In a social media post, he alleged the government was seeking to borrow from the National Cooperative Development Corporation through cooperative societies to circumvent its rising direct debt burden. He urged the government to retain the existing TNCSC procurement system and take measures to reduce its debt burden.
Tamil Nadu / All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / protest

articles.title: Massive fire at Bangkok oil refinery leaves several injured, Bangchak Corp shuts all units
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Flames rose high above the site, followed by black smoke that swept across the Thai capital’s skyline

A major fire broke out at Thailand’s Bangchak Corp’s Phra Khanong oil refinery in the capital, Bangkok, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), leaving at least seven people injured, four of those seriously, according to the city’s Erawan Emergency Medical Centre.

The company said it has ‌shut down all production ​units following the ‌fire, and later released a statement saying that the fire at its Bangkok oil refinery was “under control”. The company added that the cause of the incident was being investigated

A fire broke out at ‌the facility around ‌2.45 ⁠p.m. (local time) and was ⁠brought under control and extinguished around 30 minutes later, the ​company ‌said in a statement. The refinery has a maximum ​capacity of 1,20,000 barrels per day.
Thai energy conglomerate Bangchak operates two refineries, ⁠including the Phra Khanong facility, with ⁠a combined refining capacity of about 3,00,000 ‌barrels per day.
AFP reporters a few kilometres away said the blast shook their doors. Flames rose high above the site, followed by black smoke that swept across the Thai capital’s skyline.

articles.title: IREF say non-basmati rice export bans are unlikely, but urges exporters to remain cautious
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The government is unlikely to impose restrictions on non-basmati rice exports over the next month, the Indian Rice Exporters’ Federation (IREF) said on its portal on Wednesday (November 26, 2026).
It, however, urged rice exporters to continue business with appropriate contractual and inventory safeguards.

The Federation claimed that based on information received from sources familiar with policy discussions, its current assessment was that while policy options remain under consideration, there is no indication of an immediate move to curb exports.
However, the possibility of export duties or other policy measures cannot be ruled out, particularly if domestic rice prices continue to rise.

India’s substantial rice stocks provide an important cushion for domestic supply. The Public Distribution System (PDS), through which eligible households receive subsidised or free foodgrains under their entitlements, also helps protect beneficiaries from fluctuations in open-market prices.
However, strong international demand continues to influence domestic market dynamics. Any further significant icrease in domestic prices can prompt a review of the export policy.

articles.title: Mercury in cosmetics: What does the Kerala case reveal about the health risks of skin-lightening creams? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: What does the recent case in Kerala reveal about mercury poisoning from cosmetics? How does exposure affect the kidneys, and what safeguards are in place to regulate unsafe products?

The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Kerala.

Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm

After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online

articles.title: Action sought against author during Hubballi protest over remarks on Basavanna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Members of people’s organisations stage protest condemning derogatory remarks about the 12th century social reformer and the Constitution

Members of various people’s organisations staged a protest in Hubballi on Thursday, condemning the derogatory remarks about 12th century social reformer Basavanna and statement concerning the Constitution.

The protest, organised by the Hubballi Janapara Sanghatanegala Okkoota, began with the garlanding of B.R. Ambedkar’s statue on the occasion of Constitution Day, followed by a display and reading of the Preamble to the Constitution.

The protesters later took out a procession from Ambedkar Circle to the Tahsildar’s office where they burnt author Ravi Hanj (Hanjmath), journalist and Vishwavani editor Vishweshwar Bhat and seer of Kanheri Mutt Adrushya Kadasiddeshwar Swami in effigy.

The protesters demanded legal action against Mr. Hanj for his remarks about Basavanna, Mr. Bhat for encouraging the publication of controversial material and Kanheri seer for reportedly saying that the Constitution contains ideas from the Manusmriti.

The protest was led by Basavananda Swami of Managundi, Basavananda Swami of Rudrakshi Mutt, Shivayogi Swami of Mullalli, activists Basavaraj Sulibhavi, Gurunath Ullikashi and Mahesh Pattar, who, addressing the protestors, demanded stringent punishment for the guilty.

They later submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister through the Hubballi Tahsildar in which they said that Mr. Hanj has in an interview and also, in his book Basava Mantapa claimed that Basavanna misappropriated King Bijjala’s treasury and that the social reformer was responsible for the king’s death.
The organisations disputed these claims and sought disclosure from the author of the historical and Vachana-based evidence supporting his claims.
The protesters demanded registration of a case against Mr. Hanj under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act.

They also sought restrictions upon his entry to Karnataka, an investigation of the involvement of others in the publication and the setting up of a special investigation team under the supervision of a retired High Court judge to examine the matter.

Among those present were Sadananda Danganavar, Mohan Limbikayi, Anwar Mudhol, Lingaraj Angadi, B.S. Soppin, Rajshekhar Menasinakai, Kumaranna Patil, G.B. Halyal, C.G. Patil, Annapurna Kubasad, Gangadhar Perur, V.B. Maganur, Shankargouda Satmar, Sanju Dummakkanal, Babajan Mudhol, Husseinpasha Talewad, Mallappa Tadasad, Shiddu Teji, Shivanand Buralabaddi, Gurusiddappa Shivashimpi, Shameem Mulla, Manjula Benagi, Peersab Nadaf, Ramesh Bhusle and B.A. Mudhol.
Several Basava-oriented and Dalit organisations participated in the protest to which the Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI and Aam Aadmi Party extended support.

articles.title: No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu government is taking appropriate legal action, says VCK leader

Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) founder Thol. Thirumavalavan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said there was no need for a CBI probe into the allegations that the Kallakurichi TVK MLA had sent inappropriate messages to a District Collector. He said the Tamil Nadu government was taking appropriate legal action.
He said the VCK had consistently maintained that strict action should be taken against the MLA if he had sent messages to the Collector in a manner that caused mental distress.

“We have now received confirmation that a District Collector has formally lodged a complaint. Following this, the government has acted swiftly, registered a case against the particular MLA and initiated an investigation . We do not see any need for the CBI to intervene at this stage,” he said.

Responding to questions about the alleged delay in taking action, with 116 days having elapsed since the incident, Mr. Thirumavalavan said it was important to distinguish between the date of the alleged incident and the date on which the formal complaint was lodged.

“The incident came to light through the media and social media. The information available to us is that the Collector lodged a formal complaint only recently . We also learnt through social media reports that, when the incident occurred, she had not submitted a written complaint but had sought that the MLA be called and warned,” he contended.

He was responding to allegations that the Collector had earlier brought the matter to the attention of the Chief Secretary, who had allegedly attempted to persuade her to seek a transfer to another district. Opposition parties have cited the alleged delay and the handling of the complaint as reasons for seeking a CBI probe.

“Now that she has come forward and lodged a complaint, I believe the government is acting swiftly. A case has been registered under the appropriate sections, and I am confident that legal action will follow,” Mr. Thirumavalavan said.
Tamil Nadu / Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam

articles.title: Railways put in place extensive arrangements for Sabarimala pilgrimage; 204 train services notified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Southern Railway has put in place extensive arrangements to ensure safe, comfortable and hassle-free travel for pilgrims during the Mandala–Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026–27. Since the season commenced on November 16, 2026, a series of measures has been implemented across railway stations, especially the major stations that serve as transit points for devotees travelling to Sabarimala.

Southern Railway has put in place extensive arrangements to meet the increased passenger demand during the Mandala–Makaravilakku pilgrimage season 2026–27 in coordination with other railway zones, by introducing a record number of special train services, to facilitate the travel of Sabarimala-bound pilgrims from different parts of the country.

As on November 23, a total of 204 trips of Sabarimala special trains have been notified, covering inter-zonal and intra-zonal services with the majority of services operating between Chennai – Kollam, Thiruvananthapuram–Mangaluru, Panvel–Kottayam, Visakhapatnam–Kollam, Hyderabad–Kollam and Vijayawada–Kottayam. Further services will be planned based on passenger demand and reservation trends, said the railways in a statement here on Wednesday.

Kottayam, Chengannur, Ernakulam Junction and Ernakulam Town are the key transit stations for Sabarimala pilgrims, where special arrangements have been made for accommodation, rest, catering, sanitation and onward transportation. A three-storeyed pilgrim facilitation centre near the main entrance of Kottayam station is fully operational and can accommodate up to 900 pilgrims at a time.

In Chengannur, three spacious pilgrim shelters can accommodate up to 600 passengers. Since Ernakulam Junction is an important transit point for pilgrims from different parts of the country, AC waiting halls, catering facilities and cloakroom services are available although station redevelopment works are underway. Temporary prefabricated pay-and-use toilets have also been provided at the station for the benefit of Sabarimala pilgrims.

Pilgrim assistance booths, manned by Railway Protection Force (RPF) personnel, function round the clock at Chengannur and Kottayam to guide and assist devotees. Additional unreserved ticket counters and reservation facilities have been opened at Chengannur and Kottayam, also functioning round the clock, to handle the heavy demand for tickets.

Southern Railway is working closely with the State Revenue department, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC), Travancore Devaswom Board, Police and Medical departments for the smooth movement and welfare of pilgrims. Security has also been strengthened at important stations and on trains to ensure the safety of pilgrims throughout their journey.

Railway officials from various departments are closely monitoring special train operations, passenger amenities, station management and crowd movement throughout the season. A dedicated task force will be deployed on Makaravilakku Day at Chengannur, Ernakulam Junction and Kottayam stations to coordinate passenger movement, monitor special train operations and ensure the smooth functioning of the additional booking counters and other facilities.

articles.title: Expired food, mouldy sugarcane seized during surprise inspections in Kozhikode
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inspections found several violations of food safety and sanitation norms, including the storage of perishable ingredients in unhygienic freezers and poorly maintained kitchens

The health squad of the Kozhikode Corporation seized expired food products and mould-infested sugarcane during surprise inspections at hotels and eateries across the city on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

The inspections, which began at 6 a.m., found several violations of food safety and sanitation norms, including storage of perishable ingredients in unhygienic freezers and poorly maintained kitchens. Some establishments were also found discharging untreated wastewater into public drains without proper waste management facilities.

Expired chicken, beef, spices, and other stale food items kept for sale were seized from two hotels near Mananchira and Kozhikode South beach. The squad also confiscated mouldy sugarcane stalks stored for preparing juice from an outlet at South beach.

Officials who were part of the searches said show-cause notices were issued to two hotels that were found with unhygienic kitchens and discharging wastewater into the public drainage system. The Corporation authorities said legal proceedings were initiated against the establishments. They added that inspections would be intensified in the coming days.
The enforcement team comprised Corporation health officer (in-charge) K. Dileep Kumar, senior public health inspector K. Rishad, and public health inspectors K. Rajesh, Vishnu Prasad, and Sonia.

articles.title: Tiruvannamalai railway station nets over ₹60 lakh revenue during Karthigai Deepam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tiruchi Railway Division had made comprehensive arrangements for issue of tickets, crowd management, and had operated 24 special trains to the temple town to clear the extra rush

Amid a massive turnout of devotees for the Karthigai Deepam festival, the Tiruvannamalai railway station falling under the Tiruchi Railway Division’s jurisdiction netted over ₹60 lakh as originating revenue through sale of unreserved and reserved tickets from November 23 to 25 when special trains were operated to clear the extra rush.

Anticipating a large turnout of devotees for the annual festival, the Tiruchi Railway Division had put in place special measures at Tiruvannamalai station for ticketing facilities, crowd management, and ensuring safety of travellers. Tiruvannamalai is a block station on the Villupuram-Katpadi broad gauge section and classified under the NSG-4 category.

As for ticketing facilities, additional counters were opened in the booking office at Tiruvannamalai station besides two special counters for the festival at the Chief Booking Supervisor office. Besides these, three additional Automatic Ticket Vending Machines were installed to cater to the ticketing demand. In addition to the existing commercial staff, extra staff were deployed for the booking counters and at the enquiry booth/ help desk at the station.

Railway sources said the originating revenue of the Tiruvannamalai station on November 23, 24 and 25 was over ₹60 lakh through sale of tickets. The originating revenue peaked on November 24 when the Mahadeepam’ was lit atop the Arunachala hill at Tiruvannamalai on the Karthigai Deepam festival day. It was over ₹29.5 lakh on that day, said the sources. A day after the Mahadeepam on November 25, the originating revenue of the station exceeded ₹27 lakh. The originating revenue on November 23 was more than ₹5.29 lakh.

The sources said the total footfall at Tiruvannamalai station on November 23, 24 and 25 exceeded 85,000. The footfall at the station on the day when the Mahadeepam was lit on November 24 was more than 44,000. A team of railway officers, led by the Divisional Railway Manager, Tiruchi, camped in Tiruvannamalai from November 23 to 25 to monitor the arrangements and crowd management.

A round-the-clock help desk was set up by the Railway Protection Force at Tiruvannamalai station where a war room equipped with CCTV camera surveillance for constant monitoring of crowd movements was established. Over 90 Railway Protection Force personnel of Tiruchi Division were deployed at the station.

As Tiruvannamalai station falls on the Villupuram -Katpadi broad gauge section, train escorts were provided at both ends. Close coordination was maintained with the Government Railway Police and the local police for crowd regulation from the railway station to the temple and back.

Sources said 24 special trains were operated exclusively for the festival from November 23 to 25, including from Tiruchi to Vellore Cantonment, Villupuram to Vellore, and from Tiruvannamalai to Villupuram. Over 600 unreserved coaches were deployed to cater to the needs of the passengers.

articles.title: Serbia sets Presidential election for December 27 after students won Parliamentary vote
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25

Serbia 's Parliament speaker on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set an early Presidential election for December 27, after former President Aleksandar Vucic resigned in September to pursue what turned out to be a failed bid to become Prime Minister.
The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25.

Mr. Vucic and his party had ruled virtually unchallenged for 14 years. He had run for Prime Minister after serving two near-complete five-year terms as President, and was banned by law from seeking a third term.
“I hope we will have a tough choice between top candidates and their programmes," Speaker Aleksandar Cupic said. “Building democratic institutions is the task for all of us.”
It was not immediately clear who the Presidential candidates will be. Mr. Vucic has suggested that his SNS party could sit out the election.

The Presidency in Serbia is largely ceremonial. The President commands the Army and has a say in foreign policy but has no executive powers. While he was in office, however, Mr. Vucic concentrated power in the Presidency, facing accusations of authoritarian rule. Mr. Vucic regularly announced important state decisions and policies and even presided over government sessions.

Since losing power, Mr. Vucic has accused the election winners of imposing a “revolutionary terror,” although his government is still technically in control until a new one is formed. The change in power has led to a surge in detentions of officials and police officers suspected of abusing their positions during Mr. Vucic's rule.

The youth-led movement had led two years of street protests that started in response to a train station canopy collapse in northern Serbia that killed 16 people. Many blamed the tragedy on alleged rampant corruption and negligence during the building renovation in Novi Sad.

articles.title: U.K. net migration falls to lowest since 1997; Indians largest foreign group entering and leaving the country
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed

Net migration to the U.K. has fallen to 77,000, its lowest levels since 1997, excluding the pandemic, as per official U.K. government figures released on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group immigrating and emigrating longterm to and from the U.K.

The net migration figure, which represents the number of people arriving in the U.K. minus those emigrating, fell dramatically from 2,04,000 for the year ending June 2025 and from a record high of 9,00,000 in the year ending June 2023. The news is likely to a shot in the arm for the governing Labour Party, as migration has become a political lighting-rod in recent years.

The latest drop in numbers was predominantly due to a fall in non-EU migration to the U.K. This figure fell by more then 1,00,000 while emigration remained mostly stable. Non-EU+ nationals arriving in the U.K. fell by 17% to 7,38,000. Just under half came to study, a quarter for work, and 13% for asylum.

Of those migrating to the U.K., the largest group consisted of Indians , then Chinese, then Nigerians, Pakistanis and Americans. Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed.
More EU+ and British nationals left the U.K. than non-EU+ nationals. Some 2,45,00 Britons left the country longterm in the year ending June 2026, with net migration of Britons at -1,37,000.

These record high net migration numbers in 2023 — called the ‘Boriswave’, occurred during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative, following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, when visa rules were eased to fill certain occupations such as social care. Migration from non-EU countries consequently increased at this time. Mr. Johnson’s successors, Rishi Sunak, a fellow Conservative, and then Prime Minister Keir Starmer of the Labour Party, further tightened immigration policies resulting in falling numbers.

The latest drop in numbers was predominantly due to a fall in non-EU migration to the U.K. This figure fell by more then 1,00,000 while emigration remained mostly stable. Non-EU+ nationals arriving in the U.K. fell by 17% to 7,38,000. Just under half came to study, a quarter for work, and 13% for asylum.

Of those migrating to the U.K., the largest group consisted of Indians , then Chinese, then Nigerians, Pakistanis and Americans. Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed.

More EU+ and British nationals left the U.K. than non-EU+ nationals. Some 2,45,00 Britons left the country longterm in the year ending June 2026, with net migration of Britons at -1,37,000.

These record high net migration numbers in 2023 — called the ‘Boriswave’, occurred during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative, following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, when visa rules were eased to fill certain occupations such as social care. Migration from non-EU countries consequently increased at this time. articles.title: Situation in India-China border areas remains ‘generally stable’, says China
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh

The situation in the India-China border areas remain “generally stable”, China’s Defence Ministry spokesperson and PLA Senior Colonel Chen Xi said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) adding that China “does not recognize the so-called Arunachal Pradesh illegally set up by India.”

“China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels, including general-level talks, to jointly implement the consensus reached by the two sides and safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas”, he said in response to a question at a press briefing on recent tensions in the Eastern sector of the border, Chinese state media reported.

On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.

Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between. The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector. Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

articles.title: Indian pharma company Hetero begins supply of generic twice-yearly HIV prevention injection in Africa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir as an additional HIV prevention option, based on clinical evidence showing high efficacy in preventing HIV infection

Hyderabad-based pharmaceutical company Hetero has begun phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir, a long-acting drug for HIV prevention, to three African countries. The company plans to supply 300,000 vials initially to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.
Lenacapavir is used as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Unlike daily oral PrEP medicines, the injectable formulation is administered once every six months.

Hetero is launching the generic drug under the brand names Lexapir and Capvic. The company expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027. These tablets form part of the PrEP regimen and will be supplied by the original manufacturer, Gilead Sciences, in the interim.

The launch follows Gilead’s non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers, allowing them to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 eligible countries. The licensing arrangement is intended to expand access to the drug in low- and middle-income countries.

Hetero said its generic injectable formulation and oral initiation tablets had received an Expert Review Panel recommendation, allowing eligible procurement through applicable Global Fund channels while regulatory approval or WHO prequalification processes continue. In Zimbabwe, procurement is being supported through the United Nations Development Programme using Global Fund financing.

The company plans to supply the drug to 10 additional African countries in early 2027 and expand availability across other countries covered by its licence, subject to national regulatory approvals and procurement arrangements. It also plans to introduce generic lenacapavir in India in the coming months, subject to regulatory clearance.

articles.title: BITS Pilani-Hyderabad researchers develop affordable way to grow microalgae
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Researchers at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, have secured an Indian patent for a low-cost nutrient medium that could make large-scale cultivation of microalgae more affordable, opening possibilities for applications in renewable fuels, carbon capture and biotechnology.

The patented innovation, titled “Nutrient Medium Composition for Mass Cultivation of Microalgae” (Patent No. 603126), has been developed by Sandip S. Deshmukh of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, K. Pranav Narayan of the Department of Biological Sciences and research scholar Sama Sanghamitra, as per a press release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026).

Microalgae are microscopic organisms that use sunlight and carbon dioxide to produce biomass. They are considered a promising resource for wastewater treatment, carbon dioxide capture, biofertilisers, food and nutraceutical products, and the production of biodiesel and other bio-based fuels. However, the high cost of cultivation has limited their large-scale adoption.

The BITS team developed an alternative nutrient formulation using locally available agricultural-grade fertilisers instead of expensive laboratory-grade chemicals. The formulation supplies key nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur required for microalgal growth while reducing the complexity and cost of preparing the cultivation medium.

The macronutrients needed to prepare 100 litres of the new medium cost about ₹2.40, compared with around ₹43 for the conventional Bold’s Basal Medium (BBM). The cost is estimated to be around ₹4.50 per 100 litres, making it significantly cheaper than conventional alternatives.

The formulation is also easy to prepare and can be supplied as a dry powder, which can be dissolved in water before use. The technology was tested in laboratory, non-sterile and outdoor cultivation conditions. The microalgae was also successfully cultivated in a 10,000-litre open pond using natural sunlight and atmospheric carbon dioxide.

Researchers are now in discussions with a potential industry partner, which has proposed a two-month evaluation of the formulation for carbon capture and biomass production applications. They are also seeking collaborations with companies in biofuel, algal biotechnology and carbon management sectors to explore commercialisation of the technology.

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership.

Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

articles.title: Thousands participate at Maha Deepam festival in Tiruvannamalai temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A sea of devotees who occupied every available space around the Arunachaleswarar Temple brought back the festival spirit to the temple town of Tiruvannamalai on Tuesday as thousands chanted ‘Arunachaleshwara’ during the day-long puja that culminated in the lighting of the ‘Maha Deepam’ atop the Arunachala Hill.

The Karthigai Deepam festival began at the temple on November 15 with the hoisting of a flag and culminated with lighting of the ‘Maha Deepam’ at 6 p.m. on Tuesday. The day began with puja followed by lighting of the ‘Bharani Deepam’ at the temple at 4 a.m. It was attended by Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh and District Collector Vandhana Garg.
Later, Minister for Water Resources and Rural Development N. Anand, among other dignitaries visited the temple for Maha Deepam.
“Easy availability of bus services, especially for return journeys, remains a major challenge for women and senior citizens who visit the town for the festival,” said V. Devika, a devotee.

The flow of visitors was steady in the town since Tuesday morning with vehicles including government buses being stopped around two kms from the temple. Vehicles were allowed to park at designated parking lots that are away from the town. The parking space can accommodate over 21,000 cars.
Devotees, especially senior citizens and women, had more road space in the town as all vehicles including two-wheelers were not allowed to enter the town on Maha Deepam day to avoid congestion.

Long-distance visitors made use of 180 shuttle services operated by TNSTC from the temporary bus terminus to the 14-km Girivalam path and the Arunachaleswara Temple, around four kms away. Each commuter has to pay ₹10 per trip.
The Health Department monitored mobile health desks, mostly on the Girivalam path and bus terminuses, during the festival. Around 35 ambulances, including five bike ambulances, were also in use.
Adequate water taps (146 spots), washrooms (600 spots), 10,900 street lights were set up for the festival. A total of 2,466 sanitary staff with 344 bins were roped to keep the town clean.

To ensure the safety of visitors, 31 police watch towers were set up. They were supported by 350 bike patrols and 62 help desks in the town round the clock. Around 110 firefighters with 26 water tenders were deployed to prevent accidental fire, especially on the hillock, during Maha Deepam.

articles.title: Kerala High Court denies pre-arrest bail to former BLM Housing Society president
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The case diary clearly portrays the serious nature of the allegations and the premeditated criminal act on his part, says court

The Kerala High Court has denied pre-arrest bail to R. Premkumar, former president of Bharath Lajhna Multi State Housing Co-operative Society (BLM), in a case of alleged misappropriation of the Society funds.

Justice Kauser Edappagath found that the investigating agency had collected enough material to substantiate the allegations against Mr. Premkumar. It observed that the case diary clearly portrayed the serious nature of the allegations and the premeditated criminal act on his part. It stated that his custodial interrogation was necessary for the investigation, and that his detention was required to prevent possible witness tampering and interference with the investigation.

The court found that Mr. Premkumar had transferred ₹30 crore from BLM Society to himself, on verification of bank accounts. The investigation had revealed that the Society had purchased Ragam Theatre, Thrissur, for ₹65.42 crore out of which ₹19.95 crore was transferred to the accused’s account. The court noted that the theatre was then pledged with Brios Finvest India Ltd. for ₹50 crore, again transferred to Mr. Premkumar’s personal account.

The court noted that Vivin Luxury Suites, registered in the name of Mr. Premkumar’s wife, was bought with the Society’s funds as well. Further, 500 acres were also registered in her name in Kanchipuram. Mr. Premkumar’s family members had also availed themselves of a loan of ₹160 crore from the Society, the court found.

articles.title: HMDA to get treated waste water from Coca Cola to sustain greenery on the ORR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) has tied up with the Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB) for reuse of the treated water from the latter for sustaining greenery on the Outer Ring Road.

Under the initiative, the HCCB will supply up to 600 Kilo Litres (KL) of treated water per day from its Avinya facility, at Banda Thimmapur village of Siddipet district, which will be used to support plantations and green spaces along the identified ORR stretch in Medchal.
The water undergoes multi-stage treatment, stringent quality checks and continuous monitoring to ensure its suitability for non-potable applications, a press note from HMDA informed.
The treated water will be transported through tankers to a designated HMDA receiving points and utilised for irrigation of plantations and green spaces along the ORR, it said.

HMDA’s Director of Urban Forestry Rohith Gopidi informed that the ORR stretch has a total 98 water sumps, each with a capacity to hold 50,000 litres of water. When ORR was built, the sumps were filled by drawing ground water through bore wells.

“Most of these bore wells have gone dry now. With current EL Nino phenomenon, we decided to use grey water from industries lining the ORR for filling the sumps. It is also an opportunity for behavioural change with regard to water usage,” Mr.Gopidi said.

HCCB was sending the water to the Effluent Treatment Plant in Patancheru earlier for treatment. With the agreement with HMDA, it will divert the water to ORR sumps through its own tankers, he said. Starting with 2 lakh litres of water, the quantity will be scaled up to 6 lakh litres depending on the capacity of the treatment plant and HMDA’s needs.

An armed gang allegedly intercepted a car carrying a rowdy-sheeter and opened fire near Masti in Malur taluk of Kolar district on Tuesday (November 24). However, the bullet missed the intended target and hit his elder brother, who was driving the vehicle, leaving him injured.

articles.title: Samajwadi Party reveals 5 candidates for Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: SP president Akhilesh Yadav urged Congress to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for their alliance in most seats
The Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announced five candidates for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls.
The party named Ashu Malik as candidate for the Saharanpur assembly seat, Nahid Hasan for Kairana, Mahboob Ali for Amroha , Jyoti Lodhi for Lalitpur and Umar Ali Khan for the Behat assembly seat.

In a related development, SP president Akhilesh Yadav urged Congress to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for their alliance in most seats, describing the U.P. assembly election as a historic opportunity for secular parties to defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies and save the country from falling into the wrong hands and being ruined.

“This time is a historic opportunity when both of us secular parties can together defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies forever and save the country from falling into wrong hands and getting ruined. We want you and I to understand public expectations and realities and engage in serious discussions to ensure victory for our “alliance” in most seats. In all the seats we contest, our winning numbers should exceed the number of seats we fail to win. Only victory will make the division respectable, because winning seats brings respect,” he wrote on X.
Mr. Yadav asked Congress to mark all potential seats and send them to the SP.

“We will then discuss together which seat and which candidate is in a position to win. Based on our assessment and mathematical equation for victory, we may also inform the Congress about several winnable seats that they, for some reason, haven’t even considered,” he said.

“Our effort is that when big leaders meet, on all the seats, there should be discussion on the candidate of the ‘INDIA Alliance’ and not the candidate of Congress or the SP, and the thing which will give positive results would be that we present our candidate as the ‘PDA candidate’,” he added.

The SP chief claimed ground surveys have made it clear that the message has reached every city, neighborhood, street, and village that aggrieved and humiliated people from every community and every section of society across the state have rallied against the BJP, believing that the PDA will defeat the NDA and bring about change.

“The truth is, we don’t want seat sharing to be based on a “me-or-you” approach. We don’t want it to be a division, we want to call it ‘seat adjustment’. In seats with difficult equations, we will discuss at least two candidates together, choose the one with the most potential, and work together to ensure their victory. We don’t want alliance candidates to be imposed on each other, but rather, they should be decided by consensus,” he added.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) argued that the gold jewellery sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of livelihoods

While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.

articles.title: Court rejects PG operator’s bail in Satya Niketan building collapse case, says he put profits above students’ lives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,’ the court said

Observing that he appeared to have placed financial gains above the safety of students and labourers staying at the premises, a Delhi court on Monday refused to grant bail to Shubham Tyagi, one of operator of the paying guest (PG) accommodation in South Delhi’s Satya Niketan which collapsed in September this year leaving seven dead.

Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana of Patiala House Court denied bail to the accuse after rejecting Mr Tyagi’s argument that he had no responsibility for the construction of the PG which he has co-accused Sudhanshu Kumar had rented the property from its owners and operated a boy’s hostel.

It added that even if the construction was not being carried out under Mr Tyagi’s instructions, he was obligated to ensure that residents vacated the building until the work was completed. He was also expected to alert occupants about the potential structural danger.

“The accused persons, who are responsible for the loss of seven valuable lives, are not entitled to the benefit of discretion and such incidents must be dealt with by the courts of law with an iron hand,” court said.

Holding that Mr Tyagi could have anticipated the risks arising from alleged unauthorised construction and structural alterations court mentioned the statement of injured student Nitish Chhib, court said that it was alleged that basement construction had continued for 10-12 days despite complaints from students. The residents were allegedly threatened with eviction when they objected to the work.

Emphasising the gravity of the incident, the court observed that building collapses linked to illegal construction have repeatedly resulted in fatalities and must be treated seriously. It remarked that those allegedly responsible for the loss of seven lives did not deserve discretionary relief and that such incidents required a firm judicial response.
Denying bail, court also stated that the trial is at an early stage and public witnesses were yet to be examined and there was a possibility of witness intimidation.

The Delhi Police had filed a 638-page chargesheet in the matter earlier this month. It named building owner Hariram Gupta, his wife Urmila Gupta, their son Mahesh Gupta, labour contractor Sanoj Kumar and PG operators Mr Tyagi and Mr Kumar as accused.
