articles.title: Website selling ‘lifetime press cards’ for ₹1,799 raises concerns; Delhi Police, journalist bodies flag verification challenge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Indian Press Union offers paid identity cards to journalists, freelancers and social media content creators, promising approval within 24 hours; IFSO official says police encountered people carrying its cards, while press bodies question the organisation’s credentials and registration

A website selling ‘lifetime press identity cards’ for up to ₹1,799 has come under scrutiny, with media representatives questioning the credentials of the organisation issuing them and the implications of commercially selling identification associated with the journalistic profession. The issue has also raised concerns within the Delhi Police, who flagged individuals carrying cards issued by the platform during the anit-SIR protests in October but could not establish the organisation’s authority to issue them.

The website, Indian Press Union (IPU), offers digital membership for ₹999 and physical membership for ₹1,799. It promises applicants a “verified IPU ID Card” and a lifetime membership certificate after filling an online application with name, mobile number and email ID followed by Know Your Customer (KYC) verification using Aadhar Card. Applications, it claims, are typically reviewed and approved within 24 hours of verification.

According to Delhi Police’s IFSO Chief Sanjay Bhatia, there were instances during the protests when some people identified themselves as independent journalists but were later seen raising slogans and participating in the demonstrations. He said several of them were carrying fake press identity cards.

“Press cards were issued by a website called Indian Press Union, which was offering physical press cards for around ₹1,800 and digital cards for ₹1,000. We did not know whether it was a statutory body authorised to issue such identification cards. We asked journalists about it, and even they were unable to give us a clear answer. So, how were we supposed to establish which card was genuine?” the official said.

The concerns have assumed significance amid the ongoing debate over who qualifies as a journalist and who is a social media content creator or ‘reel-maker’. This follows the Delhi Police’s November 16 affidavit before the Supreme Court, in which it questioned whether social media content creators could claim the same protections as bona fide journalists.

Media representatives have cautioned that identity cards issued by private organisations cannot automatically be equated with government accreditation or proof of professional journalistic credentials. They have called for greater scrutiny of organisations claiming to represent journalists, particularly those charging individuals for membership and press identification.
R Srinivasan, senior journalist and member of the Editors Guild of India, said he had not heard of the Indian Press Union, despite the existence of several journalists’ unions and associations.

“This kind of website and the practice of issuing identity cards in this manner are a direct attack on the reputation of the profession. It is very concerning. Generally, press cards are issued either through the government’s accreditation system via the Press Information Bureau (PIB) or by media organisations to their employees,” he said.

Sangeeta Barooah Pisharoty, president of the Press Club of India (PCI), said the organisation was unfamiliar to the press body and that the sale of such cards was particularly worrying at a time when the distinction between journalists and digital content creators was already being debated.

“We have no clue who these people are. It is quite worrying because it is happening at a time when the Delhi Police are saying they cannot differentiate between a genuine journalist and YouTubers. When identity cards of this kind are being sold randomly, it should worry the entire journalist community,” she said.

Ms. Pisharoty said the issue needed wider consultation within the media fraternity, including scrutiny of the rules under which such organisations were registered and the authority they claimed to exercise.

Geeta Seshu, a Mumbai-based journalist and co-founder of the Free Speech Collective, which filed a contempt petition before the Supreme Court alleging police obstruction, harassment and unlawful detention of reporters, said journalists seeking membership of such organisations needed to examine their credentials thoroughly before associating with them.

articles.title: Maharashtra FDA cancels Inducare’s manufacturing licences again over nine unauthorised drugs, two found spurious
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Firm manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission; drugs worth ₹1.72 crore seized from YCM Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said it had cancelled the drug manufacturing licences of Pune-based Inducare Pharmaceutical and Research Foundation for the second time after the firm was found to have manufactured and sold nine drugs without mandatory product permission, all of which were subsequently declared substandard, misbranded or spurious by government analysts.

The cancellation order, issued on November 23 by the Joint Commissioner (Drugs), Pune Division, directed the firm to immediately cease all manufacturing, packing, testing and distribution activities. The FDA has also proposed prosecution against the firm under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

Of the nine drugs tested, two were declared spurious after government analysts found that the claimed active ingredients were absent. Ibucare Plus, a combination of ibuprofen and paracetamol, contained no ibuprofen, while Carevita-M, a multivitamin tablet, was found to contain none of the nine specified ingredients tested.

The remaining drugs failed various quality tests, with several containing significantly lower quantities of active ingredients than claimed on their labels. These included medicines used in the treatment of cardiovascular and digestive disorders.
The FDA said the firm, located in the Additional MIDC area of Jejuri in Pune district, had admitted in its written response that it had not obtained separate product permissions for the nine drugs.

The firm’s manufacturing licences had previously been cancelled on September 7 after a joint inspection conducted on July 14 and 15 revealed 25 serious deficiencies in Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).

The inspection revealed that approximately 13.86 lakh tablets of Caregyl-400 had been manufactured without mandatory batch manufacturing and packing records or test reports. Of these, 5.20 lakh tablets had already been distributed. Laboratory analysis revealed that the sampled batch contained only 32.44% of the claimed metronidazole content.

Several samples of substandard drugs were also collected from the Central Medical Store of Yashwantrao Chavan Memorial (YCM) Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad, following which stocks worth approximately ₹1.72 crore were seized on November 4.
Other irregularities included discrepancies in manufacturing and expiry dates, inadequate laboratory testing procedures, unhygienic manufacturing conditions and improper storage of finished products.
A show-cause notice was issued to the firm on October 29, following which it submitted a written response on November 3. A personal hearing was conducted on November 23.

The licensing authority rejected the firm’s contention that no patient complaints had been received, observing that the risk of treatment failure arising from spurious and substandard drugs existed even in the absence of complaints.

“Ensuring that citizens have access to safe, quality and efficacious drugs is the foremost responsibility of the Food and Drug Administration. Stringent regulatory and legal action will be taken against any manufacturer who plays with the health of the general public by manufacturing drugs without product permission,” FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said.

articles.title: Mumbai Police announce traffic curbs for VBA’s Samvidhan Samman Mahasabha at Shivaji Park
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The annual public rally, held ahead of Constitution Day on November 26, is being organised under the leadership of VBA national president Prakash Ambedkar

The Mumbai Traffic Police on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announced traffic restrictions in Dadar and adjoining areas from 9 a.m. to 11.50 p.m. on Wednesday (November 25) in view of the Samvidhan Samman Mahasabha organised by the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) at Shivaji Park.
The annual public rally, held ahead of Constitution Day on November 26, is being organised under the leadership of VBA national president Prakash Ambedkar.
With a large number of people expected to arrive from across Maharashtra, the police anticipate traffic congestion on the Western and Eastern Express Highways and roads leading to the venue.

According to the notification issued by Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Dipali Dhate, vehicular entry will be prohibited on Swatantryaveer Savarkar Marg between Siddhivinayak Temple junction and Kapad Bazar junction in Mahim. Motorists will be diverted through S.K. Bole Road, Agar Bazar, Portuguese Church and Gokhale Road.

Vehicular entry will also be prohibited between Raja Badhe Chowk and Keluskar Marg (North), on the southbound stretch of Lt. Dilip Gupte Marg from Pandurang Naik Marg junction, and between Gadkari Chowk and Keluskar Road (South).
Depending on traffic conditions, the police may also close stretches of Bal Govindas Marg and Dadasaheb Rege Marg.

Parking restrictions will be imposed on eight roads or road stretches, including Swatantryaveer Savarkar Marg, Keluskar Road (North and South), M.B. Raut Road, Pandurang Naik Marg, Dadasaheb Rege Marg, Lt. Dilip Gupte Marg, N.C. Kelkar Marg and L.J. Road.
Parking facilities have been designated at Kohinoor Square and Senapati Bapat Road in Dadar, Five Gardens in Matunga and R.A.K. Road in Wadala.

articles.title: U.S. CIA, ODNI suffer cybersecurity breach of some unclassified information, NYT reports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While it was not clear specifically what unclassified material ​was compromised, information ‌at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed in the breach

The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency ‌and the Office of the ​Director of National Intelligence recently ⁠discovered a cybersecurity breach that exposed some of their unclassified information, the New ‌York Times reported on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), citing people familiar with ‌the matter.
The intrusions affected a ‌network ⁠that looks for intelligence insights ⁠in public, unclassified material, the Times reported.
While it was not clear specifically what unclassified material ​was compromised, information ‌at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed in the breach, the Times added.
Asked ‌about the report, the ODNI ​said there had been “no disruptions to critical capabilities or ⁠classified systems.” The CIA did not immediately respond to a request for ‌comment.

The news is the latest publicly reported hack in a series of tech outages and cybersecurity incidents, including a breach reported at the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Two separate ‌breaches have recently been disclosed at ​the FBI, while the Pentagon and the Department of Homeland ⁠Security have also been caught up in ⁠recent cyber incidents.

articles.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, U.S. jury finds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds

A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud as it grew into one of the world's biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks.
However, jurors acquitted the company of the most serious charge it faced: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy to steal intellectual property from American companies.
The verdict followed a lengthy trial in which U.S. prosecutors argued that Huawei repeatedly stole technological secrets from competitors and partners in the U.S. and elsewhere.

Huawei was also accused of doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to U.S. government officials and banks as part of an effort to hide its misdeeds.

Lawyers for the company said U.S. investigators had used isolated episodes of wrongdoing by a few of Huawei's more than 200,000 employees to spin a false narrative about a grand conspiracy that didn't actually exist.

It's unclear what effect the verdict might have on Huawei's global fortunes. The company hasn't been allowed to sell equipment to U.S. carriers for years because of security concerns. It has also been blacklisted by other Western allies, including Canada and Britain.

That hasn't stopped the company from doing a robust business elsewhere. Its smartphones and other telecom equipment are sold globally. More recently, it has expanded into chipmaking as the boom in artificial intelligence fuels demand for microprocessors, becoming an important alternative in China to chips made by companies such as Nvidia.
The U.S. announced its criminal charges against Huawei in early 2019 and later expanded the allegations.
Chinese officials said the U.S. has engaged in “economic bullying” and improperly used national security as a pretext for oppressing Chinese companies.

The indictment against Huawei accused it of a long pattern of outright technology theft. Huawei, prosecutors said, once sold internet routers containing source code copied from a competitor. In another episode, a person working for Huawei slipped into a competitor's booth at a Chicago trade show to surreptitiously photograph the circuits inside another company's networking device, the indictment said. Prosecutors said that on another occasion, a Huawei worker removed a robotic arm from a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured.
The victim companies included Cisco Systems, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, Quintel USA and Fujitsu, according to court records.

“The tone was set at the top by Huawei leaders and executives who themselves engaged in criminal conduct, like lying to Congress, lying to banks, violating US sanctions and trying to interfere with the very criminal investigation that led to this case,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa told the jury at the trial.

articles.title: Under Nishant’s leadership, the future of the party remains bright for next 30 years, says Sanjay Jha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Jha also said that former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has transformed Bihar’s image and identity over the past two decades.
Janata Dal (United) on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) celebrated Sushasan Diwas (Good governance Day) to mark the day Nitish Kumar began his first full term as the Bihar Chief Minister.

JD(U) National President Nitish Kumar also attended the main programme as a chief guest organised at the State headquarters office in Patna along with his son Nishant Kumar and Sanjay Jha, National Working president of the party.
Mr. Kumar also saw his sand art displayed in the office premises. Mr. Kumar was welcomed by party workers while showering rose petals on him.

Mr. Jha while addressing the party workers, said that the new generation needs to know what conditions were like in Bihar in 2005 and how Nitish Kumar ji worked to take the state forward, with good governance, development and social justice at the centre.
‘Nitish Samvad’ (Nitish Dialogue) events were also organized in every district where JD(U) leaders spoke about the works done by Mr. Kumar.

“Nitish Kumar ji will be remembered for his work for thousands of years. Bihar needed a leader who would understand its suffering, restore its lost dignity and take it forward on a new path of development. On November 24, 2005, a new era of good governance began in Bihar under the leadership of Nitish Kumar ji,”Mr. Jha said.

He further said, “The challenges Bihar faced before 2005 are no secret. From law and order to education, healthcare, roads and electricity, the state was in a worrying state on almost every measure of development. Even Biharis, living in other states, were reluctant to reveal their identity. But through his firm resolve, clear vision and systematic efforts, Nitish Kumar ji has transformed Bihar’s image and identity over the past two decades.”
Mr. Jha asserted that today, being called a Bihari is no longer an insult, but a source of pride and self-respect as Bihar has established a new identity for itself in many areas of development.
He also pointed out that the impact of Nitish Kumar work will endure for many generations to come.
“His presence will continue to inspire all of us to carry forward his commitment to building a developed, prosperous and self-reliant Bihar of his dreams,”Mr. Jha said.
Mr. Jha also said that Nitish Kumar brought the ideology of socialism into reality on the ground.
He explained that the Bhagalpur riots occurred during the rule of the Congress government, followed by 15 years of Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) rule, yet the victims never received justice.

articles.title: Bengal film fraternity members meet CM Suvendu Adhikari; demand more Bengali film screening
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Film fraternity members said regional Bengali language films were being sidelined because of national and international films
The West Bengal film fraternity members met with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (November 24) and demanded more Bengali film screenings at the cinema halls across the State.
Actors turned Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs Roopa Ganguly, Rudranil Ghosh, and others were present at the meeting.

“Today, we made a decision about Bengali films, to preserve the dignity and respect of regional Bengali culture, one Bengali film will have to be shown during prime time under any circumstances. Special care will be taken to ensure that Bengali films are not suddenly removed from the shows,” Mr Ghosh said.

Mr. Ghosh further added that new theatres will be built at 51 new locations. 70 old halls will also be converted into cinema halls to recover the conditions of the Bengali film industry. He further added that the CM has given a structured plan to ask producers, distributors, and other stakeholders to work together to better the condition of the industry.

Speaking to journalists after the meeting with the CM, Ms Ganguly also said, “There were many problems, and many of those problems are being resolved. Financial approval for many halls has also been given.”

“If we can all work together on all those things discussed with the CM today, then the face of the Bengali film industry will be completely different five years from now,” Bengali film producer Shrikant Mohta said. He added that the CM has shown commitment towards the Bengali film industry and has promised multiple steps to help change the situation on ground.
On Monday (November 23), the makers of new Bengali film “Sadhak Bamakhyapa” had raised concerns that they are not able to secure movie halls to screen their new film in theatres across the State.

“No other regional industry allows this where they push out their own language films to give space to English or Hindi films,” actor Saheb Chattopadhyay said about the distribution issue of the film. He said that he is not against any language films but that their own regional films should not be pushed out because of national and international films and everyone should get a fair chance to screen their cinema.
After the meeting with the Bengali film fraternity members, BJP WB page posted on their social media and announced that Sadhak Bamakhyapa will not be sidelined and be screened across the State.
“The Honourable Chief Minister Shri @SuvenduWB is leading the charge to celebrate and uplift Bengali cinema, language, and culture!” The BJP WB page said on their social media post.

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Yashar ​said that Mr. Eisenkot had met with Avigdor ⁠Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, and they agreed on a deal afterward

Israel’s Yashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot , said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) it agreed to ​sign a coalition pact with a right-wing Opposition party as it ‌seeks to form a government following last month’s election.

Yashar ​said that Mr. Eisenkot had met with Avigdor ⁠Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, earlier on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) and they agreed on a deal afterward, the first such alliance since the election.

Israel’s ‌Parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government, after the election on October 27 stripped ‌Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority but left ‌others ⁠with no clear path to power.
President Isaac Herzog has ⁠tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, while Mr. Netanyahu remains caretaker Prime Minister.
Mr. Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its ​majority. It now holds 53 ‌of the Knesset’s 120 seats.

Mr. Eisenkot’s center-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners — including Mr. Lieberman — hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold ‌19 seats and are aligned with Mr. Eisenkot in their ​vehement opposition to Mr. Netanyahu.

The agreement between Mr. Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Mr. Lieberman, whose party ⁠won 7, was something of a surprise, since Mr. Lieberman had been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from ‌Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu.
Mr. Lieberman has also said his main goal is to oust Mr. Netanyahu from power.

Mr. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, but he could ask for a 14-day extension. If he fails, Mr. Netanyahu would get a shot. If ‌no one is able to form a government, another election will be held ​next year.
Talks are also ongoing between Mr. Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a ⁠unity government.

The left-wing Democrats party, which won 8 parliamentary seats, separately said ⁠it was suspending talks with Mr. Eisenkot because of progress in his talks with Mr. Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible ‌unity government and “given with the deadlock in negotiations to form a ‘change government.’
Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, has said he ​prefers a government without Mr. Netanyahu but with Arab parties.

articles.title: Juvenile Justice Board Hears Bail Plea of Child in Conflict with Law After High Court Rejection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court held that the CCL performed maneuvers with vehicles, posted videos on a page on Instagram, and operated vehicles without prioritizing safety, and that the parents knew of these acts but did not intervene

The Juvenile Justice Board is hearing a bail application under Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, submitted by a Child in Conflict with Law (CCL) concerning C.R. No.58/2026 at Tilak Nagar Police Station, which involves a collision on February 5, 2026, that caused death and disability, following orders from the Sessions Court and the Bombay High Court that cancelled bail and required placement in a centre for reformation.

The High Court held that the CCL performed maneuvers with vehicles, posted videos on a page on Instagram, and operated vehicles without prioritizing safety, and that the parents knew of these acts but did not intervene, leading the Sessions Court to set aside the bail order of March 6, 2026, on July 31, 2026, and the Bombay High Court to reject the revision on September 9, 2026, in Criminal Revision Application .

The Board noted an application dated October 21, 2026, where the CCL admitted that a paper presented as an examination timetable on October 9, 2026, did not belong to him because the paper contained subjects from a course under a scheme while the admission receipt of the CCL indicated enrollment in a course with a fee structure, and the confirmation for the paper came from the father of the CCL, who is a co-accused with a challenge to bail, and the Board had asked for confirmation on three occasions before receiving the confirmation from the father.

The report from the police stated that the CCL drove a KIA Seltos motorcar without a licence for driving and collided with a scooter on February 5, 2026, resulting in the death of Dhrumil Patel on February 15, 2026, and causing disability to the survivor, with the chargesheet filed on July 14, 2026, under Sections 281, 125, 125(A), 125(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, read with Sections 184 and 199 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998, and Section 105 of the BNS.

articles.title: Human Metabolic Chamber inaugurated at CMC in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer
A state-of-the-art Human Metabolic Chamber was inaugurated at Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore to advance research on nutrition, diabetes, obesity, and metabolic health.

According to a press release, the initiative was a joint collaboration of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and the CMC. The facility was opened by Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.

The initiative brings together two of India’s premier institutions - combining TIFR’s strengths in fundamental and interdisciplinary science with CMC Vellore’s expertise in clinical medicine and metabolic research.

Anchored by TIFR’s Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development & Aging (ARUMDA) and CMC’s Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, the collaboration will help address questions on how the body uses energy, and how this varies across diverse populations, diets, and lifestyles in India.

The chamber complements the National Analytical Facility for Nutrition and Metabolism Research, which ARUMDA established last year. Together, the two facilities allow researchers to link molecular and biochemical measurements with how the body uses energy. This ability to study metabolism at both levels places the initiative at the forefront of Indian research on metabolic diseases and aging.

The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter that measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats, and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer. These measurements reveal the total energy expenditure and how the body switches between using fat and carbohydrates across meals, activity, and sleep.

By analysing metabolism over an extended daily cycle, the chamber offers a more comprehensive picture than a brief measurement alone. It enables researchers to examine how energy use changes over time and under carefully defined study conditions. This capability is particularly important in India, whose diverse populations, dietary patterns, and lifestyles remain under-represented in global reference data.

Measurements generated through the facility can help refine the understanding of energy and nutrient requirements, and strengthen the evidence underpinning strategies against metabolic disease and malnutrition, the release said.

articles.title: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ’s ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar’s leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees

Malaysia will repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as he defended the government's engagement with Myanmar's military leadership, despite a landmark international court ruling finding the country responsible for genocide against Rohingya Muslims.
Editorial | Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice

The International Court of Justice, based in The Hague, Netherlands, last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority, with evidence showing Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in a 2017 military operation that included mass rapes and killings, and the destruction of thousands of homes.

Myanmar's government has dismissed the ruling as unfair. Mr. Anwar told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ's ruling, but would continue to engage with Myanmar's leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees.

Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya who fled a military crackdown and members of other ethnic minorities. Mr. Anwar said that efforts to resettle them in third countries had been unsuccessful and Malaysia couldn't continue bearing the burden indefinitely.
He said that talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, who visited Kuala Lumpur last month, had helped bring progress to the long-standing issue.
Another 1,500 people will be sent back on three Myanmar naval vessels on Dec. 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will return throughout next month by air, with all costs borne by Myanmar, Mr. Anwar said.
A total of 10,476 Myanmar nationals have already been repatriated this year, including 1,476 who were taken home aboard a Myanmar naval vessel on September 29, he said.
Malaysia had secured a guarantee of a “safe and dignified return” for those repatriated, Mr. Anwar said.
“So far, based on monitoring by Malaysian intelligence, none of the 10,476 individuals have been subjected to any form of pressure,” he said.

Despite the engagement with Myanmar, Mr. Anwar said that Malaysia remained committed to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' peace plan to end violence and resolve a prolonged crisis in Myanmar after the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. It sparked widespread opposition that plunged large parts of the country into conflict.

The 11-nation regional bloc has renewed diplomatic pressure on Myanmar for failing to implement its peace initiative and restricted the country's top leaders from major regional summits. Myanmar has slammed ASEAN for unfair treatment.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram row LIVE: Madurai District Collector says Devasthanam did not authorise lamp-lighting team
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devotees barred from Tirupparankundram hill for the second consecutive day and heavy security deployed

The Hindu parties orally mention an application filed before the Supreme Court seeking directions to the State and temple authorities that the deepam lit at the Deepa Mandapam be shifted to the ‘Deepathoon’.

“To light the lamp at the Deepathoon either by igniting it from the same Deepam that is still burning at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple, or by making the necessary arrangements in accordance with the order dated November 20, 2026,” the application said.

TNCC chief B. Manickam Tagore on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) accused the BJP, RSS and Hindu Munnani of attempting to “politicise” the Karthigai Deepam celebrations at Thirupparankundram to divide the people of the state.

Speaking to reporters in Thirupparankundram, a day after protests erupted over the ceremonial lamp not being lit at the disputed stone pillar (Deepathoon) atop the hill, Mr. Tagore defended the Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance government, and claimed that “both the administration and the district collector had respected the Supreme Court’s orders.”

“It clearly states that the Devasthanam will decide who will light the lamp and where it will be lit. The Devasthanam’s board of trustees (Arangavalar Kuzhu) sat for six hours and decided to light it at the same traditional place as per custom. Both the Tamil Nadu government and the collector have respected the Supreme Court orders,” he said.

The Madurai District Collector on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) squarely blamed the ‘devasthanam’ of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple on Thirupparankundram Hill for defying a Supreme Court order to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on November 24.

In a preliminary status report, Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna said he had held multiple meetings, been in constant touch with the local and police authorities and made arrangements to ensure the map was lit at the ‘Deepathoon’ ever since the evening of the Supreme Court order on November 20.

“From the side of the District Administration, every arrangement was complete and every possible difficulty had been offered an immediate solution. The only step was the authorisation of the team [to light the lamp] by the Devasthanam,” the Collector’s report said.
Supreme Court hears Deepathoon dispute as Hindu parties accuse the State of defying orders on lighting the Karthigai Deepam lamp.

The BJP on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) targeted the INDIA alliance and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the Karthigai Deepam row, accusing the Tamil Nadu government of defying the Supreme Court’s directions and showing contempt for the Constitution.
Addressing a press conference, BJP Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said the state government did not implement the Supreme Court’s order.

“I want to bring to your notice the biggest contempt for constitutional authority being committed by the INDIA alliance’s Tamil Nadu government, in utter disregard of India’s eternal culture,” he said.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram Deepathoon row: What does John Doe order passed by Madras HC mean?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Madras High Court restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a ‘limited one-time arrangement’ only.

The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, on November 24, 2026, passed a ‘John Doe’ order in the Deepathoon case with regard to the lighting of the lamp at Thirupparankundram hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai for Karthigai Deepam. The High Court bench restrained anyone from violating the November 20 Supreme Court order which allowed the lighting of the lamp on the hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement” only.

A ‘John Doe’ order is an ex parte injuction ordered against unknown persons. Ex parte injunctions are injunctions that are granted even without hearing the other party. Issued against anonymous offenders, these are also called ‘Ashok Kumar’ orders in India and are equivalents of the place holder ‘John Doe’ used in the U.S.
Often used as a prohibitory measure by the courts, John Doe orders are issued against anonymous offenders or the world at large.
In the Thirupparankundram-Deepathoon case, the High Court restricted “members of the general public” from calling for violating the November 20 order issued by the Supreme Court on the issue.

“Article 144 of the Constitution mandates that all authorities, civil and judicial, in the territory of India shall act in aid of the Supreme Court. The District Collector is a civilian authority and Article 144 will squarely apply to him. Since officials brazenly defied judicial orders last year in connection with Karthigai Deepam, we deem it necessary to remind the District Collector that he is a public servant who is answerable only to the Supreme Court in this case. He shall ignore any contra advice given by any other authority,” the Bench said.

“We are sure that no law officer worth his salt will counsel him to act in contravention of the order dated November 20. No doubt, a review petition has been filed before the Supreme Court in respect of the order dated November 20. But no order has been passed in the review petition...The law that has been laid down is that pendency of a review petition is not a ground for non-compliance,” the court added.
John Doe or Ashok Kumar orders are frequently used in intellectual property right cases.

A 2026 report in The Hindu notes that actor Salman Khan had “sought an injunction against unknown persons, joined as Defendant No. 1 (’John Doe’ or ‘Ashok Kumar’) in a case relating to a China-based AI voice generation platform seeking to vacate an interim injunction protecting Mr Khan’s personality rights.
The controversy revolves around the Thirupparankanduram hillock in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai and the lighting of a ceremonial lamp on the day of Karthigai Deepam.

On November 20, the Supreme Court had ruled allowing the lighting of the lamp on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram Hill as a “limited one-time arrangement.” The deepathoon , or stone lamp pillar, is around 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. While the dargah is on the hilltop, the Subramaniya Swamy Temple is at the base of the hillock. The court’s interim arrangement comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the dargah on the ownership of the hilltop and the deepathoon site.
However, the ruling TVK government on November 24, defied the Supreme Court order , and the festival lamp was lit only at its customary place at the Thirupparankundram hill.

articles.title: Supreme Court sets aside Allahabad High Court order for CBI, ED enquiries into DA complaint against Rahul Gandhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The top court directs the Congress leader to be impleaded as a party in the High Court case

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) set aside orders passed by the Allahabad High Court directing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) inquiries into a disproportionate assets’ complaint against Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi .

Mr. Gandhi had challenged the interim orders as a green signal to conduct a “fishing” expedition against him . The Congress leader had submitted in his appeal to the Supreme Court that the interim orders were passed without making him a party or hearing him first.
A three-judge bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant directed that Mr. Gandhi be impleaded as a party, while relegating the case back to the High Court to be heard from the very threshold.
“We are on the basic fundamentals of hearing. We will not make any observations on the merits of the case,” Chief Justice Kant said.
The complainant, Vignesh Shishir, who is the respondent before the Supreme Court in Mr. Gandhi’s appeal, said that an accused does not have an inherent right to be heard during the pre-FIR stage.
However, Justice Joymalya Bagchi pointed out that under the new law, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the scope for the accused to be heard has been expanded.

Mr. Gandhi, represented by advocate Prasanna S., termed the series of directions passed by the Lucknow Bench of the High Court in May and July directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) to probe the allegations against him as one of the rarest instances of a constitutional court acting contrary to several first principles or basic, fundamental legal rules all at once.
The Opposition Leader had termed these orders “outside the settled rules of law or erroneous, which would be a gross understatement.”
Mr. Gandhi submitted that the proceedings were characterised by the unjustified secrecy of in-chamber hearings, with documents and pleadings kept under wraps in sealed covers.
He had maintained that the High Court did not refer to the foundational material or provide reasons in the orders for directing a “roving inquiry”.

Mr. Gandhi said the High Court did not consider the fact that Mr. Shishir is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Rashtriya Swayam Sevak Sangh (RSS), who had filed multiple complaints and public-interest litigation against him in the past, including allegations of foreign citizenship, up to now, and allegations of holding disproportionate assets.

Mr. Gandhi had said that the repeated filing of proceedings against him by the same “motivated individuals”, based on “unsubstantiated allegations”, constituted a relevant background demonstrating a pattern of persistent and vexatious litigation.

articles.title: Keralam CM Satheesan says he too is victim of online attacks, alleges ‘important individual’ behind fake news campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters”

Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that he himself was a victim of online attacks, and that an “important individual” was behind the dissemination of such fake news.
At a post-Cabinet press briefing, Mr. Satheesan was responding to questions on the online attacks on Congress party leaders and members of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy’s family.

Mr. Satheesan also displayed copies of social media cards with his photograph which purportedly claim that the government had decided to discontinue the welfare pensions and another attributed to Chandy Oommen that Mr. Satheesan was among the individuals who had caused anguish to his father and Oommen Chandy. “Many such fake news were are being spread in the name of mainstream media organisations,” he said.
“All this comes from one centre, led by an important individual,” he said, but declined to name the person.

On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Mr. Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters.” Such questions should be posed to KPCC president Sunny Joseph, he said.
Mr. Satheesan said the discussions regarding appointments to the top posts of boards and corporations under the State government were in the final stages.

Mr. Satheesan’s response came amid criticism from within the Congress party and UDF constituents such as the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) that the appointments were not finalised even after the UDF government had completed six months in power.
Mr. Satheesan said the appointments would be made soon and the talks were in the final stages.

On Monday, after a State secretariat meeting of the RSP, its leader N.K. Premachandran had sharply criticised the delay and also the “absence” of regular meetings of the UDF. The RSP also wanted the appointments to be completed, if possible, this month itself.
On his part, Mr. Satheesan sought to play down the RSP leader’s remarks, saying that it was not criticism as such, and that the party merely wanted the board, corporation division completed quickly.

articles.title: 30 missing terrorists from Reasi exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms training, disturb peace in India: DGP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan

Thirty terrorists hailing from Reasi district, who had gone missing between 1991 and 2003, have exfiltrated to Pakistan and are working for a terror outfit, supplying arms, ammunition and money to revive terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir, Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan for weapons training for waging war against India.

"These persons are now working for HM [Hizbul Mujahideen] in Pakistan and are supplying arms and ammunition, money, to promote terrorism in J&K, besides instigating and radicalising the youth for taking part in terror activities in the area," the DGP said on X.

The 30 terrorists operating from Pakistan have been identified as Mohd Qayoom of Shadole, Mohd Sabdar of Shajroo, Ghulam Mohd and Ghulam Qadir, both sons of Samdoo and residents of Khour, Mushtaq Ahmad of Khour and Khushal Hussain, a resident of Dada.

The list further names Abdul Majeed, Mohd Rafiq, alias Shabir, Shabir Ahmad and Manzoor Ahmad, all residents of Karmkatha, Makhna and Alaf Din, both residents of Shajroo, Abdul Majeed of Lar, Ghulam Mohd, alias Gamma, of Shajroo, and Mushtaq Ahmad of Sildhar.

articles.title: Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27

Air passenger services recorded 35.52% inflation in the July-September quarter, recording the highest rate of price rise among the seven major services for which the inflation data was released on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

Securities transaction services and banking services, however, recorded a deflation of 6.93% and 3.96% respectively, the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27 released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry showed.
The PPI has inflation data for seven major services — Banking, Securities Transaction, Insurance, Management of Pension Funds, Railways, Air (Passenger), and Telecom — with base year 2022-23.
Service PPI measures the change in the average prices received by producers on production of a service.
As per the data, inflation in Air (Passenger) Services rose 35.52% YoY in the second quarter, compared to 31.94% in the first quarter.
Annual inflation in the railway passenger service price index rose 2.17% during the September quarter, lower than 3.50% in the June quarter.
Inflation in 'Banking Service Contribution' was 3.86% in Q2 of FY27, higher than 2.62% in Q1. The 'Banking Service Price' witnessed 3.96% deflation in Q2, vis-a-vis 4.98% deflation in Q1.
Securities Transaction Service Prices saw a deflation of 6.93% in Q2, compared to 1.32% deflation in June quarter.

Pension fund management, insurance and telecom services recorded an inflation of 1.01%, 0.49% and 0.54%, respectively in September quarter, compared to 5.48%, 0.98% and 0.72%, respectively in the June quarter.
The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.

The government in June came out with the maiden PPI data for both goods and services to better reflect price movement at producer's level, paving the way for phasing out wholesale price index (WPI)-based inflation numbers in the next five years. Thereafter, in August the services PPI data was issued.

articles.title: Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fuel ‘clout’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the negotiating process more urgent than ever.

The failure of the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, to agree on its central political statement, with countries unable to bridge their differences over fossil fuels and other key questions of climate action, has exposed the fragility of international climate cooperation. It should also sharpen scrutiny of who gets access to climate negotiations, whose interests they represent and what safeguards keep decisions accountable to the public.

The Türkiye summit ended without agreement on an overarching statement. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he shared the “deep disappointment” of many that the conference was unable to reach consensus on a statement that typically sends a policy signal to all nations. Some separate negotiating decisions were reached though. Nevertheless, the absence of a political consensus was a serious setback.

The breakdown does not show that fossil fuel lobbying caused the impasse. But it does make more urgent a separate question about the credibility of the process. A forum that asks governments to make decisions in the global public interest must be transparent about who is seeking to shape those decisions, what interests they represent and how conflicts are managed.

The international climate negotiations that take place every year still lack a comprehensive, enforceable system to identify and manage conflicts of interest involving powerful commercial interests, including fossil fuel companies and state-owned energy businesses. The Antalya conference has underlined why that gap matters.

articles.title: Why are landmine casualties rising as the global ban comes under threat? | Explained

fullParagraphs: Why is the Mine Ban Treaty facing a crisis? Why are more civilians falling victim to landmines? Are countries turning away from the landmine ban?

The story so far: Landmines and explosive remnants of war (ERW, meaning unexploded or abandoned ordnance) killed or injured more people in 2025 than in any year since 2020, according to the 28th annual Landmine Monitor report, which was released on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines (ICBL). Its findings come as the Mine Ban Treaty, which bans antipersonnel mines, has seen its first-ever withdrawals.

The treaty came into force on March 1, 1999, after a campaign that won the ICBL the Nobel Peace Prize in 1997. Countries that join must stop the use, stockpiling, production, and transfer of antipersonnel mines. They must destroy their stockpiles within four years and clear mines in areas they control within 10 years. A total of 162 countries are now bound by the treaty, while 35 remain outside it.

articles.title: India-Nepal joint military exercise begins in Rupandehi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The exercise, involving battalion-level soldiers from the two countries, will run till December 8
A joint military training exercise between Nepal and India, focusing on disaster management, forest welfare and humanitarian assistance, commenced on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).
The 20th edition of the training exercise, “Abhyas Suryakiran”, began at Nepal Army Battle School in Saljhandi, Rupandehi district, according to a press release issued by the Nepal Army.
The exercise, involving battalion-level soldiers from the two countries, will run till December 8.

During the exercise, the military personnel of the two countries will exchange theoretical and practical aspects as well as special experiences relating to disaster management, forest warfare and humanitarian assistance, according to the Nepal Army.
The 19th edition of the joint military exercise was held in Uttarakhand’s Pithoragarh last year.

The Nepal Army believes such types of military exercises will further deepen friendly military relations between the two countries and also enhance professional skills and understanding between the soldiers of the two countries, the press release said.

articles.title: China launches crewed spaceship carrying first Pakistani astronaut to its space station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Using a Long March-2F rocket, the spacecraft took ‌off at 8:18 a.m. (0018 GMT) ‌from ⁠the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre ⁠in northwest China

China on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) launched its Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship carrying three astronauts , including Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali , the first foreign national to participate in the country’s crewed space programme.
The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China, with officials declaring the launch successful minutes later.
The crew comprises mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi and Ali, who will become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s orbiting Tiangong space station.
Mr. Ali will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after spending about a week in orbit, while Chinese astronauts typically stay at the station for about six months.

articles.title: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Riyadh; New Delhi condemns strike
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia
Two Indians were among those injured in an attack on a financial district in Riyadh that triggered strong condemnation from New Delhi.
India also denounced continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

“Two Indians are among those injured in the attack on Riyadh financial district. The embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
The attack was carried out on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). Local authorities said the injured included two Saudi citizens, three Nepalese and four Egyptian nationals.

The MEA said India strongly condemns the attack in Riyadh as well as the continued strikes targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. “These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks,” it said in a statement.

India also reiterated its firm solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed its unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
“We earnestly hope that peace and normalcy will return to the region at the earliest,” the MEA said.
There has been a sudden escalation in tensions in West Asia, especially after the Houthis carried out several strikes on Saudi Arabia.
The West Asia conflict began in February following attacks on Iran by the U.S. and Israel. New Delhi has consistently called for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.

India has been specifically voicing serious concern over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s civilian infrastructure and economic assets, cautioning that such strikes undermine regional stability and threaten freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

articles.title: North Korea declares a Swiss diplomat persona non grata and orders him to leave
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un,c ondemned Switzerland for imposing sanctions on a youth camp in eastern North Korea over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russia-occupied areas of Ukraine

North Korea on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) declared a senior Swiss diplomat heading the country's newly opened diplomatic office in Pyongyang persona non grata and ordered him to leave the country within 48 hours.

The move came a day after Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, threatened to close the office. She condemned Switzerland for imposing sanctions on a youth camp in eastern North Korea over its alleged role in the transfer of children from Russia-occupied areas of Ukraine.

The Korean Central News Agency said a senior Foreign Ministry official summoned Astier Sylvain, who heads the Swiss diplomatic office that opened in Pyongyang last month, and handed him a notice demanding the office's closure and his departure, in protest of the Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp in Wonsan.

articles.title: All you need to know about: Primary ciliary dyskinesia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: PCD is a rare genetic disorder that affects the cilia, which help move mucus and other particles out of the respiratory tract. Mucus is therefore not cleared effectively and builds up in the respiratory tract, increasing the risk of recurrent infections

Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited disorder that affects tiny, hair-like structures in the body called cilia. When these structures fail to move properly, mucus and bacteria accumulate in the airways, increasing the risk of recurrent respiratory infections and long-term lung damage.

While there is currently no cure, early diagnosis and regular treatment can help manage symptoms and preserve lung function. Recent research into the genetic causes of PCD is also offering new insights into the disease and its diagnosis.

articles.title: What is Beaver Supermoon, when is the next supermoon and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth

Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon

The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze.

Supermoon appears 14 per cent bigger and 30 per cent brighter than a micromoon, which occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being near its apogee — the farthest point from Earth in its orbit.
The “Beaver moon” is a moniker for November’s full moon adopted by the Old Farmer’s Almanac , supposedly from Algonquian languages once spoken by Native Americans in the New England territory.

Though not a rare occurrence, supermoons only happen three to four times a year and always appear consecutively. Because the Moon is in its closest point to Earth, it can cause higher tides than usual, according to NASA.
Supermoon is visible to the naked eye wherever skies are clear and no special equipment is required.
The next supermoon will be on December 24, 2026. The last supermoon of the year, it will be the largest full moon.
The first supermoon of 2027 will be on January 22, also known as the Wolf Supermoon.

‘Wolf moon’ is a traditional name for the first full moon that happens in January. Many full moons have old seasonal names, often popularised in folklore, that helped people keep track of the time of the year before the advent of modern calendars.

articles.title: When public duty meets medical privacy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A legislator undergoing prolonged treatment may retain the ability to perform official responsibilities. Functional capacity, rather than diagnosis alone, is therefore central to the legal question of what the public has the right to know

Sonia Gandhi, in her recently published memoir, recalls being advised surgery for suspected breast cancer in 2010. Since she is a prominent public figure, she wonders, in her book, whether she was entitled to even a modicum of privacy with regard to her health. Her account assumes renewed significance following a recent petition before the Madras High Court that inquired about the health of Kolathur MLA V.S. Babu (now deceased). These episodes expose a fundamental legal tension between the privacy politicians may want about their health, and the accountability they owe their constituents in a democracy. Does the public’s right to information justify waiving or limiting an office-holder’s medical confidentiality? How should a democracy reconcile these competing interests?

Medical information is among the most sensitive forms of personal information. A diagnosis may reveal not merely someone’s present condition but also their reproductive history, genetic predispositions, psychiatric illness or future health risks. Disclosure can invite discrimination, political exploitation and public speculation. In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court recognised privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21. Holding public office does not automatically extinguish this protection. A politician receiving treatment need not publish laboratory reports. Nor does a disability establish an inability to govern. State intrusion needs lawful justification, not curiosity.

The Constitution does not prescribe a general medical-fitness requirement for occupying high public office. Article 58 sets eligibility conditions for the President but requires no medical-fitness certificate. Article 65(2) allows the Vice-President to perform presidential functions when the President cannot do so through absence, illness or another cause. The Constitution recognises presidential illness but does not specify a detailed procedure or medical authority to determine contested incapacity. This distinction between eligibility to assume office and capacity to continue functioning deserves closer scrutiny.

For legislators, Articles 102 and 191 prescribe disqualification when a person is of ‘unsound mind’ and stands so declared by a competent court (not by a medical board). Section 16(1)(b) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, similarly provides for disqualification from electoral registration (by court not medical board). For Supreme Court judges, Article 124(4) permits removal on proof of incapacity, while the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, provides a procedure that may involve a Medical Board. Article 317(3)(c), governing Public Service Commission members, permits removal for unfitness arising from ‘infirmity of mind or body’.

When public duty meets medical privacy

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

A legislator undergoing prolonged treatment may retain the ability to perform official responsibilities. Functional capacity, rather than diagnosis alone, is therefore central to the legal question of what the public has the right to know

Sonia Gandhi, in her recently published memoir, recalls being advised surgery for suspected breast cancer in 2010. Since she is a prominent public figure, she wonders, in her book, whether she was entitled to even a modicum of privacy with regard to her health. Her account assumes renewed significance following a recent petition before the Madras High Court that inquired about the health of Kolathur MLA V.S. Babu (now deceased). These episodes expose a fundamental legal tension between the privacy politicians may want about their health, and the accountability they owe their constituents in a democracy. Does the public’s right to information justify waiving or limiting an office-holder’s medical confidentiality? How should a democracy reconcile these competing interests?

Medical information is among the most sensitive forms of personal information. A diagnosis may reveal not merely someone’s present condition but also their reproductive history, genetic predispositions, psychiatric illness or future health risks. Disclosure can invite discrimination, political exploitation and public speculation. In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court recognised privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21. Holding public office does not automatically extinguish this protection. A politician receiving treatment need not publish laboratory reports. Nor does a disability establish an inability to govern. State intrusion needs lawful justification, not curiosity.

The Constitution does not prescribe a general medical-fitness requirement for occupying high public office. Article 58 sets eligibility conditions for the President but requires no medical-fitness certificate. Article 65(2) allows the Vice-President to perform presidential functions when the President cannot do so through absence, illness or another cause. The Constitution recognises presidential illness but does not specify a detailed procedure or medical authority to determine contested incapacity. This distinction between eligibility to assume office and capacity to continue functioning deserves closer scrutiny.

For legislators, Articles 102 and 191 prescribe disqualification when a person is of ‘unsound mind’ and stands so declared by a competent court (not by a medical board). Section 16(1)(b) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, similarly provides for disqualification from electoral registration (by court not medical board). For Supreme Court judges, Article 124(4) permits removal on proof of incapacity, while the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, provides a procedure that may involve a Medical Board. Article 317(3)(c), governing Public Service Commission members, permits removal for unfitness arising from ‘infirmity of mind or body’.

articles.title: The cow, the flea and the genome: One Health and the statecraft of prevention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A cattle virus at home and a plague scare abroad make the same argument this World One Health Day: life is epidemiologically indivisible, and the institutions that govern and study it must learn to be so too

In the second of his Major Rock Edicts, cut into stone in the third century BCE, Ashoka records that he has provided medical care of two kinds, for people and for animals, and has had healing herbs planted wherever they were lacking. Twenty-three centuries before the phrase existed, an Indian State treated the health of humans, animals and the land as a single charge of government. Rudolf Virchow, who introduced the word ‘zoonosis’, restated the idea for the age of the microscope: between animal and human medicine there is no dividing line, nor should there be.

Modern governance, however, forgot what Ashoka and Virchow knew. It allotted people to one ministry, livestock to another and forests to a third, and pathogens, which recognise no such allocation of business, have exploited the gaps ever since. One Health, which the world marks on November 3, is the effort to recover that lost unity with the tools of the 21st century by bringing human, animal and environmental health into a common framework for research, surveillance and prevention. The Indian philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam , which regards the world as one family, resonates with this understanding of interconnected life.

This year the case makes itself. Lumpy skin disease (LSD) has returned to India. The September forecast from ICAR-National Institute of Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease Informatics’ early-warning system placed 219 districts across 28 states and Union Territories at risk, and Rajasthan had recorded more than 10,400 cases in 10 eastern districts by mid-September. In Siberia, a young technician at Irkutsk’s anti-plague institute died in early October, of what Russian authorities called pneumonia of unknown cause, amid reports of pneumonic plague. Nearly 200 people were placed under observation. Whatever the final diagnosis, Yersinia pestis , the organism of the Black Death, has never left us. It persists in rodents and their fleas, from the marmots of the Central Asian steppe to the prairie dogs of New Mexico and the rats of Madagascar.

Neither story respects a departmental boundary. LSD does not infect people, but it drains milk cans, household incomes and children’s nutrition. Plague is at once a problem of wildlife ecology, laboratory biosafety, clinical medicine and public trust.

articles.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he is in therapy as comeback rally fades
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board

Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.

"I made some terrible mistakes," Mr. Huang told an hourlong all-hands meeting at the company's Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a livestream of the event.
He told staff it was "not acceptable" that he had broken a code of conduct he had helped write, and dismissed suggestions that he was back because U.S. President Donald Trump had pressured the board.
But Mr. Trump told CNBC on Monday (November 23, 2026) that he had been in contact with directors about Mr. Huang's return. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he said. "And I convinced them."
After vaulting more than 30% on Monday (November 23, 2026), Nvidia shares were down about six percent at close on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."
So far Monday's surge was a "one day wonder...We are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.

Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.
Mr. Trump was reportedly talked into backing the return of the Taiwan-born CEO after top tech investors told him the U.S. economy and Wall Street depended on it.
Nvidia said Monday (November 23, 2026) that it had reinstated Mr. Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.
Mr. Trump is also an investor in Nvidia, owning as many as 370,000 shares in the company as of September 30, according to filings.
Shares linked to the AI boom have fallen steeply in recent weeks amid fears that the AI bubble, inflated since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022, was finally bursting.

articles.title: Workers in high-risk jobs to receive shots against rabies in Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Sanitation workers, dog catchers, animal handlers and others involved in veterinary activities to be vaccinated; govt. sanctions ₹2.22 crore for drive

Over a lakh persons belonging to high-risk occupational groups, including animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies, in all 38 districts will receive Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) against rabies under the Tamil Nadu State Action Plan for Dog-Mediated Rabies Elimination (SAPRE) - Vision 2030.

The State government has given the administrative sanction for implementation of the initiative at a cost of ₹2.22 crore, which will be met from the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, an order issued recently said.
In just four months of 2026, Tamil Nadu records 2.63 lakh dog bites, 17 deaths
Gaps in anti-rabies treatment persist in Chennai’s health centres

The Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine noted that certain occupational groups are routinely exposed to dogs and other animals in the course of their duties. Provision of PrEP to such identified high-risk personnel will provide an additional layer of protection and strengthen the State’s rabies elimination strategy.
The programme aims to provide PrEP to identified personnel of occupational groups having sustained risk of exposure to dogs and other potentially rabid animals.

The main categories include sanitation workers, animal handlers and dog catchers of local bodies and eligible personnel of the Animal Husbandry Department involved in animal handling, dog catching, veterinary and para-veterinary activities.

As per the National Guidelines on Rabies Prophylaxis, eligibility will be determined based on occupational exposure risk and the nature of duties performed. Based on the presently available department data, the preliminary beneficiary estimation was 1,29,009 - 1,21,844 local body sanitation workers, 3,324 local body animal handlers/dog catchers and 3,841 personnel attached to the Animal Husbandry department, the directorate said.

The initiative will be implemented through designated government health facilities, including Primary Health Centres (PHC), Urban PHCs, government hospitals, and medical college hospitals. Identification of beneficiaries and mobilisation will be carried out by the respective local bodies and Animal Husbandry Department.

articles.title: Over 23 lakh vehicles in Keralam have failed to clear Pollution Under Control checks since 2021
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Motor Vehicles department in coordination with State Police has imposed a total penalty of ₹43.2 crore from 2022 to September 30, 2026 for violations related to pollution-control requirements
About 23.9 lakh vehicles in Keralam have failed the mandatory Pollution Under Control (PUC) testing over the past five years.

A total of about 5.74 crore PUC tests were held from the financial year 2021 to September 30, 2026. About 5.5 crore vehicles had passed the test while 23.9 lakh vehicles failed to clear it, according to estimates by the Department of Transport.

About 57.5 lakh tests were conducted from March 2026 to September 30, 2026 and 1.87 lakh vehicles failed the PUC test during this period, said a report furnished by the Transport department before the National Green Tribunal in a case related to a plea for reducing vehicular emissions and promoting environmentally sustainable transport systems in the State.

Officials of the Transport department said that vehicles failing the PUC test were required to rectify the defects and undergo retesting before being given permission to resume operations. The pollution monitoring has been strengthened through a network of PUC testing centres that are integrated with the Vahan/Parivahan portal. The department has introduced an Aaadhaar-based mobile OTP system to prevent and reduce fake applications for getting the Pollution Under Control certificate, they said.

The Motor Vehicles department in coordination with the State Police had imposed a total penalty of ₹43.2 crore from the year 2022 to September 30, 2026 for violations related to pollution-control requirements, including vehicles without valid PUC certificates and those with high-emissions. Of the total penalty of ₹43.2 crore slapped, the authorities have collected ₹11.96 crore as on September 2026, according to official estimates.

About 23.9 lakh vehicles in Keralam have failed the mandatory Pollution Under Control (PUC) testing over the past five years.

articles.title: Kallakurichi police serve summons on TVK MLA Arul Vignesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: An Inspector attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person

The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh in connection with a case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer.

Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Mr. Arul Vignesh at the house.

The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages.
FIR registered against Kallakurichi TVK MLA for ‘misbehaving’ with woman IAS officer, Madras High Court told
Udhayanidhi Stalin submits petition to Tamil Nadu DGP demanding arrest of Kallakurichi and Thuraiyur TVK MLAs
Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Internal Complaints Committee has been constituted, Madras High Court told
The police have booked a case against the MLA under four sections including the POSH Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita

Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case registered at the Kallakurichi All Women Police station, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25).
The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry.
Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the Kallakurichi All Women Police station and the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.
