articles.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin submits petition to Tamil Nadu DGP demanding arrest of Kallakurichi and Thuraiyur TVK MLAs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The DMK leader’s petition also seeks transfer of the probe to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and inquiry into the Chief Secretary’s failure to act on a woman IAS officer’s complaint dated July 31, 2026.

Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) submitted a petition at the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police (DGP) office in Chennai demanding the immediate arrest of Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), action against Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, and the transfer of the assault case involving Thuraiyur TVK MLA and Deputy Speaker M. Ravishankar to the CB-CID.
Kallakurichi police serve summons on TVK MLA Arul Vignesh
DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector
Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Internal Complaints Committee has been constituted, Madras High Court told

The petition seeks the arrest of Arul Vignesh, preservation of electronic evidence in his possession, and securing of required CCTV footage. It also called for transfer of the probe to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and initiation of inquiry into the Chief Secretary’s failure to act on a woman IAS officer’s complaint dated July 31, 2026.

On the November 8 Thuraiyur incident, the petition urged the police to register an FIR against the Deputy Speaker, Samayapuram Police Inspector, and others involved, transfer the investigation to an independent agency, and ensure protection for the victim.
DMK members protest at Thuraiyur against Deputy Speaker for ‘assaulting’ man
Minister Nirmal Kumar denies allegations against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh

Speaking to reporters outside the DGP office, Udhayanidhi Stalin alleged that ruling party functionaries — including district secretaries, Ministers, and MLAs — are behind several acts of violence across Tamil Nadu.

Noting that the TVK government assumed office in May and the Kallakurichi MLA had allegedly harassed the IAS officer by July, he claimed that when the officer flagged the issue 116 days ago, the Chief Secretary merely advised the official to “move to another district.”

He pointed out that an FIR was registered in the case after a 116-day delay only following the court’s intervention. He questioned whether the Chief Secretary had apprised the Chief Minister of the complaint, and if so, why the Chief Minister failed to take action.

Similarly, highlighting that no action has been taken even 16 days after Deputy Speaker M. Ravishankar allegedly assaulted a petitioner at his residence, Udhayanidhi Stalin demanded the arrest of both the legislators and reiterated his call for a CBI probe into the Kallakurichi case.

articles.title: Telangana Govt to set up single window system for hassle free development of poultry sector: CM Revanth Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Revanth Reddy says poultry sector will be treated as priority area to formulate long term policies
The Telangana Government will soon introduce a single window system facilitating hassle free establishment of poultry farms at gram panchayat level across the State.

The single window system was contemplated after the industry took the challenges faced by it in establishing poultry units in the State and requested for the government’s support during times of crisis. The government has resolved to recognise poultry sector as a priority area and formulate policies aimed at providing long-term solutions.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has assured that there is no need to worry about the government policies and decisions. Accordingly, steps will be taken to provide all necessary assistance and support to the Poultry industry. The Chief Minister, who inaugurated the Poultry India Expo 2026 in Hyderabad on Wednesday (November 25, 20256), stressed the need for revising the existing policies in alignment with the requirements of the industry.

here was no “policy paralysis” in the State and the government would introduce new policies from time to time even as a decision was taken to continue the effective policies introduced by the previous governments. The efforts come in the backdrop of the efforts to achieve the goal of transforming Telangana into a US $3 trillion economy by 2047.

The Chief Minister said the government was firm on resolving the problems faced by the sector including shortage of maize and directed the Ministers concerned to take immediate steps in this direction. Appreciating the industry for organising a major expo, he said Telangana produced 5.3 crore eggs and lauded the important role played by the poultry entrepreneurs in providing nutritious food to students and the youth.

The industry displayed resilience in overcoming challenges and sustained its operations. He said that efforts should be made to provide more employment opportunities for agricultural labourers and farmers for further growth of the section . Poultry industry, he said, would strengthen the economic power of farmers apart from production of chickens and eggs.
Referring to the ongoing El Nino phenomenon, he said the government had kept stocks of fine rice ready for meeting the requirements for the next two years.

articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Internal Complaints Committee has been constituted, Madras High Court told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He also complains to Justice V. Lakshminarayanan that Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin had made factually incorrect statements to the media on the issue despite a gag order.

State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) informed the Madras High Court that the Tamil Nadu government has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 for inquiring into a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer against Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh .

Making a mention before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP said, a Government Order had been issued formally notifying the ICC and listing out its members. After hearing him, the judge said, the State should also ensure that an ICC was in place not only to deal with the present complaint but also with other future complaints that may arise due to sexual harassment of women at workplace.

Mr. Sathyan further told the judge that the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin had submitted a complaint to the Director General of Police (DGP)/Head of Police Force on Wednesday morning regarding the Kallakurichi MLA issue and addressed the media despite the court having passed a gag order on Tuesday (November 24) restraining the media from violating Section 16 of the POSH Act, 2013.

The SPP said, the LoP had spoken about a lot of things without ascertaining the foundational facts and that most of his statements were factually wrong. Responding to it, the judge said, he had already issued a direction to pull down all objectionable posts related to the issue from the social media and therefore, the cybercrime wing police would be at liberty to pull down videos and other materials related to the issue.

Further, taking note of the SPP’s submissions with regard to constitution of the ICC for an internal inquiry apart from the criminal investigation that shall happen parallelly, the judge decided to hear the matter next on Friday (November 27). In his interim order on Tuesday, the judge had appointed Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh as the investigating officer in the criminal case booked against the MLA.

He had also ordered that Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini, serving at the office of the Director General of Police/Head of Police Force in Chennai, shall monitor the investigation to be conducted pursuant to the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) booked at the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station on Monday (November 23).

Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Internal Complaints Committee has been constituted, Madras High Court told

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

He also complains to Justice V. Lakshminarayanan that Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin had made factually incorrect statements to the media on the issue despite a gag order.

State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) informed the Madras High Court that the Tamil Nadu government has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 for inquiring into a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer against Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh .

Making a mention before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP said, a Government Order had been issued formally notifying the ICC and listing out its members. After hearing him, the judge said, the State should also ensure that an ICC was in place not only to deal with the present complaint but also with other future complaints that may arise due to sexual harassment of women at workplace.

Mr. Sathyan further told the judge that the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin had submitted a complaint to the Director General of Police (DGP)/Head of Police Force on Wednesday morning regarding the Kallakurichi MLA issue and addressed the media despite the court having passed a gag order on Tuesday (November 24) restraining the media from violating Section 16 of the POSH Act, 2013.

The SPP said, the LoP had spoken about a lot of things without ascertaining the foundational facts and that most of his statements were factually wrong. Responding to it, the judge said, he had already issued a direction to pull down all objectionable posts related to the issue from the social media and therefore, the cybercrime wing police would be at liberty to pull down videos and other materials related to the issue.

Further, taking note of the SPP’s submissions with regard to constitution of the ICC for an internal inquiry apart from the criminal investigation that shall happen parallelly, the judge decided to hear the matter next on Friday (November 27). In his interim order on Tuesday, the judge had appointed Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh as the investigating officer in the criminal case booked against the MLA.

He had also ordered that Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini, serving at the office of the Director General of Police/Head of Police Force in Chennai, shall monitor the investigation to be conducted pursuant to the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) booked at the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station on Monday (November 23).

1. Core Context & Background: He also complains to Justice V. Lakshminarayanan that Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin had made factually incorrect statements to the media on the issue despite a gag order.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. Arul Vignesh .

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He had also ordered that Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini, serving at the office of the Director General of Police/Head of Police Force in Chennai, shall monitor the investigation to be conducted pursuant to the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) booked at the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station on Monday (November 23).

articles.title: Wildlife, forests, and culture in Gudalur: Sculptures, stories, and interactive workshops
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Into the Forest, an ongoing exhibition in Gudalur explores the relationship between forests, wildlife and people through sculptures, stories, workshops for children and creative artefacts made using invasive plant species

What if the plants choking the forests of the Nilgiris could be given a second life as works of art?An ongoing exhibition in Gudalur hopes to tell that story, bringing together conservation, craftsmanship and narratives of the intimate relationship between people and the natural world. “For all of us, sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea Antony, who takes care of storytelling and design at The Elephant People, a social enterprise based in Gudalur in the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve that makes hand-carved wildlife sculptures, masks, and everyday objects from invasive plant species like Lantana camara and Senna spectabilis.
Handcrafted objects made using invasive species vegetation | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

The exhibition is an attempt to draw attention to the changing landscapes of the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve, where the invasive species have spread across native habitats. These fast-growing plants suppress native vegetation, particularly grasses, affecting the food sources of wildlife and sometimes pushing animals towards human settlements.
ALSO WATCH Watch: How communities are rebuilding the Nilgiris ecosystem

The Elephant People collective works with Forest Departments of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka in clearing these invasive species. Instead of treating the recovered vegetation as waste, they transform the wood into handcrafted objects and sculptures inspired by the region’s wildlife, people, and landscapes.
The team includes over 50 makers across carving, painting, design, production, and operations | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Titled Into the Forest, the first exhibition by The Elephant People features stories of wildlife, people, shared landscapes, and practices connected to the land. “These stories are brought to life through art and craft, with sculptures and installations created by a team of makers from the Nilgiris, for whom sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea. The exhibition features large-scale sculptures, smaller carved pieces, and interactive storytelling experiences. For children, there will be facilitated painting and story-building workshops, alongside interactive art installations that let them explore the forest through play. These installations offer opportunities to learn about different species, their habitats, and the sounds they make.

“Over the last three years, we’ve been exploring the stories of the Nilgiris and finding ways to bring them to life through art and craft. The region has been central to this journey. It’s wildlife, landscapes, people and the many relationships between them have shaped the stories we are drawn to and the work we create ,” says Rhea. While discovering stories of different species, they also learnt about encounters between people and wildlife, traditional practices, food cultures and ways of living that keep the forest at the centre. Some came from conversations with people, others from naturalists and researchers, and many from simply observing the fascinating relationships that exist within these landscapes.
ALSO WATCH Watch: A day at Baralikadu: Coracles, tribal food and community-led tourism
There are smaller objects like magnets and key-chains to large-scale sculptures and interactive installations | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Each of these stories became a starting point. Over the years, they have experimented with different forms, from smaller objects like magnets and key-chains to large-scale sculptures and interactive installations.

The use of invasive vegetation as a raw material also creates an opportunity to build livelihoods around craft, while taking the story of forest restoration to audiences beyond the region. The Elephant People’s work builds on the experience of The Real Elephant Collective, known for its life-size elephant sculptures made using lantana.

articles.title: Andhra’s revenue rises 18.7% to ₹74,342 crore; Naidu asks officials to raise more without burdening people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State has achieved 58% of its annual own-revenue target of ₹1,27,506 crore, officials tell the Chief Minister

Andhra Pradesh’s own revenue increased by 18.7% to ₹74,342 crore as on November 23 in the 2026-27 financial year, registering an additional collection of ₹11,738 crore compared with the corresponding period last year.

The State has achieved 58% of its annual own-revenue target of ₹1,27,506 crore, officials told Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu during a review meeting on revenue-generating departments on Wednesday (November 25, 2026).

Mr. Naidu asked officials to improve government revenues without imposing an additional tax burden on people or increasing existing charges. Administrative reforms, transparency, online services and measures to plug revenue leakages had begun yielding results over the past two-and-a-half years. The departments should focus on improving revenue collections every week, analyse the performance and make necessary corrections to achieve better results. All departments should use artificial intelligence (AI) and a dedicated AI stack to identify revenue leakages and improve collections, he said.

ప్రభుత్వానికి ఆదాయం సమకూర్చే శాఖలపై గౌరవ ముఖ్యమంత్రి శ్రీ నారా చంద్రబాబునాయుడు నేడు ఉన్నత స్థాయి సమీక్ష నిర్వహించారు. ఈ సమావేశానికి రాష్ట్ర ప్రభుత్వ ప్రధాన కార్యదర్శి శ్రీ సాయి ప్రసాద్, ఆర్ధిక, రెవెన్యూ, ఎక్సైజ్, స్టాంపులు రిజిస్ట్రేషన్లు, గనులు, రవాణా, పురపాలక, పంచాయితీరాజ్ శాఖల ఉన్నతాధికారులు హాజరయ్యారు. ప్రభుత్వం తీసుకున్న చర్యల ద్వారా లీకేజీలు తగ్గడం, వ్యవస్థీకృత లోపాలను సరిదిద్దడంతో ఆయా శాఖల్లో మెరుగైన ఫలితాలు వచ్చాయని ఈ సందర్భంగా సీఎం తెలిపారు. రాష్ట్రంలో వివిధ ప్రాంతాల్లో జరుగుతున్న అభివృద్ధి కార్యక్రమాల ఫలితాలు ఆదాయంలో ప్రతిఫలించాలని, పన్నుల భారం లేకుండా, కొత్తగా ఛార్జీలు పెంచకుండా వివిధ ప్రభుత్వ శాఖల్లో ఆదాయం పెంచేందుకు కృషి చేయాలని అధికారులను ఆదేశించారు. #AndhraPradesh

Calling for coordinated use of the State's data lake to analyse information across departments and identify gaps in revenue mobilisation, he set March 2027 as the deadline for achieving complete improvements in the functioning of revenue-generating systems.

Mr. Naidu asked departments, including Commercial Taxes, Excise, Mines, Stamps and Registration, Municipal Administration, Panchayat Raj and Forests, to adopt technology-driven monitoring mechanisms. Revenue growth should be tracked continuously from the constituency level to the State level, he said.

The Chief Minister also asked the Stamps and Registration Department to study land market values and registration charges, while directing the Excise Department to ensure end-to-end tracking of liquor from manufacturing to retail sales. The Transport Department was asked to electronically monitor vehicle loads, e-way bills and other relevant parameters.

Officials said tax revenue had increased from ₹53,692 crore during the corresponding period last year to ₹63,796 crore this year, generating an additional ₹10,104 crore. Tax revenue grew by 18.8%, while non-tax revenue registered a growth of 31.3%.
Commercial Taxes revenue rose by 18.3% to ₹38,241 crore, an increase of ₹5,917 crore. GST collections grew by 18.1% to ₹24,073 crore, generating an additional ₹3,694 crore.
Excise revenue increased by ₹3,287 crore, or 19.6%, to ₹20,083 crore. Stamps and Registration revenue rose by 16.6% to ₹8,020 crore, while vehicle tax collections increased by 17.3% to ₹3,649 crore.
The Mines and Geology Department recorded 13.2% growth, with revenue reaching ₹2,086 crore. Forest revenue increased by 22.3% to ₹22 crore. Non-tax revenue rose from ₹1,330 crore to ₹2,091 crore.
Officials said gram panchayats had collected about ₹239 crore in taxes between April 1 and November 20, while urban local bodies had mobilised around ₹2,366 crore during the same period.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Officials said gram panchayats had collected about ₹239 crore in taxes between April 1 and November 20, while urban local bodies had mobilised around ₹2,366 crore during the same period.

articles.title: Andhra CM calls for report on illegal sand mining, damage to drinking water pipeline in Kadapa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Following the directive, District Collector informs CMO the action taken against those involved in the illegal activity and measures initiated to prevent recurrence of such incidents

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought a report on the alleged illegal sand mining in the Penna river in Proddatur mandal of Kadapa district and the damage caused to a drinking water pipeline during the activity.
Taking note of media reports on the incident on Wednesday, Mr. Naidu directed the officials to immediately submit a comprehensive explanation.
Following the instructions, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) sought a report from the Kadapa district administration.

The CMO said the government viewed the alleged illegal mining and damage to a public drinking water pipeline seriously. It directed the District Collector to ensure that those involved in illegal mining or causing damage to government property were not spared.

In his report to the CMO, the Collector said the village panchayat secretary had alerted the police after detecting illegal sand mining near Somulavaripalli. Officials immediately intervened and stopped both the mining activity and transportation of sand, the Collector said.

A police complaint was lodged, providing details of the tractors used for illegal transportation of sand, their owners and others allegedly involved in the offence. An FIR was registered and investigation was under way, the Collector said.

Cases under stringent sections were registered against those responsible for damaging the drinking water pipeline and the tractor owners. Repairs to the damaged pipeline were completed on a war-footing and water supply was restored, he added.

The Collector said the district administration had initiated measures to prevent recurrence of such incidents. Special check-posts were established along the Penna and Chitravathi rivers to curb illegal sand mining and transportation.

District and mandal-level committees were also constituted to monitor mining activities. Village panchayat secretaries and tahsildars of the mandals concerned were instructed to coordinate and prevent illegal transportation through the check-posts, the Collector said, adding that continuous surveillance was arranged along the Penna river.

articles.title: AIMIM MLA Akhtarul Iman sparks row with sexist remarks on Muslim women
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: I ask you to refrain from attending weddings where you cannot even differentiate whether a person is Jamila or Sita, he said
All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul-Muslimeen (AIMIM) Bihar president and MLA Akhtarul Iman triggered a controversy after a video of him making sexist remarks went viral on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

“Even a tawaif (courtesan) does not sit as decked out and adorned as the bride. Have you no shame, groom? And you, the groom’s father — have you no shame either? Other people are staring at your daughter-in-law; don’t you have any shame? This is the characteristic behaviour of a pig, who invites another male to join him with his female,” said the MLA, who represents the Amour constituency , in the video.

Mr. Iman made the remarks at a religious gathering in Saharsa on Monday (November 23, 2026). He also questioned traditions within the Muslim community, such as muh-dikhai (the ritual of unveiling the bride’s face), the acceptance of gifts during walima (wedding receptions), and excessive spending.

“On one hand, a daughter wears a burqa after marriage, yet on the other, 16-year-old girls walk around with their hair wide open. I ask you to refrain from attending weddings where you cannot even differentiate whether a person is Jamila or Sita,” he said.
The AIMIM MLA said while the number of people in society wearing the topi (skullcap) has increased, the dupatta (headscarf) has slipped not only from daughters’ heads but also from their chests.

He added that someone is often tasked with sitting down with pen and paper to record money received from guests, describing this as social posturing and an unnecessary tradition, and urged people to rethink these practices.

The Bihar State Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance of the matter and served him a show-cause notice asking for a reply within a week. Commission member Sajal Jha said he has no right to dictate what women should or should not do, adding that his language is insulting to all women, irrespective of caste or religion.
Bihar BJP media coordinator Danish Iqbal strongly opposed the AIMIM MLA’s statement, saying such remarks cannot be tolerated in India.
“Those who wish to adopt Sharia in place of the Constitution have the option to go to countries like Afghanistan or Pakistan; they are free to leave India and move there,” Mr. Iqbal said.

When The Hindu asked him about his derogatory remarks, Mr. Iman said he had not insulted anyone and had only blamed the groom and the father-in-law, adding that people were making an issue out of nothing.

“India is guided by the Constitution and Islam is guided by the Quran and Sharia. Among Muslims, we have the purdah system. I respect the way Hindu women use sindoor; at the same time, Muslim women wearing the hijab should also be respected. When Hindu men remove the hijab of Muslim women, we criticise it, so it is my duty to criticise those Muslims who are themselves removing the hijab of their sisters and daughters. I have not compared our daughters with anyone. It was just a reference for context. For instance, when we say someone is the son of a lion, it does not mean he is the offspring of an animal,” Mr. Iman said.

“I never want to suppress our sisters and daughters. In fact, I am helping open a school for girls. I was telling them to act like daughters and not turn themselves into a source of public amusement; daughters are a family’s honour. If a son goes rogue, the family’s reputation is not ruined; however, if a daughter runs away with someone, it brings disgrace upon the entire family,” he added.

articles.title: No tampering, violation found at Sheshnag lake: J&K Minister Altaf Kaloo
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The BRO has not done anything to the lake. The viral video is misleading, as there is a gap of 200-300 ft. between the [pilgrim] track and the lake,’ says J&K Forest Minister Altaf Kaloo

Responding to a viral video that purportedly showed damage caused during an inspection of Sheshnag Lake in Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir Forest Minister Altaf Kaloo said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) that a 12-member team of officials had inspected the high-altitude lake and “found no tampering or violations” at the site.

“A team was sent to the spot yesterday [Tuesday] on the directions of the Chief Minister. Later, I was apprised by officials that Sheshnag lake is completely safe. The BRO [Border Roads Organisation] has not done anything to the lake. The viral video is misleading, as there is a gap of 200-300 ft. between the [pilgrim] track and the lake. No tampering has been done. Not a speck of earth has fallen into the lake. It is a sacred, religious place for Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs,” Mr. Kaloo said.

The Minister referred to the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by the Omar Abdullah government and the BRO’s Project Beacon in 2025 on the Amarnath route. “An unfortunate eventuality occurred in 2012, and the Supreme Court, while taking cognisance [of it], ordered a 12-ft. track. The current track is in accordance with the SC’s ruling,” he said.

The track underwent a maintenance drive in 2022 after the yatra was over, he said. “The drive is meant to fix broken tiles and edges. We are checking all the parameters of the MoU to ensure they are followed. I wanted to visit the lake but could not because of security reasons. I was told that there was no security ahead,” Mr. Kaloo said.

The team that visited the spot included officials from Environment, Ecology, and Territorial Forests divisions, and the Forest Protection Force, he said. The People’s Democratic Party (PDP) and the BJP were making “a mountain out of a molehill to create an issue for the Uttar Pradesh elections”, the Minister said.

Another leader and legislator of the ruling National Conference (NC), Tanvir Sadiq, said the Omar Abdullah government “will not allow any deviation in the Sheshnag road project and will not allow anyone to play with the environment”. Mr. Abdullah had ordered an environmental assessment of the Sheshnag road project, and assured action in case of any violations, Mr. Sadiq said.

“This project started in 2022. In 2022, the plan was made; in 2023, the MoU was signed; and in 2024, the SC gave its approval. After the 2024 approval, the work started. Where was Mehbooba Mufti sahiba in 2022, 2023, and 2024? Did she not have shoes to go trekking to see this?” Mr. Sadiq said, responding to PDP president Mehbooba Mufti’s allegations on the J&K government signing an MoU with the BRO.
This was a deliberate plan of the BJP and the PDP “to show the whole country that Muslims are against it so that the BJP can sell it not only in Jammu but also in the U.P. elections”, Mr. Sadiq said.
The J&K government was aware of the “importance of the environment and will not allow anyone to play with it”, Mr. Sadiq said.
“At the same time, it will not allow these people to play the Hindu-Muslim card again,” he added.

Ms. Mufti, who was stopped from travelling to Sheshnag on November 24, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said she was “shocked” that on January 23, 2026, the Omar Abdullah-led J&K Cabinet had cleared the road to Sheshnag by extending an MoU with the BRO’s Project Beacon. “In the name of development, it is an assault on our fragile ecology, putting both the Sheshnag ecosystem and the Amarnath Yatra at risk,” Ms. Mufti said.
NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar, however, ruled out the construction of any road on the Amarnath route.

articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.
Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.
Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions

Bangladesh beefed up security across several districts, deploying 108 platoons of border paramilitary forces, including 56 in exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's home district, Gopalganj, as political tensions mount over her planned return next month.

There have been incidents of violence, including arson attacks targeting trains, buses and banks, across Bangladesh in the last many days surrounding the 79-year-old politician's possible return. Ms. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
Police blamed activists of Awami League and its affiliated organisations for several of the incidents.

The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions.

In a press statement on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) announced the deployment of 108 platoons in seven districts "to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and deal with any untoward situation", news portal bdnews24.com reported.
Of them, 56 platoons have been deployed in Gopalganj amid persistent unrest, the BGB said.

Gopalganj, a stronghold of the Awami League, has witnessed incidents of violence, arson and vandalism in recent days. Around 2,000 police personnel and 10 BGB platoons, along with personnel of the Special Response Battalion (SRB), were deployed in the district last week.
According to the BGB statement, 18 platoons have been deployed in Dhaka, six in Narayanganj, 18 in Gazipur, two in Mymensingh, three in Chattogram and one in Cox's Bazar districts.
"In addition, four platoons of BGB members have been kept on alert for deployment," it said.

The deployment has been made on the instructions of the Home Ministry, with BGB personnel coordinating with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.
Security has been strengthened at key installations, industrial zones and other sensitive locations.
The BGB headquarters is monitoring the situation round the clock through a dedicated monitoring cell, using live footage from drones, body cameras and other surveillance equipment.

articles.title: Execution of proclamation orders against Hafiz Saeed, five other 26/11 accused still awaited
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year; the court is currently conducting the trial against handler Abu Jundal

While the trial in the 26/11 terror attacks is on against Zabiuddin Ansari alias Abu Jundal, the handler who taught the 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists Hindi, steps to execute the proclamation orders against six other perpetrators, including Lashkar operatives Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, are yet to be taken.
A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year. The court is currently conducting the trial against Jundal.

In August and September this year, the prosecution told the court that it had requested the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to serve the proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks case. However, the MHA has not responded to the request yet.

Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said that while there has been no development regarding the execution of the proclamation orders issued against the wanted accused, he assured that the perpetrators of the attacks would be punished in India.
"The prosecution will ensure that all those persons who facilitated the dastardly attacks would be punished on Indian soil," Mr. Nikam told PTI .

He said, as per procedure, non-bailable warrants and Interpol Red Corner notices were issued through diplomatic channels against the absconding accused, who are the main perpetrators and conspirators behind the attacks.
"But I am sure that the Pakistan government will not respond as that country continues to be a haven for terrorists," Mr. Nikam said.

The prosecution had in August and September told the court that the MHA was requested to take necessary steps to serve the proclamation orders, through Interpol, against the accused believed to be residing in Pakistan.

Mr. Nikam had then told the court that amid the procedural compliance, the trial against the absconding accused would commence as Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 allows criminal trials in absentia for absconding proclaimed offenders, even where there is no immediate prospect of arrest.

The trial against Jundal, which had been on hold since 2018 pending a petition filed by government authorities over the furnishing of certain documents to the accused, commenced in November last year after clearance from the Bombay High Court.

Jundal is accused of not only having planned the attacks but also of personally training the 10 Pakistani terrorists who struck Mumbai on November 26, 2008, specifically teaching them Hindi and crucial details about Mumbai's topography to help them blend in.

"But I am sure that the Pakistan government will not respond as that country continues to be a haven for terrorists," Mr. Nikam said.

The prosecution had in August and September told the court that the MHA was requested to take necessary steps to serve the proclamation orders, through Interpol, against the accused believed to be residing in Pakistan.

Mr. Nikam had then told the court that amid the procedural compliance, the trial against the absconding accused would commence as Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 allows criminal trials in absentia for absconding proclaimed offenders, even where there is no immediate prospect of arrest.

The trial against Jundal, which had been on hold since 2018 pending a petition filed by government authorities over the furnishing of certain documents to the accused, commenced in November last year after clearance from the Bombay High Court.

Jundal is accused of not only having planned the attacks but also of personally training the 10 Pakistani terrorists who struck Mumbai on November 26, 2008, specifically teaching them Hindi and crucial details about Mumbai's topography to help them blend in.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While the trial in the 26/11 terror attacks is on against Zabiuddin Ansari alias Abu Jundal, the handler who taught the 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists Hindi, steps to execute the proclamation orders against six other perpetrators, including Lashkar operatives Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, are yet to be taken.

articles.title: U.S. set to slap tariffs on China, EU and others after probe on excess industrial capacity: report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India was also named among 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners; Together, the duties are meant to ​rebuild Trump’s global “Liberation Day” tariffs that were struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February

The Trump administration is poised ​to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected.

The results of the investigation are expected as soon, these people said. The U.S. Trade Representative’s office is expected to propose ‌new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during President Donald Trump’s second term.

The duties would partly replace tariffs struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. The administration’s tariffs have in part ‌contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November’s midterm elections ‌showed ⁠62% of respondents would support efforts to repeal the tariffs.

It is unclear what tariff rates ⁠would be proposed. One of the people said that the duties would be specifically tailored to each country, with goods from Mexico and Norway unlikely to see any immediate levies.
USTR has been investigating most of the US’s largest trading partners under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 over what it called ​evidence of excess industrial capacity.

The White House is ‌expected to honor capped tariff rates that were included in finalized US trade deals with partner countries, this person said. These include duty caps of 15% on goods from the EU, Japan and South Korea and 19% for Malaysia.

The U.S. also is expected to honor the 20% cap on Trump’s second-term tariffs on goods from China, as long as a ‌trade truce due to expire on January 10 is extended. If it expires, the Chinese excess capacity rate would ​rise to a higher level.
The U.S. Trade Representative’s office and the White House did not respond to Reuters queries about the pending announcement.
Ryan Majerus, a former senior Commerce Department trade official, said he ⁠expects a lengthy report that could include differentiated tariff remedies for each of the 16 trading partners.

Majerus, a partner with King & Spalding, said the administration could propose high tariff rates of 15% to 25% on imports from countries deemed to have excess capacity in various sectors. ‌Those levies would stack on top of existing tariffs of 10% or 12.5% imposed under a separate investigation into lax enforcement of anti-forced labor laws.

However, he said the administration could also propose lower tariff rates with escalation clauses that would ratchet rates higher over time unless countries take steps to reduce excess production capacity.

The countries included in the probe are China, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia, along with the European Union.

articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after historic outage, internal memos show
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The November 12-13 outage ​hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms ⁠and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure

Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” drive to ​overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures after a 24-hour outage exposed shortcomings in its engineering ‌systems and crisis response, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters.

The November 12-13 outage ​hit governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms ⁠and disrupted airline communications, fueling broader concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.
Microsoft blamed the outage on an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. CEO ‌Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption.

The Code Red signified the most severe and urgent alert to address weaknesses in Microsoft’s engineering and operational practices after the outage disrupted ‌Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and ‌other ⁠Microsoft 365 products.
It was the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online, ⁠M365 Core President Jason Henderson said in a memo to staff on Friday.
Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson added.
Job cuts, retirement plan, voluntary exits: What’s going on at Microsoft?
Microsoft says services fully restored after hourslong global outage
Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact

Amanda ​Silver, Microsoft’s corporate vice president overseeing M365 ‌Core and Work IQ, the company’s workplace intelligence platform for AI agents, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers had to work through a “fog of war” as the outage unfolded.

Despite deploying top engineering personnel, responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats and struggled to maintain ‌a cohesive picture of hypotheses and decisions because diagnostic data was scattered across fragmented internal ​tracking systems, Silver said.

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth ⁠of acceptable failures,” according to Silver’s memo.

articles.title: Air pollution accelerates dementia by reprogramming brain's immune cells: study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third
Air pollution helps cause dementia by changing the genes that are switched on in microglia, the brain's immune cells, in ways that disrupt their normal functions, a new study has found.
The study, published in the Journal of Neuroinflammation , combined health records from nearly half a million people from the UK Biobank with experiments in mouse models.

"By recreating in mice what happens when people breath polluted air, we found that pollution causes major changes in which genes are active in the brain's immune cells," senior author Sanjay Rajagopalan, professor of medicine and director of the Cardiovascular Research Institute at the Case Western Reserve University's school of medicine, said.

"These cells normally keep the brain healthy by clearing away debris and fighting infection. Seeing how pollution disrupts them helps explain how a stress that affects much of the world's population harms the brain, and it points us toward a way to treat it," Rajagopalan said.

Mice were exposed to outdoor Cleveland (US) air for five months. The fine particles in the air, known as particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), were concentrated to levels similar to those found in the world's most polluted cities.

Otherwise healthy mice developed memory problems, a leaky blood-brain barrier and brain inflammation. Their brains also showed a lower chemical balance reflecting its energy status and ability to withstand injury and disease.
The mice's brains also showed an increased death of newborn neurons in the hippocampus, the brain's centre for learning and memory.
The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third.
Further, in mice genetically prone to Alzheimer's, air pollution caused the same harm and also sped up amyloid plaque buildup -- a hallmark of the neurodegenerative disease.

The authors wrote: "These population-scale data in humans and experimental data in mice​ support PM2.5 as an environmental neurotoxicant and define microglial regulatory programs through which genetic background shapes the biological response to a common and modifiable exposure."

"We've identified a key way that air pollution harms the healthy brain and speeds up Alzheimer's disease," co-senior author Andrew Pieper, professor in translational psychiatry at Case Western Reserve University, said.

"This helps us understand how factors in our environment can accelerate and intensify brain diseases of aging. It also opens the door to studying other environmental stresses on the brain, and to finding ways to keep the brain resilient even when we can't avoid those stressors," Pieper said.

articles.title: Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing.
The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar

The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands.

Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on.
The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar

The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey.

This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite.

Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.”
Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.
File photo of little stints and kentish plovers | Photo Credit: PRINCE FREDERICK

For more than four decades, researchers have been monitoring shorebird populations in the Gulf of Mannar region. “The numbers have fallen by 60 percent across the monitored shorebird population . The mudflats are not merely places to pause, they are feeding stations where the birds replenish the energy needed for their onward journeys. When these habitats disappear, there is no easy alternative,” says Sivakumar.

articles.title: ₹300-crore Bhadrachalam temple development works under way, structures designed to last 200 years: Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said development works at the historic Sri Sitaramachandra Swamy temple in Bhadrachalam are being undertaken at a cost of ₹300 crore, with the structures designed to last for 200 years and be appreciated by future generations.

The works are part of the development of temples located along the Godavari riverbanks under the temple corridor from Basar to Bhadrachalam, in preparation for the Godavari Pushkaralu-2027, at an estimated cost of ₹1,100 crore, he said.

The Minister reviewed the temple development works in Bhadrachalam on Wednesday. He inspected the concrete construction works being undertaken from Dammakka Annadana Satram to the stairway, as well as the works surrounding the main temple.
He also held a review meeting with officials at the Sub-Collector’s office in the temple town.
Later, speaking to reporters, he said the major development works would be completed by December 19, 2026, on the occasion of Mukkoti Ekadasi, ensuring that devotees would not face any inconvenience.
Stating that the slab construction works had been completed, the Minister said the Cabinet sub-committee was reviewing the progress of the works once every fortnight.

He said Bhadrachalam was expected to attract more than one crore pilgrims during the Godavari Pushkaralu-2027 and that all arrangements were being planned accordingly to ensure the smooth conduct of the mega religious event.
The Minister also undertook an extensive tour of the Bhadrachalam Agency, inaugurating and laying foundation stones for various development works in Bhadrachalam, Charla and Dummugudem mandals.
He laid the foundation stones for a Ground-Level Service Reservior (GLSR) at Ranganayakula Gutta and a tribal multi-purpose market on the premises of the Agriculture Market Yard in Bhadrachalam.

Later, he inaugurated additional classrooms at the Ashram School in Narayanaraopeta village and laid the foundation stone for an Overhead Service Reservoir (OHSR) at Parnashala Ghat in Dummugudem mandal.
In Charla mandal, he inaugurated internal cement concrete roads in Kudunuru and Devarapalli villages and laid the foundation stone for a new dormitory building at the Tribal Girls’ Hostel in Charla.

articles.title: Moderate rain likely for two days in State
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Trough brings rain to several parts of the State with highest of 45.3 mm recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district
South Coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded moderate showers on Wednesday due to a trough extending from the Gulf of Mannar to the southwest Bay of Bengal.

As of 3 p.m., the highest rainfall of 45.3 mm was recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district, followed by 41.5 mm at Allampadu in Nellore district. Other areas that received rainfall included Gudur (32.7 mm), Vakadu in Tirupati district (32.5 mm), Vidavalur in Nellore district (32 mm), Pennepalle in Tirupati district (30 mm), Molakalapundla in Nellore district (28 mm), Nellore (23.2 mm) and Bhimavaram (22.7 mm).
Light to moderate rainfall, accompanied by lightning, may continue for the next two days, according to the India Meteorological Department.

On Thursday, light to moderate rainfall is likely at isolated places in Polavaram, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati districts. Scattered light rainfall is also expected in other districts.

articles.title: Akbaruddin Owaisi questions low spending, high dropouts in minority schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi on Wednesday flagged low utilisation of funds by the Minorities Welfare Department, shortfall in minority student enrolment in welfare schools and delays in processing overseas scholarship applications, even as he called for corrective measures to address the gaps.

Raising these concerns at a meeting of the Joint Committee for Welfare of Minorities in the Legislative Assembly, Mr. Owaisi questioned why admissions of students from minority communities in schools run by the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGMREIS) were falling short of the prescribed quota.

The Society has reserved 75% of seats for students from minority communities and 25% for others. However, of the approximately 85,000 students enrolled, around 56,000 belonged to minority communities and 29,000 to non-minority communities, accounting for about 66% and 34%, respectively. He expressed concern over the shortfall in minority enrolment and the high dropout rate, and called for systematic measures to address the issue.

To check dropouts, Mr. Owaisi suggested that the State government introduce its own pre-matric scholarship scheme, irrespective of the Centre’s decision to discontinue its scheme. He also proposed using data from the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) to analyse dropout rates and identify the reasons behind them.

While welcoming the proposed constitution of a Sikh Minority Finance Corporation, a promise in the Congress’s Minority Declaration ahead of the Assembly elections, he pointed out that a Christian Minorities Finance Corporation was already in existence. He suggested renaming the State Minorities Finance Corporation as the Muslim Finance Corporation.

On the Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship Scheme, Mr. Owaisi questioned the delay in verifying applications and sought clarity on the pending reimbursement of tuition fees and maintenance of tuition fees. The outstanding dues for the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26 stood at ₹1,273 crore. Asking who would bear the financial burden, he cautioned that students would ultimately suffer.
He also expressed concern over the department’s low fund utilisation. Against a budgetary allocation of ₹3,768 crore, the Minorities Welfare Department had spent only around ₹1,013 crore, he said.

The department and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned strength of 6,986 employees, but only 4,028 posts were filled. Mr. Owaisi said the large number of vacancies could affect the department’s efficiency and delivery of services.

He stated that the MWD and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned cadre strength of 6,986, but pointed out that only 4,028 were working, and indicated that the yawning gap in vacancies was a matter of concern, especially as regards the efficiency of the department, and service delivery.

Akbaruddin Owaisi questions low spending, high dropouts in minority schools

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi on Wednesday flagged low utilisation of funds by the Minorities Welfare Department, shortfall in minority student enrolment in welfare schools and delays in processing overseas scholarship applications, even as he called for corrective measures to address the gaps.

Raising these concerns at a meeting of the Joint Committee for Welfare of Minorities in the Legislative Assembly, Mr. Owaisi questioned why admissions of students from minority communities in schools run by the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGMREIS) were falling short of the prescribed quota.

The Society has reserved 75% of seats for students from minority communities and 25% for others. However, of the approximately 85,000 students enrolled, around 56,000 belonged to minority communities and 29,000 to non-minority communities, accounting for about 66% and 34%, respectively. He expressed concern over the shortfall in minority enrolment and the high dropout rate, and called for systematic measures to address the issue.

To check dropouts, Mr. Owaisi suggested that the State government introduce its own pre-matric scholarship scheme, irrespective of the Centre’s decision to discontinue its scheme. He also proposed using data from the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) to analyse dropout rates and identify the reasons behind them.

While welcoming the proposed constitution of a Sikh Minority Finance Corporation, a promise in the Congress’s Minority Declaration ahead of the Assembly elections, he pointed out that a Christian Minorities Finance Corporation was already in existence. He suggested renaming the State Minorities Finance Corporation as the Muslim Finance Corporation.

On the Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship Scheme, Mr. Owaisi questioned the delay in verifying applications and sought clarity on the pending reimbursement of tuition fees and maintenance of tuition fees. The outstanding dues for the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26 stood at ₹1,273 crore. Asking who would bear the financial burden, he cautioned that students would ultimately suffer.

He also expressed concern over the department’s low fund utilisation. Against a budgetary allocation of ₹3,768 crore, the Minorities Welfare Department had spent only around ₹1,013 crore, he said.

The department and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned strength of 6,986 employees, but only 4,028 posts were filled. Mr. Owaisi said the large number of vacancies could affect the department’s efficiency and delivery of services.

He stated that the MWD and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned cadre strength of 6,986, but pointed out that only 4,028 were working, and indicated that the yawning gap in vacancies was a matter of concern, especially as regards the efficiency of the department, and service delivery.

3. articles.title: Permission denied for staging of controversial play Gandhi Hatyeya Satya in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Department of Kannada and Culture has denied permission for staging the controversial play Gandhi Hatyeya Satya at Kirurangamandira, located within the Kalamandira premises in Mysuru, on Thursday.

The denial has been attributed to the Mysuru City Police’s inability to provide adequate security for the performance, as elaborate arrangements have to be made for the Constitution Day celebrations scheduled to be held on the same day.

In a letter to former Rangayana Director Addanda C. Cariappa, who is staging the play, Assistant Director of the Department of Kannada and Culture, Mysuru, M.D. Sudarshan said permission would be granted only if Mr. Cariappa obtained written clearance from the police department confirming that adequate security arrangements had been made.

Mr. Sudarshan also referred to the Karnataka High Court’s order in this regard and said the police department must confirm adequate security arrangements to ensure that the performance takes place peacefully without any untoward incidents or disruption to law and order.

Around 1.5 lakh people are expected to attend the Constitution Day celebrations at Maharaja’s College grounds, where Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, his Cabinet colleagues and other dignitaries are scheduled to participate. Another Constitution Day programme is scheduled to be held at the Convocation Hall of Karnataka State Open University (KSOU) the same evening.

Earlier in the day, a delegation of Congress leaders led by Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) spokesperson M. Lakshmana met City Police Commissioner N. Vishnuvardhan and urged him to register a case against playwright Addanda C. Cariappa, alleging that the play denigrated Mahatma Gandhi.

In a memorandum submitted to the Police Commissioner, Mr. Lakshmana, along with Mysuru City Congress president R. Murthy and Mysuru Rural District Congress president Beerihundi Basavanna, alleged that several passages in the play went “beyond the scope of creative expression” and contained unsubstantiated allegations attributed to real historical personalities.

The memorandum alleged that the work also contains provocative content concerning religious communities and attributes specific statements about Mahatma Gandhi and other national leaders to a figure like Nathuram Godse.

Pointing out that the author had described the work as an attempt to bring the “hidden truths of history” before the public, the Congress leaders sought an investigation into whether the claims presented as historical facts were supported by original documents and credible references.

They urged the police to register an FIR and conduct a thorough investigation, besides initiating action against the author if it was established that false or fabricated statements had been deliberately published and presented to the public as historical facts through the play.

3. articles.title: U.S. announces new 25% tariffs on India, second-highest among 14 countries against whom action was taken
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The order by the U.S. Trade Representative also opens the door for a lower 17% tariff if India and the U.S. sign a trade deal

The U.S. government on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) announced a tariff of 25% on goods imported from India in response to India’s “unreasonable acts, policies, and practices” that “burden or restrict U.S. commerce”. This is the second-highest tariff among the 14 economies on which the latest action has been taken, second only to the 35% tariff levied on Vietnam.
However, the order by the office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) also said that, should the U.S. and India reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, the tariff on India could drop to 17%.
ALSO WATCH U.S. midterm results could accelerate India trade deal but raise tariff risks

Further, while it says that the 25% tariffs would be net of existing tariffs levied on India, meaning they will not add to the 10% already in effect, the order also said that it remained for the USTR to decide whether these new tariffs will be adjusted keeping in mind those other tariffs.
The Hindu has reached out to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry for a comment, and this report will be updated when one is received.

The USTR had in March launched two separate investigations into American trade partners, including India, under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act. The first investigation related to forced labour resulted in a tariff of 10% on India. The new tariffs announced on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) are a result of the second investigation into structural excess capacity.

Apart from this, the U.S. also levies a tariff of 50% on imports of aluminium and steel from all countries under Section 232 of its Trade Expansion Act. The new tariffs will not be added to these. Under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, the U.S. government is also empowered to levy a tariff of up to 100% on countries like India that import large quantities of Russian oil. This tariff has been temporarily paused by U.S. President Donald Trump.

In its report on India, the USTR concluded that India’s acts, policies, and practices “create, sustain, or contribute to structural excess capacity” that burden or restrict U.S. commerce by harming U.S. producers and exporters through unfair competition and reduced commercial opportunities, harm the U.S. economy due to lost exports, trade deficits, and a diminished manufacturing sector, and create economic security risks for the U.S.

“The Trade Representative proposes that appropriate action to obtain the elimination of the acts, policies, and practices would include applying tariffs of up to 25% on all goods of India, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods,” the order by the USTR said.

However, the order also says that the USTR further proposes to consider whether the additional duties applied should be adjusted to account for duties applied under other existing Section 301 actions, duties applied under Section 232, “or were India to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the United States that is responsive to the determinations in this investigation into the acts, policies, and practices of India, a tariff rate of 17%”.

The 25% tariffs are higher than those levied on Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan, the European Union (15% each), Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand (18% each), Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, and Singapore (up to 20% each).
Only Vietnam faces a tariff of 35%, higher than that for India, but even that stands to be reduced to 20% if it signs a trade deal with the U.S.

articles.title: Over 17,700 units of blood collected in Karnataka-wide drive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State Health Department, in association with the KSBTC, organised the drive, with the main programme held at Koramangala Indoor Stadium in Bengaluru

As many as 17,778 units of blood were collected from 21,150 voluntary donors at 270 blood centres across Karnataka on Wednesday as part of a State-wide blood donation drive organised to mark National Voluntary Blood Donation Day.

The State Health Department, in association with the Karnataka State Blood Transfusion Council (KSBTC), organised the drive, with the main programme held at Koramangala Indoor Stadium in Bengaluru. Health Minister U.T. Khader, who inaugurated the programme, also donated blood.

Of the total collection, 3,120 units were collected at the mega camp in Bengaluru, where around 3,500 donors participated. The camp was organised in collaboration with 25 government and private blood centres, including Bengaluru Blood Centre, Shushruta Blood Centre, Lions Blood Centre, the Indian Red Cross Society, Rotary TTK and K.C. General Hospital.
Simultaneous camps were held in all districts and at selected taluk-level centres in coordination with district administrations and the Health Department.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Khader described voluntary blood donation as a vital humanitarian service, noting that blood could not be manufactured and had to be sourced through voluntary donations. He called upon young people, students, educational institutions, government and private organisations, IT companies and NGOs to promote a culture of regular blood donation.

He stressed the need to ensure timely availability of safe blood for accident victims, patients undergoing major surgeries, women requiring transfusions during childbirth, children with thalassaemia and other blood disorders, and those being treated for serious illnesses. No patient should be denied treatment because of the non-availability of blood, he said.
Fifty regular voluntary donors, including two from each participating blood centre, were felicitated at the programme.

The Minister appreciated the efforts of the KSBTC, participating blood centres and Health Department officials and staff. He urged district health officials and blood centre heads to continue awareness and donor mobilisation activities.

The department had made arrangements for donor registration, medical screening, safe blood collection, emergency medical services and transportation of collected blood under the prescribed cold-chain system. Participating centres were instructed to follow standard operating procedures to ensure donor safety and maintain the quality of blood collected.

The campaign sought to strengthen the voluntary donor network through educational institutions, the National Service Scheme, the National Cadet Corps, the Indian Red Cross Society, youth organisations, IT companies and community groups. Its slogan was “One Drop of Humanity. Give Blood. Save Lives.”

articles.title: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists

The Election Commission of India on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) directed that any incorrect or erroneous entries flagged in the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR) would be corrected using Form 8 after comparing the entries with the corresponding information collected during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
All the changes would be made after verification by the concerned officials and not through automated matching.
Form 8 is the ECI application for correction in voter details.
The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists.
The directive was given to the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and UTs where the SIR has been completed and SSR is on.

The States and UTs are Andaman and Nicobar Island, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Karnataka and Meghalaya.
The ECI had ordered the SSR of electoral rolls with reference to January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date in these States/UTs through letters on October 15, November 4 and November 11.
