articles.title: After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”.

The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin.

Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said.
The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said.

Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996.

“This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal.

VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)

While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD.

The alliance had won 93 seats in the 1997 Assembly election, with the SAD winning 75 seats and the BJP winning 18 seats. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab’s trend of voting out incumbent governments.

The SAD walked away from the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Badal also resigning her position as Minister in the Modi government at the Centre over the three farm laws that sought to re-engineer agri-commerce, igniting months-long protests on Delhi’s borders. To a question by the media on what the SAD had to say about the farm laws now, Mr. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.

Mr. Modi had pushed for the alliance, for both sentiment and realpolitik, sources in the know said. “The sentiments with regard to the Sikh community, and an alliance of parties appealing to both Hindu and orthodox Sikh panthic support, is important for social harmony in Punjab, and blunts any appeal that Waris Punjab De might have. Repeated surveys also show that an alliance between the two parties would energise cadres,” a senior BJP leader said.
Waris Punjab De is a political outfit founded in 2021 around issues of the political rights of Sikhs, headed by incarcerated Lok Sabha MP Amritpal Singh.

articles.title: Karnataka moves Supreme Court to restrain Tamil Nadu in Cauvery–South Vellar–Vaigai–Gundar Link Project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka argued that Tamil Nadu cannot undertake any work on the CVG Link without clearance from the Union government

The State of Karnataka has moved the Supreme Court seeking a temporary injunction against Tamil Nadu and the Union government with regard to the Cauvery (Kattalai)–South Vellar–Vaigai–Gundar Link Project (CVG Link) and related works for utilising surplus Cauvery waters flowing down from Karnataka.

The application for injunction has been filed in Karnataka’s original suit challenging the legality of the CVG Link, for which Tamil Nadu has sought the Union government’s ‘in-principle approval’, and declaration as a national project on January 5, 2021.

The court had disposed of a similar application in January last year, saying the Centre had not given in-principle approval to the CVG Link, and hence, it was not necessary to consider any interim relief at that point.

The new application filed a few days ago on November 20 submitted that Karnataka happened to come across an order passed by the Madras High Court which extracts a status report of Tamil Nadu stating that work on parts of the first phase of the CVG Link had been “going on since January 21, 2021”.

Karnataka alleged that these facts were not placed before the Supreme Court by Tamil Nadu. Karnataka said that, according to its information, several Phase-I structures have already been completed and land has been acquired for further works.
The State argued that Tamil Nadu cannot undertake any work on the CVG Link without clearance from the Union government. The works, if any, already undertaken by Tamil Nadu were illegal.
Farmers of southern districts disappointed with poor fund allocation for Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar river-linking project

In its application, Karnataka argued that Tamil Nadu has worked out the water for the project from the surpluses at Mettur Dam, placed at about 8.60 TMC at 50% dependability. Karnataka said the unilateral utilisation of surplus waters coming from Karnataka may later be relied upon by Tamil Nadu to claim equities, to the prejudice of Karnataka’s rights in the surplus waters of the Cauvery.

In its application, Karnataka has urged the court to restrain Tamil Nadu from executing the Cauvery–South Vellar Link Project (the first phase of the CVG Link), including the ongoing works, and from taking up any further works under Phase-I, Phase-II and Phase-III.

It has also sought a judicial direction to stop Tamil Nadu from executing or utilising non-Tamil Nadu Cauvery waters under other projects, including diversion of flood waters from Mettur Reservoir to the Sarabanga sub-basin, the New Kattalai Barrage at Mayanur, and barrages and check dams across the Cauvery and Kollidam.

Karnataka has asked the court to intervene and direct the Union government not to process Tamil Nadu’s January 2021 request for in-principle approval, and to refrain from declaring the CVG Link a national project.
Further, the State pressed the court to direct Tamil Nadu to demolish the works already completed in Phase I of the CVG Link.

articles.title: BJP MLA Rekha Patra’s condition improves, legislator remains under observation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rekha Patra is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly

The health condition of BJP MLA Rekha Patra has improved, with her slurred speech reducing considerably, but doctors have kept her in the intensive care unit (ICU) for close observation, hospital sources said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The Hingalganj MLA was taken off ventilator support on Monday (November 23, 2026) and has not required it since. She is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly, BJP leader Archana Das Majumdar said.
However, the three-member medical team treating her is not willing to take any chances and has recommended that she remain in the ICU for continued monitoring.
Hospital sources said she was still receiving supplemental oxygen due to low oxygen levels in her body.
While other clinical parameters indicate a positive recovery, doctors remain concerned about possible complications arising from the poisoning.

Following the suspected poisoning, excessive saliva had accumulated in Ms. Patra's mouth. As she was not fully conscious, some saliva entered her lungs, affecting oxygen supply to the body, an earlier CT scan had found.
Doctors said the effects of impaired oxygen supply to the lungs may not become immediately apparent and could manifest after some delay.

A repeat CT scan of her chest was scheduled for Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon to assess the extent of any lung damage. Her further recovery would depend, among other factors, on the findings of the scan, they said.
Meanwhile, doctors are yet to establish the exact composition of the suspected poison detected in her stomach.
According to the medical team, the substance found in her stomach was described as a herbal larvicide (herbal pesticide), but its precise ingredients remain unknown.
The container of the pesticide, details of which were provided by her family members, did not carry any information about its composition.
In the absence of clarity over the ingredients, doctors at the private hospital are continuing treatment based on the symptoms associated with poisoning.

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government
Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan.

Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.”

Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament.

Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community.

Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began?

With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him.

Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities.

While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto!
One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery.

Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs.
The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

“The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. What do lemurs and opera singers share?

Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began?

With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him.

Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities.

While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto!

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery.

Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs.

The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

“The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. “Every time the pitch of an indri’s song rose, we could see its mouth opening wider, frame by frame,” said Dr De Gregorio. “It’s the kind of fine-tuned coordination between voice and body that we usually associate with trained human singers, not with a lemur singing from the forest canopy.”

This method is called vocal tract tuning (formant or resonance tuning), and it is the deliberate adjustment of the vocal tract’s shape via the jaw, tongue, lips, larynx, and pharynx to align its resonant frequencies with the sound harmonics produced by the vocal folds.

articles.title: Teenager arrested in online fraud case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The boy reportedly acted as an intermediary in an alleged online financial fraud involving bank accounts rented from students at Changaramkulam and nearby areas

The police arrested a teenage boy who reportedly acted as an intermediary in an alleged online financial fraud involving bank accounts rented from students at Changaramkulam and nearby areas. Around a dozen cases were registered in connection with the alleged fraud.

The accused allegedly persuaded students, including his friends and relatives, to allow money to be transferred to their bank accounts. Amounts ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh were deposited into each account. The account holders were paid up to ₹10,000 to withdraw the money and hand it over.

Several students who took part in the transactions without knowing their connection to the alleged fraud are now facing charges in cybercrime cases. The cases could affect their higher education, overseas travel, and prospects of securing government jobs, the police said.

The alleged fraud money was traced to Rajasthan. Following this, a police team from Rajasthan visited Changaramkulam and questioned the suspects. The police at Changaramkulam also registered a first information report (FIR) in connection with the case.

articles.title: Karnataka developing dedicated app for ST welfare schemes, says Raghumurthy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Scheduled Tribes Welfare T. Raghumurthy said in Mysuru on Tuesday that the State government is developing a dedicated mobile application to provide Scheduled Tribe (ST) beneficiaries with real-time information on various welfare schemes and departmental services.

Speaking at a review meeting with district officials at the Mysuru Zilla Panchayat hall, the Minister said the proposed app would bring information on all welfare schemes and facilities under a single digital platform, enabling beneficiaries to access details easily.

The government was also focusing on ensuring that welfare programmes reach all tribal communities, including more than 50 sub-tribes such as Valmiki, Nayaka, Kadu Kuruba, Jenu Kuruba, Soliga and Hakki Pikki, he said.

Referring to his recent visits to tribal hamlets or haadis , Mr. Raghumurthy said several infrastructure gaps and difficulties had come to his notice. He directed officials to take steps to ensure residents received all eligible government facilities.

He instructed officials to conduct targeted surveys in the hamlets and organise special camps to help residents obtain Aadhaar cards and income certificates, which were essential for securing ration cards.

Reviewing the progress of the housing project being implemented through the Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited, the Minister said 100 houses had been sanctioned for tribal hamlets. While 15 houses had been completed, the remaining 85 were under construction.
He assured officials that funds were available and directed them to expedite construction and ensure early completion of the houses.

Anil Chikkamadu, H.D. Kote MLA; G.D. Harish Gowda, Hunsur MLA; M. Ramappa, Karnataka State Bhovi Development Corporation chairman; G. Lakshmikantha Reddy, Deputy Commissioner; S. Yukesh Kumar, Zilla Panchayat CEO; Mallikarjun Baladandi, Superintendent of Police; M.K. Savita, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner; Ashok D.R., ST Welfare Department Director; and Ashok Dudagunti, Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki ST Development Corporation Managing Director were present.

articles.title: Mysuru division gears up for better SSLC, II PU results
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The School Education Department has set its sights on significantly improving SSLC and II PU examination results in the Mysuru division, with officials and resource teachers in four districts directed to work towards securing a place among the State’s top-performing divisions.

Additional Chief Secretary to the Department of School Education and Literacy Rashmi V. Mahesh, who chaired a high-level review meeting and resource teachers’ training workshop in Mysuru on Tuesday, directed officials to identify even the weakest students in classrooms and provide them with special attention to improve their academic performance.

The meeting, held at Vidya Vikas College of Engineering on Bannur Road, reviewed preparations for the 2026-27 SSLC and II PU annual examinations in Mysuru, Mandya, Kodagu and Chamarajanagar districts.

Officials presented details of school-wise preparations and the implementation of various initiatives, including ‘Mission 110 Days’, ‘Kalika Mitra’, ‘Kalika Khathri Parikshe’, ‘Nanna Oduva Samaya’, Mission 60+’ and a series of preparatory examinations.
Interacting with resource teachers, Ms. Mahesh stressed the need for regular writing practice and special remedial teaching classes for students lagging in their studies.

“Examination results are not merely statistics; they open the doors to higher education and shape the future of every child,” she said, urging teachers and officials to focus not just on pass percentages but also on improving the quality of education.

She asked principals and lecturers to motivate every science student to appear for the CET with confidence and make use of the 7.5% special reservation available to students from rural backgrounds who have studied in government schools and colleges for admission to professional courses.
She called upon the four districts to work in a “mission-mode” approach to secure top rankings at the State level.

School Education Commissioner Prabhulingaswamy Kavalikatti, Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board Chairman and Director of Pre-University Education Bharat, Board Director (Examinations) Anita Nazare, Divisional Secretary and ex-officio Joint Director Vivekananda, Deputy Directors of School Education, DIET principals and Block Education Officers of the four districts attended the meeting.
Separate training sessions were conducted for resource teachers in six subjects — Kannada, English, Hindi, Mathematics, Science and Social Science.

Principals of PU colleges were also given specific guidelines on the effective use of blueprints, question banks and model question papers, besides ensuring time-bound writing practice to improve II PU results.

articles.title: DGP inaugurates advanced command centre in Nellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Integrated facility aims to improve crime detection, law and order monitoring and public grievance redressal

Director-General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta inaugurated a state-of-the-art District Integrated Command and Control Centre above the Umesh Chandra Conference Hall at the Police Ground in Nellore on Tuesday. He also inaugurated the new Chinna Bazaar Police Station and participated in the bhoomi puja for the construction of men’s and women’s police barracks, a Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS) Conference Hall and a Road Safety Control Room.

The Command and Control Centre integrates district-wide CCTV cameras, drones, emergency services and police monitoring systems on a single platform. It can monitor live footage from 30 drone cameras simultaneously and is equipped with Artificial Intelligence (AI), Facial Recognition Technology, CCTV 360, the Trinetra App and the LHMS system to identify suspected criminals and suspicious activities.

Mr. Gupta inspected the advanced technological systems at the centre and enquired about their functioning and operational capabilities. He appreciated its role in crime detection, investigation, law and order monitoring, issuing real-time instructions and ensuring the prompt resolution of public grievances.

He lauded the initiative towards technology-driven policing and said steps would be taken to replicate the model in other districts. He said the modern police station would help provide efficient and prompt services to the public. The new building would also offer a better working environment for police personnel, strengthen operational efficiency and promote people-friendly policing.

Superintendent of Police Ajitha Vejendla thanked the DGP for his encouragement and support in establishing the centre with advanced technological facilities. She said the initiative aimed to make policing more transparent, accountable and accessible to the public through technology, effective monitoring and prompt response.

articles.title: Expanded NCD survey in Andhra Pradesh to cover four additional health conditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In addition to the existing five major conditions, obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders are now a part of the exercise conducted every financial year

The Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare has announced that health screenings being conducted in the State under the Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) survey will be expanded to cover four additional health conditions — obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders.
Until now, screening has been conducted for people aged 18 and above for five major health conditions — hypertension, diabetes, oral cancer, breast cancer and cervical cancer.
The health screenings will be conducted every financial year, and the survey for the financial year 2026–27 is expected to begin soon.
“The programme is being expanded, considering changing lifestyles, rising obesity levels and growing risk of other chronic diseases,” a release from the department said on Tuesday.

Participating in a virtual review meeting on the upcoming NCD programme, Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav briefed officials on the proposed changes and the precautions to be taken. “The focus is on identifying these diseases at an early stage before the problem becomes a serious one,” he said.

Under the new survey, individuals who are overweight will be identified at an early stage, and their risk of developing other health complications will be assessed. They will also receive guidance on dietary habits, physical activity and weight management. People with obesity, hypertension, diabetes and thyroid disorders will also be assessed for their risk of developing fatty liver disease.

The survey will also identify those with chronic respiratory conditions at an early stage. Those with symptoms will be examined by medical officers at the Primary Health Centres (PHCs). Patients requiring further investigations will be referred to the regional and district hospitals, where spirometers will be made available to assess lung function.

To assess the mental health condition of an individual, a questionnaire will be prepared, which will include questions to identify symptoms of depression, anxiety, memory-related problems and psychotic disorders.

Individuals identified as being at risk will undergo preliminary telephonic assessments through Tele-MANAS. Those requiring further medical evaluation will be referred to the appropriate healthcare facilities through the District Mental Health Programme.

The Minister directed the officials to adopt a Facial Recognition System (FRS)-based identification mechanism during the upcoming survey, which means biometric details would be collected during the survey for verification.

An Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) ID would be generated for individuals, and their medical records linked to it. Details of screenings, disease diagnosis, treatment and follow-up consultations would be digitally recorded.

articles.title: Lula draws the line amid Trump interference in Brazil’s close and tough election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Lula says ‘Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard’ even as the country’s top intelligence agency raises the risk of U.S. interference in the October 4 elections to a ‘critical level’. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs and sanctions

In an unprecedented move last Wednesday (September 23, 2026), Brazilian President Lula da Silva’s campaign asked the country’s Federal Supreme Court (STF) to “investigate the possible U.S. interference in the country’s electoral process”. Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) also filed a case with the Superior Election Tribunal (TSE) against the far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, seeking a probe into alleged U.S. support for his campaign.

The petitions came the same day as 14 countries belonging to the Shield of the Americas, a group of right-wing Latin American governments assembled by U.S. President Donald Trump, signed a pact designating 24 drug-trafficking groups as “shared threats”. Brazil’s two criminal organisations, First Capital Command (PCC) and Red Command (CV), were among the groups mentioned in the deal. Lula immediately hit back at the decision. “Brazil does not underestimate the challenge posed by organized crime, but it does not intend to outsource the responsibility of protecting its citizens,” the Brazilian leader said in his speech at the United Nations.

In his UN speech, Lula minced no words about how the U.S. threat is being perceived in Brazil. “In Latin America and the Caribbean, geographical proximity to the world’s greatest military power is inescapable… But Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard,” Lula declared to loud applause. The Brazilian did not meet Mr. Trump in New York; instead, he engaged with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, in what was seen as a political message to Mr. Trump.

Brazil goes to the polls on October 4 in a tense election. Lula leads Mr. Flávio by five points in the first-round polls. If they meet again in the second round on October 25, polls show a close race, adding to fears of U.S. interference influencing the result. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs , sanctions and by classifying PCC and CV as terrorist organisations.

Adding to the concerns is a confidential report sent recently by Brazil’s Intelligence Agency (Abin) to the President and TSE. The report raised the risk of U.S. interference to a “critical level”. The Abin assessment, reported widely by the Brazilian media, says the “reaffirmation of U.S. hegemony” in Latin America is a priority for Washington, particularly to counter China’s influence over strategic assets.

articles.title: China announces shock corruption probe into Politburo member
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining was earlier expected to assume a top leadership role in 2027

A prominent Chinese politician who is a member of the ruling Communist Party of China’s Politburo and was widely tipped for a top national leadership position in 2027 was placed under a shock disciplinary investigation on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The surprising announcement of “suspected severe violations” by Chen Jining, who has since 2022 been the top CPC leader in Shanghai and has served on the 25-member Politburo, left political observers in Beijing stunned.

Mr. Chen (62) was tipped to take on a prominent national role in the once-in-five-year Party Congress set for next year, which will see a major reshuffle. President Xi Jinping is expected to begin a fourth term in 2027.

Mr. Chen “is being investigated by the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision for suspected severe violations of discipline and laws,” a brief statement said.

Mr. Chen was previously the president of Mr. Xi’s alma mater, Tsinghua University, and served as the mayor of Beijing between 2018 and 2022, before his promotion to the Politburo as the Party Secretary of China’s financial centre, Shanghai.

In Shanghai, Mr. Chen was popular with foreign business representatives and is among the few leaders in the top echelons of the CPC with significant international exposure, having conducted his doctoral studies in environmental engineering at Imperial College London.

Politburo members are rarely investigated, and only half a dozen Politburo-level members in the last three decades have been removed. Notably, removals have often coincided with the run-up to Party Congresses that see leadership promotions and reshuffles.

Another former Shanghai Party Secretary, Chen Liangyu, was removed in 2006, a year before the 2007 Congress that saw the anointment of Mr. Xi as former leader Hu Jintao’s successor. The year of Mr. Xi’s ascension in 2012 saw the removal of Bo Xilai, then Party Secretary in Chongqing.

Under Mr. Xi, two Politburo-ranked members have been removed, including the former security chief Zhou Yongkang who retired from the Politburo Standing Committee, the party’s highest body, in 2012 and was placed under investigation in 2014. Another former Chongqing Party Secretary, Sun Zhengcai, was removed in 2017. Mr. Chen will likely be the third.

Mr. Chen was present at the CPC’s Fifth Plenum in Beijing last month, a key annual meeting that confirmed the expulsion of as many as 33 members of the party’s Central Committee, including 16 PLA Generals, and concluded with a pledge to “persevere with full and rigorous party self-governance”.

articles.title: Brazil, India are building strategic ties for a changing world, says Brazil’s Foreign Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: On whether BRICS seeks to replace the U.S. dollar, the Brazilian envoy says the possible use of local currencies for settling part of bilateral trade is something many countries already do, and that governments do not tell companies which currency they must use

In an interview with The Hindu in New Delhi, Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira praises India’s BRICS presidency, says bilateral trade could exceed the $30 billion target well before 2030 and argues that BRICS is not an anti-Western bloc.

articles.title: Maharashtra panel recommends ₹10 crore fine, life imprisonment for those guilty of exam paper leaks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Panel, headed by TISS director, calls for task force and special courts to deal with leak cases, the creation of a body to manage exam venues, third-party audits, cyber security measures, and monitoring devices

People involved in leaking recruitment examination papers should be punished with a fine of ₹10 crore and life imprisonment, according to the recommendations of a committee set up by the Maharashtra government, which submitted its report on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The panel, headed by the director of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, also proposed a framework to oversee the process of conducting tests, including a third party audit and a new body to manage exam venues.

This committee was set up in the wake of a paper leak in an examination to recruit pharmacists and drug inspectors for 954 posts, conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission on March 22. It was later discovered that the paper had already been leaked on WhatsApp, leading to the cancellation of the recruitment process on August 25, and an investigation into the matter. The State government set up the committee on September 4, after candidates sought a review of the exam process to recommend changes in the system.

Apart from a recommended penalty of a ₹10 crore fine and life imprisonment for individuals involved in paper leaks, the panel called for the establishment of a task force to address leak incidents, courts for the disposal of cases, and a body to manage exam venues, to bring accountability to district officials and prevent such leaks.

The panel proposes a third party audit, a cyber security cell, surveillance cameras, and signal-blocking devices at venues. Police personnel should be appointed to the Commission’s teams and non-governmental institutions need to be monitored to reduce irregularities in the selection of venues, the committee said. It also called for the publication of statistics regarding vacant posts and the development of a portal to resolve issues faced by candidates.

With regard to the pharmacist selection exam, the report recommends a fee refund by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission for all candidates who file income tax returns. The panel also suggested an increase in the number of posts for the Group-C exam, an extra attempt for candidates, an exam schedule to be announced by October, and a grievance portal to ensure transparency.

articles.title: KSEB revokes suspension of engineer over power disruption during Minister’s programme in Kannur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has revoked the suspension of Satheesh Babu P.V., a sub-engineer attached to the Kannur electrical section. He was suspended following a power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph at the Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21.

The suspension was withdrawn through an order issued by the executive engineer on Tuesday (November 24), following a review of the circumstances surrounding the incident and the report submitted by senior officials. Mr. Babu had been suspended pending inquiry after power supply was disrupted during the Minister’s programme on the morning of November 21.
The decision to reconsider the suspension followed a direction from the Deputy Chief Engineer, Electrical Circle, Kannur, on November 23.
In his report, the assistant executive engineer said that the official was unaware of the programme attended by the Minister and had intended to carry out routine maintenance work.
The suspension had triggered protests from KSEB employees’ organisations.

articles.title: Demand gets louder for restrictions on nightlife at Kozhikode beach
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kuttichira residents urge the district administration and the police to restrict activities at Kozhikode beach and in their neighbourhood from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

Nightlife at the Kozhikode beach and surrounding areas, one of the major tourist attractions in the city, is in the news, with residents seeking restrictions on people’s activities there in view of the reported involvement of anti-social elements.

District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty and District Police Chief (Kozhikode City) A.P. Shoukathali conducted a surprise inspection of the stretch from the South Beach to Konnad Beach on November 21. They were accompanied by officials from the departments of Port, Fisheries, and Health, and those from the district tourism promotion council and the Kozhikode Corporation. In view of a special branch report citing safety concerns, the officials examined complaints related to a lack of proper lighting in the area, broken tiles, disposal of waste, and the management of wastewater from the Food Street on the beach.

The special branch had reportedly said that restrictions could be imposed in places that lacked proper lighting and security arrangements. Though the stretch from the open stage to Mukhadar beach is relatively secure, areas such as Butt Road, Kothi beach, and Konnad beach are in a pitiable condition. The suggestion is to restrict the entry of people into these places around midnight and move them to secure areas. According to sources, a proposal was subsequently made to restrict nightlife from behind Freedom Square to Konnad beach.

Residents of the Kuttichira area, a heritage site, had earlier expressed their concerns related to the activities of anti-social elements. Thekkeppuram Jagratha Samithi, a collective of residents there, have submitted a memorandum to the District Collector and the District Police Chief seeking restrictions on the Kozhikode beach and Kuttichira between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. K. Moideen Koya, former councillor, and chairperson of the samithi, told The Hindu on Tuesday (November 24) that under Section 440 of the Municipalities Act, the local body’s secretary can issue direct orders to “stop any activity” or “remove any condition that disturbs residents’ rest, sleep, health, or safety”. “The police have promised to strengthen night patrolling in our area. We are planning to install CCTV cameras as well,” he said.

The Kozhikode Corporation, meanwhile, is reportedly toying with the idea of partial restrictions as its cleaning activities at night are getting affected because of the presence of people on the beach.

articles.title: Jagan calls for fair elections in Srikakulam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy spoke to District Collector, Superintendent of Police and other officials, asking them to ensure free and fair elections in the Srikakulam Municipal Corporation, where polling is scheduled to be held on November 26, 2026, said former minister Dharmana Prasada Rao.

Addressing the party’s final public meeting on Tuesday evening, Mr. Prasada said that Mr. Jagan was confident of the victory of YSRCP Mayor candidate Gunda Lakshmi Devi and the corporators in 60 divisions, provided officials discharge their duties impartially, and prevent malpractices and violence.

“YSRCP leaders and activists are ready to face any eventuality on the day of the elections given the large scale violence witnessed during nominations, scrutiny, polling and counting in urban and rural local body elections. The elections in Srikakulam which are being held after a long delay, needs to be conducted in accordance to the rules and regulations. Otherwise, if the YSRCP comes to power in the 2029 Assembly elections, it will take stern action against the officials,” said Mr. Prasada.
Senior party leaders Dharmana Krishnadas, Mandavilli Ravi, Konark Srinivas and others attended the public meeting held in Srikakulam.

articles.title: Guru Nanak’s message of equality, harmony resonates at Prakash Purab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thousands of Sikh devotees and people from other faiths gathered at Nampally Exhibition Grounds on Tuesday to celebrate the 557th Prakash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism, with prayers, devotional music and a community meal.

The congregation, held on the occasion of Guru Nanak’s birth anniversary, was jointly organised by the managing committees of Gurudwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, Ashok Bazar, and Gurudwara Saheb, Secunderabad. The programme began at 11 am and continued until 4.30 pm.
Devotees offered prayers before the Sri Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture of Sikhism, followed by Gurbani kirtan and katha (religious discourse).

Their renditions highlighted spiritual values and the importance of communal harmony.

articles.title: Centre to strengthen border surveillance, expand de-addiction centres from 300 to 2,000: Kishan Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Centre has drawn up an ambitious plan to tackle drug abuse by increasing the number of de-addiction centres across the country from 300 to 2,000, strengthening border surveillance, expanding de-addiction facilities and launching a massive awareness campaign aimed at the country’s youth, said Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

He said at a press conference in Hyderabad that special anti-drug units are being established within paramilitary forces, intelligence networks are being strengthened, and the use of sniffer dogs is being enhanced to curb drug trafficking.

An awareness programmes targetting 50 crore youth is being launched and one lakh ‘ Nasha Mukt Bharat Mitra ’ volunteers will be trained in the first phase. The Centre is working towards a drug-free India by 2029 through a “whole-of-government, whole-of-India and whole-of-society” approach under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, said the Minister.
Union Minister of Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy addressing a press conference in Hyderabad on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: SIDDHANT THAKUR

Stressing that the fight against drugs cannot be left to law enforcement agencies alone, he called for active participation from parents, teachers, media organisations and citizens. Mr. Kishan Reddy expressed concern over the growing impact of drugs on young people, warning that India’s future would be jeopardised if its youth were not protected from substance abuse.

Referring to Punjab, he said a state once known for its achievements in agriculture and industry had suffered severely because of the drug menace, and cautioned against the spread of similar problems to other parts of the country.

He alleged that drug trafficking networks backed by anti-India elements in neighbouring countries were using narcotics as a means to generate funds for unlawful activities. He also pointed to changing social conditions, including the decline of joint family systems, increasing isolation among youngsters and excessive dependence on mobile phones and social media, as factors contributing to vulnerability to drugs.

Emphasising a compassionate approach, the minister said young drug users should be treated as victims requiring support and rehabilitation rather than as criminals. He urged families, teachers and peers to help affected youth recover with dignity and rejoin mainstream society through continued education and employment opportunities.

Mr. Kishan Reddy also appealed to the Telangana government to preserve public lands for sports facilities and playgrounds, saying initiatives such as K helo India, F it India and yoga could help steer youngsters away from addiction.

articles.title: Kaliningrad: Why Russia’s Baltic exclave is a new flashpoint
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Moscow has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around the strategic exclave and has sent a formal diplomatic note to the NATO over what it sees as attempts to isolate the territory; however, NATO has rejected the accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’

On October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin issued a warning to the West. In a grand hall in Moscow, Mr. Putin sat before an audience of foreign policy experts at the Valdai Discussion Club. “If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation... then, of course, the question of the Russian Federation deploying all types of weapons at our country’s disposal will inevitably and immediately be on the agenda. This is inevitable.”

Mr. Putin continued to insist that Moscow had no plans to attack anyone — neither in 2029, not in 2030, not even in 2050. But if aggression came, he said, Russia would be compelled to respond. European citizens, he added, should understand this clearly. The warning did not appear out of nowhere. For months, NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) countries have been increasing military activities in the Baltic Sea and around Russia’s western borders.

Russia has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around Kaliningrad and has sent a formal diplomatic note to NATO over what Moscow sees as attempts to isolate the territory. NATO, however, has rejected those accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’.

“I can confirm that Russia sent a non-paper to NATO and that we have sent a response, noting that NATO is a defensive alliance and none of our activities or exercises pose a risk to any part of Russia,” said alliance spokesperson Allison Hart. “We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric,” she added.

articles.title: Estonia on the edge as Russia-NATO tensions rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The NATO member is overhauling its military strategy, moving troops closer to the border and investing in long-range arms as Russia is carrying out grey-zone tactics in NATO’s eastern flank; the country’s defence spending is set to rise by 42% in 2026, reaching €2.4 billion, or around 5.4% of its GDP; the U.K. has maintained some 1,200 troops in Estonia as part of NATO’s forward defence

On October 12, NATO’s top military commander issued a stark warning to Russia. General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said that if Moscow were “foolish enough” to attack an alliance territory, NATO would destroy “anything and everything” involved in the attack.
His remarks came at a time of rising tensions between Russia and European nations. And one country that finds itself under pressure on the hot Russia-NATO border is the tiny Estonia.

When the U.S., Canada, and 10 other European nations came together in 1949, in the early phase of the Cold War, to form the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), they had a clear goal. As Lord Hastings Lionel Ismay, the alliance’s first Secretary General, famously put it, the purpose was to “keep the Soviet Union out, the Americans in, and the Germans down.”

Throughout the Cold War, NATO had been the primary military bulwark against Soviet power in Europe. After the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991, Russia fell into a phase of strategic retreat, while NATO expanded towards Eastern Europe. This set the stage for renewed tensions once Russia started reasserting itself in the region.
The situation became even more complicated after Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

articles.title: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government

Three weeks after President Lula da Silva’s election victory, Brazilian institutions are tightening the screws on Big Tech over alleged interference in favour of his far-right rival Flávio Bolsonaro during the campaign. The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference from outside through digital platforms. We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula told his supporters after winning the election on October 25.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the Brazilian government stepped up efforts to pass a bill which would give the country’s competition regulator (CADE) more powers to monitor the Big Tech operations. Pending since September 2025, the bill is modelled on European Union regulations and it faces opposition from Bolsonaro allies.

Meanwhile, both Big Tech and the Bolsonaro camp are feeling the heat. In a landmark ruling on November 10, Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) fined Meta 7.5 million reais (US$1.5 million) for “failing to provide complete information” in a case alleging bias in the distribution of online content. The decision came after a civil society group filed a petition accusing Meta of restricting pro-Lula posts while allowing content favouring Flávio during the campaign. Meta has dismissed the allegations as “false and unfounded”, but internal documents of the company, exposed by Brazilian media, showed that Lula’s Instagram accounts had been restricted during the campaign.

In another decision that can have far-reaching consequences for Flavio and his Liberal Party (PL), a Brazilian Supreme Court judge has ordered the Federal Police (PF) to investigate possible foreign interference in the electoral process, with focus on hidden financing of campaigns. In his order, Justice Flávio Dino cited allegations that two Brazilian businessmen acted on behalf of the US-based Rockbridge Network to raise funds for Flávio’s campaign in the United States. “The prohibition on foreign financing under Brazilian law has a parallel in the US as well. For this reason, it is even more important that resources allegedly originating from that country should not be allowed to influence the Brazilian election,” the judge said in his order.

The Rockbridge Network is an American right-wing organisation co-founded in 2019 by US Vice-President JD Vance and businessman Chris Buskirk, with tech billionaire Peter Thiel bringing them together. Justice Dino has directed the police to investigate whether money and services were channelled to Flávio’s campaign. He also cited concerns over Meta’s handling of political content, including an October 22 report by the company’s Oversight Board highlighting gaps in safeguards for electoral integrity and concerns raised by United Nations observers on October 21.

Three weeks after President Lula da Silva’s election victory, Brazilian institutions are tightening the screws on Big Tech over alleged interference in favour of his far-right rival Flávio Bolsonaro during the campaign. The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference from outside through digital platforms. We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula told his supporters after winning the election on October 25.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the Brazilian government stepped up efforts to pass a bill which would give the country’s competition regulator (CADE) more powers to monitor the Big Tech operations. Pending since September 2025, the bill is modelled on European Union regulations and it faces opposition from Bolsonaro allies.

Meanwhile, both Big Tech and the Bolsonaro camp are feeling the heat. In a landmark ruling on November 10, Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) fined Meta 7.5 million reais (US$1.5 million) for “failing to provide complete information” in a case alleging bias in the distribution of online content. The decision came after a civil society group filed a petition accusing Meta of restricting pro-Lula posts while allowing content favouring Flávio during the campaign. Meta has dismissed the allegations as “false and unfounded”, but internal documents of the company, exposed by Brazilian media, showed that Lula’s Instagram accounts had been restricted during the campaign.

In another decision that can have far-reaching consequences for Flavio and his Liberal Party (PL), a Brazilian Supreme Court judge has ordered the Federal Police (PF) to investigate possible foreign interference in the electoral process, with focus on hidden financing of campaigns. In his order, Justice Flávio Dino cited allegations that two Brazilian businessmen acted on behalf of the US-based Rockbridge Network to raise funds for Flávio’s campaign in the United States. “The prohibition on foreign financing under Brazilian law has a parallel in the US as well. For this reason, it is even more important that resources allegedly originating from that country should not be allowed to influence the Brazilian election,” the judge said in his order.

The Rockbridge Network is an American right-wing organisation co-founded in 2019 by US Vice-President JD Vance and businessman Chris Buskirk, with tech billionaire Peter Thiel bringing them together. Justice Dino has directed the police to investigate whether money and services were channelled to Flávio’s campaign. He also cited concerns over Meta’s handling of political content, including an October 22 report by the company’s Oversight Board highlighting gaps in safeguards for electoral integrity and concerns raised by United Nations observers on October 21.

articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

With a smirk, Flávio Bolsonaro squinted at the camera and called President Lula da Silva “nine fingers” in the televised debate just two days before Brazil went to the polls for the presidential runoff. It was a cynical attempt to weaponise an old scar – and a gossip – against the Workers Party’s leader. Lula reacted sharply, reminding the audience how he had lost a finger on his left hand while working in a factory. “If there is anyone who lost a finger at the age of 17, it was me, working at night because I had to work,” Lula said, staring into the cameras. A red-faced Flavio didn’t know where to look. On October 25, Lula made history by becoming the first Brazilian president to finish second in the first round of an election, held on October 4, and go on to win the presidency in the run-off.

Ever since Lula entered politics more than three decades ago, his opponents have peddled the rumour that he deliberately chopped off his own finger to gain sympathy and claim compensation. But those familiar with his life know the struggles that shaped him. Born on October 27, 1945, in a dusty corner of Brazil, Lula grew up amid hunger and deprivation in the state of Pernambuco.

His family migrated to São Paulo in search of a better life, joining thousands who fled the region trapped in poverty and hopelessness. Raised by his mother, Dona Lindu, whose resilience left a lasting impression on him, Lula received only primary education before joining the workforce as a teenager. His mother passed away at 64 in 1980, while Lula was in prison during a workers’ strike. “I believe in a more just country because one day my mother taught me that, even in a simple home, no one can give up,” Lula said on Mother’s Day this year, fighting back tears as he remembered Dona Lindu.

Lula’s journey – from a parched corner of Brazil to the industrial belt of Sao Paulo – was brought to life in Lula, the Son of Brazil , a 2010 film directed by Fábio Barreto. Tracking his life, the film showed how Lula’s political training began on the factory floors of Sao Paulo’s industrial region known for its massive factories.

Amid the clutter of machines and the daily struggle with poverty, Lula rose from an apprentice to a metalworker and trade union leader and became the voice of workers who were not willing to accept low wages and political exclusion. “During the late 1970s, as Brazil’s military dictatorship sought to contain dissent, Lula emerged as one of the most prominent figures in the labour movement. His leadership brought him into direct confrontation with the regime and in 1980 he was arrested for his role in the strikes,” said Mr. Barreto.

articles.title: Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind deal on satellite systems
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites

Indian space companies GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) signed a multi-year contract in which Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building.

This made the deal the “largest business-to-business order” one Indian private space company has placed with another since the space sector opened to private players in 2020, a press release noted. While private companies have participated in India’s space sector since inception, it has usually been as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
The GalaxEye-Bellatrix deal was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA). The financial details of the contract were not disclosed.

GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR satellite constellation. OptoSAR is a proprietary imaging technology that allows customers to see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke, and darkness. Bellatrix builds the thrusters that steer and position satellites once they reach orbit, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions.

“OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration. Our thrusters have already fired in orbit on ISRO missions, and we have built the production lines to deliver that same performance at constellation scale,” Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, said in a statement. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles.

Mission Drishti, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, became the world’s first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. It validated GalaxEye’s spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm, the company stated.

In September, the Department of Science and Technology’s Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore from the Government of India’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for GalaxEye’s next multi-sensor satellite, which targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres. Sourcing propulsion from a partner in the same city gives GalaxEye closer engineering control and shorter lead times as it builds that satellite.
“Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close,” Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement.

ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said that private industry was now indispensable to India’s space ecosystem. “Today, we are extremely happy that 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. Whenever a launch vehicle lifts off or we place a satellite, 70-80% of the budget is pumped into the Indian industry. Without the support of Indian industry, we would not have reached the present level.”

Other officials, however, pointed out while India was putting in place a system to increase capacity, it had to work towards increasing demand for products from the private space ecosystem. “The first phase of India’s space reforms opened the sector and created an institutional framework for private participation. Now India has to work on generating heavy demand. I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created. The second is to have enough money coming into the sector, and number three, to have procedures at all levels. Space is not a sector that is going to give you a payback in six months or nine months. Perseverance is required, and the government must continue to have policy stability,” said Pawan Goenka, chairman, InSpace, India’s single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector.

articles.title: Iran rules out talks with U.S. until its seven conditions are met
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection

Iran reiterated Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that it would not hold talks with the United States to end the conflict, saying that seven conditions must be met first, though it didn't specify the conditions.
Iran also said three oil tankers had struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire despite U.S. aerial protection.
Meanwhile, at least nine Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes in Gaza, local officials said.

Iran's chief negotiator and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Tehran wouldn't negotiate with the U.S. "until Iran's seven conditions are met,” according to Iranian state television.

Iranian authorities haven't publicly stated what those conditions are. But Iranian state media have said they include the lifting of sanctions, the ending of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and the release of seized Iranian assets.
He also warned that Iran would “shift the geographical scope of the conflict should the enemy make a mistake.”
The naval arm of Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the three oil tankers struck the naval mines because they were “in violation of regulations” regarding passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Guard's navy said in a post on Telegram Monday (November 23, 2026) that the strait “is not a place to test unauthorised routes or to disregard maritime warnings.”
It said the tankers were “engulfed in flames” after hitting the mines despite being under U.S. aerial escort.

At least nine people were killed in four Israeli strikes Monday night (November 23, 2026) and Tuesday morning (November 24, 2026), officials in Gaza said. Among those killed was a senior security official in the Hamas-run government's Interior Ministry.

The ministry said Na'im Abu Nahl, director-general of its internal security service, was killed in a strike west of Gaza City on Tuesday (November 23, 2026). Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the killing and said Israel would continue targeting Hamas security forces.

Hospital officials across Gaza reported at least eight other deaths in four strikes, including a child killed in an airstrike in central Gaza on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) and three police officers killed in Khan Younis.

articles.title: Former members say EPG report was ‘highly positive’ for India-Nepal ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Their reaction comes a day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group “not relevant”

A day after Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri termed the report of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) “not relevant”, arguing that India will take a “forward looking” approach regarding boundary issues with Nepal, a former member of the EPG has said the report was “highly positive” for both India and Nepal and that it was “odd” that the group did not get a chance to present the report to the Government of India.

“The EPG report was produced after extensive research and field visits. We visited Visakhapatnam and other ports that are of interest to Nepal and spoke with many stakeholders before compiling the report and there are interesting recommendations in the report that could be of great use for India and Nepal and it was highly positive for Delhi-Kathmandu relations,” said Mahendra P. Lama, former professor of Jawaharlal Nehru University, who served as a member of the EPG.
ALSO WATCH India-Nepal ties: What does Modi-Balen partnership promise? | Above the Fold | Nov 23, 2026

The EPG returned to the spotlight on Monday (November 23, 2026) when Mr. Misri announced in a press conference held after the visit of Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah that New Delhi would adopt a “forward-looking” approach to the border issues. “The leaders have given a direction as part of the overall very forward-looking discussions that have been held today for the foreign secretaries to take the task forward. We will do so in a forward-looking manner, taking inspiration from the vision document and from the directions and indeed the spirit in which the discussions were held. I would say that EPG is in the past. We are not looking backward,” said Mr. Misri in response to a question. He described the EPG report as “not relevant”.

Former Nepali ambassador and coordinator of the EPG on the Nepali side, Bhek Bahadur Thapa, described the EPG report as a step forward for the bilateral consultation process. “It was not a unilateral document, it was a document created through bilateral consultation among experts appointed by New Delhi and Kathmandu,” said Mr. Thapa, who has also served as Foreign Minister of Nepal during 2004-05. The EPG report dealing with a broad spectrum of India-Nepal relations, including the Kalapani dispute and the 1950 India-Nepal Friendship Treaty was completed in 2018 but it remained under sealed covers. “It is odd that the report could not be launched here in Delhi. The Nepali side said the EPG report should be unveiled first by the Indian Prime Minister and on the same day we were supposed to return to Kathmandu for the report’s unveiling by the Nepali Prime Minister, “ said Prof. Lama, informing that they made a mistake as Kathmandu could have also unveiled the report first. “Our recommendations now can be accessed by other stakeholders in Kathmandu and I don’t think that is a positive thing,” said Mr. Lama.

The EPG was institutionalised according to an understanding that was reached during the delegation-level talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Nepali Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli in February 2016. The visit of Mr. Oli took place against the backdrop of months-long blockade on Nepal-India border that Kathmandu said was imposed by India but India blamed the Madhesi agitators of Nepal for imposing the blockade that hindered flow of essential items such as cooking gas into Nepal. During the time of its existence, a part of the Institute of Defence Studies and Analyses (IDSA) in Delhi served as the secretariat for the EPG. The then Director General of the IDSA Jayant Prasad was also part of the EPG.

Incidentally, officials who are currently playing key roles in India-Nepal relations were also involved in the EPG process. Former members recounted that the newly appointed Indian ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela was the Joint Secretary (North) in the Ministry of External Affairs and was part of the EPG process during 2016-18. That apart, the new Nepali ambassador to India Nischal Nath Pandey also was part of the EPG process in Kathmandu.

articles.title: A Russian strike on Ukraine kills two, wounds 48 as Kyiv explains its attack in Libya
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A Russian nighttime attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine has killed two civilians and wounded 48 others including four children

A Russian nighttime attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia killed two civilians and wounded 48 others, including four children, officials said Tuesday (November 24, 2026), as authorities in Ukraine and Libya debated the legitimacy of an unprecedented Ukrainian strike on a Russian warship docked in Benghazi.

The Zaporizhzhia glide bomb attack destroyed a private house and partially destroyed a five-story apartment building, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration. The youngest wounded child was less than a year old, he said, adding that the others were ages 4, 6 and 16.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that the Ukrainian military is sending reinforcements to the Zaporizhzhia region, which lies on the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine.

Russia and Ukraine have escalated their aerial strikes in recent months even as they engage in U.S.-mediated talks to end the war that began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago.

Mr. Zelenskyy noted in a speech that Ukraine needs 115 billion euros ($126 billion) in aid from foreign countries next year to keep up the fight. Funding of 90 billion euros ($98.7 billion) is already assured, he said, but Ukraine needs to find another 25 billion euros ($27.4 billion).

The United Nations says the war has killed close to 18,000 Ukrainian civilians and wounded more than 57,000 others since the all-out war broke out on Feb. 24, 2022. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers from both sides are believed to have died on the battlefield.
Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya

More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war, according to an estimate by independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona, which have been tracking Russian military losses for several years.

They said that they received a huge dataset earlier this month that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. They added projected deaths not yet recorded by Russian authorities.

Their analysis, released Monday (November 23, 2026), cross-checked the hacked government statistics against public records and other available data and offers a much larger number than previous estimates.
The Associated Press didn’t independently confirm the data or the analysis. Russia hasn’t released official figures on battlefield deaths for several years.

In January, a report by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank estimated that Russia had recorded up to 325,000 troop deaths between February 2022 and December 2025.
